--- headless structure ---
"""Unattended CLI runs: flags answer the per-run questions, and a run with no
terminal stops up front, naming what to set, instead of waiting on a prompt."""

import datetime

import pytest
import typer

from cli import prompts, run, selections
from cli.models import AnalystType, AssetType

UNATTENDED_ENV = {
    "TRADINGAGENTS_OUTPUT_LANGUAGE": "English",
    "TRADINGAGENTS_MAX_DEBATE_ROUNDS": "1",
    "TRADINGAGENTS_MAX_RISK_ROUNDS": "1",
    "TRADINGAGENTS_LLM_PROVIDER": "openai",
    "TRADINGAGENTS_QUICK_THINK_LLM": "gpt-6-luna",
}
FLAGS = {"ticker": "NVDA", "date": "2026-09-23", "analysts": "market,news", "save": True, "show": False}


@pytest.mark.unit
class TestFlagValues:
    def test_a_ticker_is_normalised_and_an_empty_one_refused(self):
        assert prompts.parse_ticker("0700.hk") == "0700.HK"
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="ticker"):
            prompts.parse_ticker("  ")
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="ticker"):
            prompts.parse_ticker("NV DA")

    def test_a_date_must_be_a_past_or_present_day(self):
        assert prompts.parse_analysis_date("2026-09-23") == "2026-09-23"
        tomorrow = (datetime.date.today() + datetime.timedelta(days=1)).isoformat()
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="future"):
            prompts.parse_analysis_date(tomorrow)
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="YYYY-MM-DD"):
            prompts.parse_analysis_date("23/09/2026")

    def test_analysts_are_named_and_checked_against_the_asset(self):
        assert prompts.parse_analysts(" Market, news ", AssetType.STOCK) == [AnalystType.MARKET, AnalystType.NEWS]
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="market, sentiment, news, fundamentals"):
            prompts.parse_analysts("market,macro", AssetType.STOCK)
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="crypto"):
            prompts.parse_analysts("fundamentals", AssetType.CRYPTO)
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="at least one"):
            prompts.parse_analysts(" , ", AssetType.STOCK)


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_flags_skip_exactly_their_own_steps(monkeypatch):
    for name, value in UNATTENDED_ENV.items():
        monkeypatch.setenv(name, value)

    def no_prompt(*a, **k):
        raise AssertionError("prompted although a flag answered the step")

    for step in ("get_ticker", "get_analysis_date", "select_analysts"):
        monkeypatch.setattr(selections, step, no_prompt)
    monkeypatch.setattr(selections.updates, "enabled", lambda: False)


```

{
  "filePath": "<workspace>/code/CS5351/TradingAgents-team-FR-A1/docs/architecture/adr/adr-fr-a1-risk-gate.md",
  "content": "# ADR-FR-A1: Deterministic Risk Gate\n\n- Status: Proposed (tests and design approved for authoring; production implementation\n  blocked pending review of the written tests)\n- Date: 2026-11-11\n- Owner: A\n- Requirement: FR-A1 (with INV-A1, NFR-A1, NFR-A2)\n- Baseline: team commit `46bde74`; upstream TradingAgents v0.7.1 (`9fa1196`)\n\nThis ADR records an architecture decision **before** production implementation, as\nrequired for a safety-critical change. It distinguishes newly generated work from\ninherited baseline functionality.\n\n## 1. Context\n\nThe TradingAgents baseline produces a final decision as Markdown:\n\n- `TraderProposal` (`tradingagents/agents/schemas.py:146`) carries `action`,\n  `reasoning`, `entry_price`, `stop_loss`, and free-text `position_sizing`.\n- `PortfolioDecision` (`tradingagents/agents/schemas.py:221`) carries a 5-tier\n  `rating`, `executive_summary`, `investment_thesis`, `price_target`, `time_horizon`.\n- Both are rendered to Markdown (`render_trader_proposal`, `render_pm_decision`)\n  and the Pydantic objects are **discarded**; only the strings\n  (`trader_investment_plan`, `final_trade_decision`) and `final_rating` reach state.\n- `PortfolioContext` (`tradingagents/portfolio.py:33`) has positions with only\n  `ticker`, `quantity`, `average_price`; no market value, no sector.\n- There is no deterministic final risk gate. `run_rating` passes model output\n  through unchanged (`tradingagents/agents/rating.py:106`).\n\nFR-A1 requires that before any trade decision is output, the system validates\n`TraderProposal` and `PortfolioDecision` against a versioned policy, returning\n`APPROVED` / `REJECTED` / `NEEDS_REVIEW` with rule IDs, and that decisions missing\na stop-loss or exceeding the single-name cap are never `APPROVED`.\n\n## 2. Scope\n\nIn scope (this ADR and the accompanying test plan):\n\n- FR-A1 core verdict, INV-A1 invariants, NFR-A1 (latency, no network), NFR-A2 (audit).\n\nOut of scope (not approved for implementation in this stage):\n\n- FR-A2 human approval queue. FR-A1 must *emit* `NEEDS_REVIEW` and block automatic\n  execution, but the approval workflow itself is pending separate scope confirmation.\n- FR-A3 advanced/configuration-driven policy thresholds.\n- Features owned by B (evidence), C (token budget), D (structured adapter\n  internals), E (eval harness, CI). FR-A1 depends on D's structured path but does\n  not modify it.\n\n## 3. Previous feasibility findings (verified against `46bde74`)\n\nAll prior read-only findings were re-verified in the current team repository. All\nhold. One additional finding, material to the design: **structured objects are\ndiscarded after rendering**, so a gate cannot rely on Markdown re-parsing.\n\n## 4. Architecture candidates\n\n### A. Guard inside the Portfolio Manager node\nEvaluate inside `portfolio_manager_node`. Rejected: couples deterministic policy to\nan LLM node, poor isolation for NFR-A1/A2, embeds approval logic in agent code.\n\n### B. Dedicated Risk Gate graph node\nInsert `Portfolio Manager → Risk Gate → END`. Pros: deterministic, isolable,\nfirst-class audit in state. Cons: requires retaining structured objects; changes\ngraph shape and checkpoint signature; and a *separate node* is not by itself a\nsafety guarantee.\n\n### C. Post-graph wrapper in `_run_graph` / `record_decision`\nCons: the CLI uses `stream_run` and calls `record_decision` itself\n(`cli/run.py:353`), so a wrapper misses the CLI path; verdict is not in streamed\nstate.\n\n### D. Pure engine + mandatory evaluation at the PM output boundary (selected)\nSplit into:\n\n- a **pure, injectable engine** (`tradingagents/risk_gate/`) with no LangGraph,\n  no network, no file I/O, no LLM, no dependency on a graph node; and\n- an **integration layer** that guarantees evaluation happens before any public\n  decision is emitted, at the Portfolio Manager output boundary.\n\nThe engine is the unit under test; the integration may be a graph node **and/or**\nan invocation inside the manager boundary, but correctness must not depend on\n\"having a separate node\". Publication is gated by the *enforcement point*, not by\ngraph topology.\n\n## 5. Decision\n\nAdopt **D**. Human review corrections (see §6) refine it as follows.\n\n### 5.1 Authority boundary (safety enforcement)\n\nA risk verdict must affect the *effective* recommendation at the public decision\nboundary:\n\n- The original model rating is preserved separately (`model_rating`).\n- A `REJECTED` or `NEEDS_REVIEW` recommendation must **not** propagate as an\n  actionable final recommendation. At the public boundary it is surfaced using the\n  existing `REVIEW` sentinel semantics (`tradingagents/agents/rating.py:30`).\n- No final recommendation may bypass risk evaluation. Both the programmatic API\n  (`TradingAgentsGraph.propagate` returning a signal) and the CLI stream path\n  (`cli/run.py`) must reflect the gate. Enforcement must be at a boundary that\n  cannot publish before evaluation; if a graph node cannot guarantee that, the\n  pure engine is invoked at the PM output boundary instead.\n\n### 5.2 Verdict and actionability (kept distinct)\n\n- `risk_verdict ∈ {APPROVED, REJECTED, NEEDS_REVIEW}`.\n- `decision_status ∈ {ACTIONABLE, BLOCKED, PENDING_REVIEW, NO_TRADE}`:\n  - `APPROVED` + actionable trade → `ACTIONABLE`\n  - `REJECTED` → `BLOCKED`\n  - `NEEDS_REVIEW` → `PENDING_REVIEW`\n  - `APPROVED` + `HOLD` → `NO_TRADE` (an approved HOLD is not ACTIONABLE)\n- Aggregation precedence: `REJECTED > NEEDS_REVIEW > APPROVED`. All applicable\n  rule results are collected (no first-fail short circuit).\n- Every evaluation produces a complete per-rule result set with rule identifiers,\n  including successful evaluations. `triggered_violation_ids` is kept separate from\n  `evaluated_rule_ids`.\n\n### 5.3 Inputs\n\n- Position sizing: use an explicit structured `target_position_weight` (projected\n  post-trade single-stock portfolio weight, fraction in [0, 1]). Preserve\n  `position_sizing` prose for compatibility. **Never infer approval from free\n  text.** Missing/ambiguous/invalid weight or supporting portfolio data →\n  `NEEDS_REVIEW`.\n- Never substitute average purchase price for current market value.\n- Sector concentration: a minimal structured **portfolio risk snapshot**\n  (portfolio value, holdings with market values and sectors, valuation date)\n  supplied explicitly by the caller or through an additive local portfolio input\n  contract. Projected sector exposure is computed deterministically. No network,\n  no invented values or sectors. Missing/inconsistent data prevents approval when\n  a rule requires it.\n\n### 5.4 Supported trade scope\n\n- Ordinary long BUY is the priority: stop-loss required; projected single-name\n  exposure ≤ 10%; projected sector exposure ≤ 30%; require stop < entry < target;\n  reward-to-risk ≥ 1.5; stock not blacklisted.\n- HOLD never creates an actionable trade (`NO_TRADE`).\n- SELL is treated as risk-reducing only when supported by explicit existing-position\n  and trade data. Unsupported short initiation or ambiguous direction →\n  `NEEDS_REVIEW`.\n- HOLD/SELL exemption applicability is flagged for team confirmation; proposed\n  tests are recorded separately rather than silently assumed.\n\n### 5.5 Policy and audit\n\n- Versioned policy, initially `fr-a1-v1`, stable `policy_hash`. Draft thresholds\n  10% / 30% / 1.5.\n- Deterministic, injectable blacklist policy; consistent ticker normalization\n  (`tradingagents/dataflows/symbols.py`).\n- Audit record includes per-rule outcomes, minimal structured input snapshot,\n  verdict, policy version and hash, UTC timestamp, evaluation latency. No\n  credentials, raw prompts, or unnecessary personal portfolio details.\n- Core engine has no network, no file I/O, no LLM. Audit persistence is an\n  integration-layer responsibility.\n\n## 6. Human review corrections incorporated\n\n1. Verdict must affect the effective recommendation; preserve model rating\n   separately; use `REVIEW` semantics at the boundary; verify API and CLI; no\n   bypass; a separate node is not itself the safety guarantee.\n2. Structured `target_position_weight`; no free-text approval; missing/ambiguous →\n   `NEEDS_REVIEW`.\n3. Minimal structured portfolio risk snapshot; deterministic projected sector\n   exposure; cash-funded long assumptions documented; no network/invention.\n4. Long-BUY scope; HOLD vs SELL handling; applicability documented; INV-A1 not\n   weakened; exemptions flagged.\n5. Verdict semantics and precedence; `NO_TRADE`; complete per-rule results;\n   separate violation vs evaluated IDs.\n6. Versioned policy and hash; injectable blacklist; audit fields; core purity;\n   persistence at integration layer.\n7. FR-A2/FR-A3 not approved; block `NEEDS_REVIEW` from automatic execution;\n   do not modify shared requirements registry; do not implement B/C/D/E.\n\n## 7. Consequences\n\nPositive:\n\n- Deterministic, offline-testable safety gate with first-class audit.\n- Clear separation of model rating from risk judgment and actionability.\n- Fail-closed on missing evidence; no silent weakening of INV-A1.\n\nNegative / costs:\n\n- Requires retaining structured objects in state (additive; source files must add\n  state keys and return the Pydantic objects alongside unchanged strings).\n- Requires a structured portfolio risk snapshot contract (additive input surface).\n- Bumping the graph layout marker in `_run_signature` invalidates older checkpoints\n  (they restart fresh) — intentional and safer.\n- Integration must cover both entry paths to avoid divergence.\n\nNeutral:\n\n- Rendered Markdown, memory log, and existing `final_rating`/`run_rating`\n  semantics remain the model rating; the gate adds adjacent fields.\n\n## 8. Reopening conditions\n\nReopen this ADR if any of the following are established by test evidence:\n\n- Deterministic projected sector exposure cannot be computed from available\n  structured data offline, and the team declines the additive portfolio snapshot.\n- The enforcement boundary proves unable to cover both API and CLI without a\n  network or LLM dependency.\n- Team confirmation changes HOLD/SELL applicability in a way that alters rule sets.\n- Any change would weaken INV-A1 or an approved requirement.\n\n## 9. Compliance\n\n- This is new implementation work; the inherited TradingAgents baseline is\n  explicitly not counted as the team's contribution beyond the integration points\n  documented above.\n- Architecture decision and verification evidence are recorded before production\n  implementation, per the course's safety-critical process.\n"
}

{
  "content": "# FR-A1 Test Plan — Deterministic Risk Gate\n\n- Status: Authoring approved; production implementation blocked pending review of these tests.\n- Date: 2026-11-11\n- Owner: A\n- Requirement: FR-A1, with INV-A1, NFR-A1, NFR-A2\n- Related ADR: `docs/architecture/adr/adr-fr-a1-risk-gate.md`\n- Baseline: `46bde74`\n\nThis plan describes the agreed contract and its offline test coverage. It is\nwritten before production implementation so the tests can be reviewed. Tests\nreference the requirement/invariant they enforce. Intentional safety-related\nbehavior changes are marked `[SAFETY]`; everything else must remain an existing\nbehavior (`[PRESERVE]`).\n\n## 1. Proposed interface (contract under review)\n\nThe tests are written against this interface. It is expected to match the\neventual implementation; production code is not written yet.\n\n### 1.1 Package `tradingagents.risk_gate`\n\nModules (proposed): `models.py`, `policy.py`, `engine.py`, `sizing.py`,\n`portfolio_snapshot.py`, `node.py` (integration). The core engine modules have no\nnetwork, no file I/O, no LLM imports.\n\n### 1.2 Enumerations\n\n```python\nclass RiskVerdict(StrEnum):\n    APPROVED = \"APPROVED\"\n    REJECTED = \"REJECTED\"\n    NEEDS_REVIEW = \"NEEDS_REVIEW\"\n\nclass DecisionStatus(StrEnum):\n    ACTIONABLE = \"ACTIONABLE\"\n    BLOCKED = \"BLOCKED\"\n    PENDING_REVIEW = \"PENDING_REVIEW\"\n    NO_TRADE = \"NO_TRADE\"\n\nclass RuleOutcome(StrEnum):\n    PASS = \"PASS\"\n    VIOLATED = \"VIOLATED\"\n    NOT_APPLICABLE = \"NOT_APPLICABLE\"\n    UNKNOWN = \"UNKNOWN\"\n```\n\n### 1.3 Rule identifiers\n\n| ID | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `R1_STOP_LOSS_REQUIRED` | Long actionable BUY must carry a stop-loss |\n| `R2_SINGLE_NAME_CAP` | Projected single-name weight ≤ 10% (0.10) |\n| `R3_SECTOR_CONCENTRATION` | Projected sector exposure ≤ 30% (0.30) |\n| `R4_REWARD_RISK` | Direction-aware reward-to-risk ≥ 1.5 and ordering stop<entry<target |\n| `R5_BLACKLIST` | Ticker not on the deterministic blacklist |\n| `R6_INPUT_INTEGRITY` | Structured inputs present, consistent, unambiguous |\n| `R0_ALL_RULES_PASSED` | Positive marker so every verdict carries a rule ID |\n\n`R0` is a synthetic \"pass\" entry: every evaluation carries at least one rule ID,\nsatisfying \"100% of verdicts carry a rule identifier\" (`requirements.yaml:28`),\nincluding clean approvals.\n\n### 1.4 Input models\n\n```python\nclass TargetPosition(BaseModel):\n    target_position_weight: float | None   # projected post-trade single-name weight, 0..1\n\nclass Holding(BaseModel):\n    ticker: str\n    market_value: float          # current market value; never average cost\n    sector: str | None\n\nclass PortfolioRiskSnapshot(BaseModel):\n    valuation_date: str          # ISO date; must match the run's trade_date when required\n    portfolio_value: float       # total portfolio value used for weight denominators\n    holdings: list[Holding]\n    cash: float | None = None\n\nclass RiskInputs(BaseModel):\n    ticker: str\n    trade_date: str\n    action: str | None           # TraderProposal.action, if structured output produced it\n    entry_price: float | None\n    stop_loss: float | None\n    price_target: float | None   # PortfolioDecision.price_target\n    model_rating: str | None     # PortfolioDecision.rating, verbatim\n    target_position: TargetPosition | None\n    portfolio: PortfolioRiskSnapshot | None\n```\n\n### 1.5 Output models\n\n```python\nclass RuleResult(BaseModel):\n    rule_id: str\n    outcome: RuleOutcome\n    detail: str                      # deterministic; no PII/credentials\n    observed: float | None = None\n    threshold: float | None = None\n\nclass RiskEvaluation(BaseModel):\n    verdict: RiskVerdict\n    decision_status: DecisionStatus\n    model_rating: str | None\n    evaluated_rule_ids: list[str]        # every rule considered\n    triggered_violation_ids: list[str]   # only VIOLATED rule ids\n    rule_results: list[RuleResult]       # complete per-rule results\n    policy_version: str\n    policy_hash: str\n    input_snapshot: dict                 # minimal, redacted snapshot\n    evaluated_at_utc: str                # ISO8601 UTC\n    latency_ms: float\n\nclass RiskAuditRecord(BaseModel):\n    audit_id: str\n    evaluation: RiskEvaluation\n```\n\n### 1.6 Engine entry points\n\n```python\ndef evaluate_risk(inputs: RiskInputs, policy: RiskPolicy | None = None) -> RiskEvaluation: ...\n\nclass RiskPolicy:\n    version: str          # \"fr-a1-v1\"\n    policy_hash: str      # stable hash of the constants\n    single_name_cap: float = 0.10\n    sector_cap: float = 0.30\n    min_reward_risk: float = 1.5\n    blacklist: frozenset[str] = frozenset()\n```\n\n`evaluate_risk` is pure and deterministic. Ticker normalization uses\n`tradingagents.dataflows.symbols.normalize_symbol`.\n\n## 2. Rule semantics and applicability\n\nPrecedence for the final verdict: `REJECTED > NEEDS_REVIEW > APPROVED`.\n\n| Rule | Applies when | Violated → | Unknown/inapplicable → |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| R1 stop-loss | long actionable BUY (action Buy) | REJECTED | — |\n| R2 single-name | BUY with a resolvable weight | REJECTED (>0.10) | NEEDS_REVIEW (missing weight) |\n| R3 sector | BUY with a resolvable snapshot | REJECTED (>0.30) | NEEDS_REVIEW (unknown sector/value) |\n| R4 reward-risk | BUY with entry/stop/target | REJECTED (ratio<1.5 or bad ordering) | NEEDS_REVIEW (missing leg) |\n| R5 blacklist | any ticker | REJECTED (on list) | — (list always known) |\n| R6 input integrity | always | — | NEEDS_REVIEW (missing/contradictory) |\n\nBUY: all of R1–R5 apply. HOLD: no actionable trade; approved HOLD → `NO_TRADE`.\nR4 not applicable to HOLD (proposed; flagged for team confirmation §7). SELL:\nrisk-reducing only with explicit existing position + trade data; otherwise\n`NEEDS_REVIEW` (proposed; flagged §7).\n\n## 3. Requirement traceability\n\n| Requirement | Contract element | Test file |\n|---|---|---|\n| FR-A1 verdict + rule IDs | `evaluate_risk`, `rule_results` | `test_rules.py`, `test_verdict_semantics.py` |\n| FR-A1 5 injected violations 5/5 blocked | R1–R5 fixtures | `test_rule_violations.py` |\n| FR-A1 100 invalid fixtures 0 approvals | fixture generator | `test_100_invalid_fixtures.py` |\n| INV-A1 no approval without stop / over cap | invariants | `test_invariants.py` |\n| NFR-A1 p95 ≤ 2 s, 0 network | pure engine + import guard | `test_latency_no_network.py` |\n| NFR-A2 audit completeness | `RiskAuditRecord` | `test_audit_trail.py` |\n| §5.1 verdict affects recommendation | boundary enforcement | `test_decision_boundary.py` |\n| §5.2 NO_TRADE for approved HOLD | `DecisionStatus` | `test_verdict_semantics.py` |\n| §5.3 structured weight/snapshot | `TargetPosition`, `PortfolioRiskSnapshot` | `test_input_contract.py` |\n| §5.4 trade scope | applicability | `test_trade_scope.py` |\n| §5.5 policy version/hash | `RiskPolicy` | `test_policy_versioning.py` |\n| Structured retention (API+CLI) | state keys | `test_integration_retention.py` |\n\n## 4. Test matrix\n\nAll tests are `@pytest.mark.unit`, offline (the repo's `conftest.py` already\nblocks sockets), parameterized deterministically. Files live under `tests/risk_gate/`.\n\n### 4.1 Rule-level (`test_rules.py`)\n\n- R1: BUY missing stop → REJECTED, id `R1_STOP_LOSS_REQUIRED`.\n- R2: weight 0.12 → REJECTED; weight 0.10 → PASS; weight 0.099 → PASS.\n- R3: sector 0.35 → REJECTED; 0.30 → PASS.\n- R4: long RR 2.0 → PASS; RR 0.5 → REJECTED; short direction-aware.\n- R5: blacklisted ticker → REJECTED; normalization for `aapl`/`AAPL`.\n- Valid BUY (all in bounds) → APPROVED, `R0_ALL_RULES_PASSED` present.\n- Wrong-side stop (long stop ≥ entry) → REJECTED; wrong-side target → REJECTED.\n\n### 4.2 Exact boundaries (`test_boundaries.py`)\n\n- 10% weight: `0.10` PASS, next representable above → REJECTED.\n- 30% sector: `0.30` PASS.\n- 1.5 RR: exactly `1.5` PASS; `1.4999...` REJECTED.\n\n### 4.3 Injected violations (`test_rule_violations.py`)\n\nFive individually isolated fixtures, each expected rule ID + verdict, and the\nother rules passing: missing stop, single-name 12%, sector 35%, RR 1.0,\nblacklist.\n\n### 4.4 Malformed / missing inputs (`test_input_contract.py`)\n\n- Missing structured object → NEEDS_REVIEW (R6).\n- Missing weight → NEEDS_REVIEW (R2 unknown).\n- Missing portfolio/sector → NEEDS_REVIEW (R3 unknown).\n- NaN/invalid floats → NEEDS_REVIEW (never APPROVED).\n- Contradictory proposal/decision direction → NEEDS_REVIEW.\n\n### 4.5 Verdict semantics (`test_verdict_semantics.py`)\n\n- Precedence REJECTED > NEEDS_REVIEW > APPROVED.\n- All applicable rules collected (no first-fail).\n- `triggered_violation_ids` ⊆ `evaluated_rule_ids`; both present for clean runs.\n- Approved HOLD → `NO_TRADE`; approved BUY → `ACTIONABLE`; rejected → `BLOCKED`;\n  needs-review → `PENDING_REVIEW`.\n\n### 4.6 Trade scope (`test_trade_scope.py`)\n\n- HOLD never ACTIONABLE.\n- SELL without explicit position/trade data → NEEDS_REVIEW.\n- SELL with explicit data → evaluated as risk-reducing (proposed behavior).\n- Unsupported short initiation / ambiguous direction → NEEDS_REVIEW.\n\n### 4.7 Invariants (`test_invariants.py`)\n\n- APPROVED ⇒ stop-loss present for actionable BUY.\n- APPROVED ⇒ weight ≤ 0.10.\n- APPROVED ⇒ decision_status in {ACTIONABLE, NO_TRADE}.\n- Sweep over deterministic grid: no APPROVED violates INV-A1.\n\n### 4.8 100 invalid fixtures (`test_100_invalid_fixtures.py`)\n\nDeterministically generated in code (no 100 redundant JSON files): cartesian\nproduct over rule-violating and malformed shapes, truncated/selected to exactly\n100. Assert **0 of 100 APPROVED**, each has ≥1 rule ID.\n\n### 4.9 Audit (`test_audit_trail.py`)\n\n- Every evaluation has a complete audit record (rule ids/outcomes, snapshot,\n  verdict, policy version+hash, UTC timestamp, latency).\n- 10 evaluations → 100% audit coverage; no credentials/raw prompt fields.\n\n### 4.10 Policy versioning (`test_policy_versioning.py`)\n\n- `version == \"fr-a1-v1\"`; `policy_hash` stable; distinct hash when a threshold\n  changes; version present in evaluation.\n\n### 4.11 Latency / no network (`test_latency_no_network.py`)\n\n- 1000 evaluations; p95 additive latency ≤ 2000 ms.\n- Core `tradingagents.risk_gate` modules import no network modules; evaluation\n  raises under socket monkeypatch (already enforced by conftest).\n\n### 4.12 Integration acceptance (`test_integration_retention.py`, `test_decision_boundary.py`)\n\n`[SAFETY]`/`[PRESERVE]` marked. These exercise the graph and CLI; many are expected\nto fail before implementation and are reported honestly.\n\n- Structured objects retained in state without Markdown parsing (`[SAFETY]`).\n- Programmatic API: rejected BUY does not escape as actionable; public signal is\n  `REVIEW`/blocked (`[SAFETY]`).\n- CLI stream path: same enforcement (`[SAFETY]`).\n- Audit persistence via integration layer (`[SAFETY]`).\n- Checkpoint safety: layout marker invalidates pre-gate checkpoints (`[SAFETY]`).\n- Existing rendered strings and `run_rating` unchanged (`[PRESERVE]`).\n\n## 5. Expected outcomes before implementation\n\nBecause production code is absent, the risk-gate tests will fail at import\n(`ModuleNotFoundError: tradingagents.risk_gate`). Collection of the test files\nsucceeds; execution failures are *expected* and reported honestly, never counted as\npasses. Existing tests must remain unaffected (`[PRESERVE]`).\n\n## 6. Intentional safety changes vs regression\n\n- `[SAFETY]` items intentionally change observable behavior at the decision\n  boundary (non-APPROVED directions become `REVIEW`/blocked). These are not\n  regressions.\n- `[PRESERVE]` items must remain identical; failing ones indicate unintended\n  regression and must not be \"fixed\" by weakening assertions.\n\n## 7. Pending scope decisions (proposed tests recorded separately)\n\nThese are written as `test_proposed_*` and marked `xfail(strict=False)` or\ndocumented, so their assumptions are visible and not silently treated as approved:\n\n- P1 HOLD applicability of R4 (proposed: not applicable).\n- P2 SELL risk-reducing criteria and required explicit data.\n- P3 Blacklist source (injectable policy vs. config); proposed injectable.\n- P4 FR-A2 boundary: NEEDS_REVIEW blocked from automatic execution.\n- P5 Sector snapshot additive contract details.\n",

{
  "content": "\"\"\"Verdict semantics: precedence, completeness, and actionability (FR-A1, §5.2).\n\nThe model rating, the risk verdict, and the deliverable status are independent.\nAggregation precedence is REJECTED > NEEDS_REVIEW > APPROVED, all applicable\nrules are collected, and an approved HOLD is NO_TRADE, never ACTIONABLE.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport pytest\n\npytest.importorskip(\n    \"tradingagents.risk_gate\",\n    reason=\"tradingagents.risk_gate not implemented yet (pre-implementation)\",\n)\n\nfrom tests.risk_gate._support import (  # noqa: E402\n    R0,\n    R1,\n    R2,\n    R4,\n    evaluate,\n    make_buy,\n    violated_ids,\n)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_approved_buy_is_actionable():\n    \"\"\"FR-A1 §5.2: APPROVED + trade -> ACTIONABLE.\"\"\"\n    result = evaluate(make_buy())\n    assert result.verdict == \"APPROVED\"\n    assert result.decision_status == \"ACTIONABLE\"\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_rejected_is_blocked():\n    \"\"\"FR-A1 §5.2: REJECTED -> BLOCKED.\"\"\"\n    result = evaluate(make_buy(stop_loss=None))\n    assert result.verdict == \"REJECTED\"\n    assert result.decision_status == \"BLOCKED\"\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_needs_review_is_pending_review():\n    \"\"\"FR-A1 §5.2: NEEDS_REVIEW -> PENDING_REVIEW.\"\"\"\n    result = evaluate(make_buy(price_target=None))\n    assert result.verdict == \"NEEDS_REVIEW\"\n    assert result.decision_status == \"PENDING_REVIEW\"\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_precedence_rejected_over_needs_review():\n    \"\"\"FR-A1 §5.2: REJECTED dominates NEEDS_REVIEW when both apply.\"\"\"\n    # missing weight (needs review) AND missing stop (reject)\n    result = evaluate(make_buy(stop_loss=None, target_position=None))\n    assert result.verdict == \"REJECTED\"\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_all_applicable_rules_are_collected():\n    \"\"\"FR-A1 §5.2: no first-fail short circuit; all violated rules reported.\"\"\"\n    result = evaluate(make_buy(stop_loss=105.0, price_target=95.0))\n    # stop above entry and target below entry both break ordering (R4); the\n    # engine must still report every rule it evaluated.\n    assert R4 in violated_ids(result)\n    assert result.evaluated_rule_ids\n    assert set(result.triggered_violation_ids) <= set(result.evaluated_rule_ids)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_clean_run_carries_rule_ids():\n    \"\"\"FR-A1: 100% of verdicts carry rule IDs, including successes (R0).\"\"\"\n    result = evaluate(make_buy())\n    assert result.rule_results\n    assert R0 in {r.rule_id for r in result.rule_results}\n    assert result.evaluated_rule_ids\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_model_rating_preserved_on_reject():\n    \"\"\"FR-A1 §5.1: the model's rating is preserved even when the gate rejects.\"\"\"\n    result = evaluate(make_buy(model_rating=\"Buy\", stop_loss=None))\n    assert result.verdict == \"REJECTED\"\n    assert result.model_rating == \"Buy\"\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_approved_hold_is_no_trade():\n    \"\"\"FR-A1 §5.2: an approved HOLD is NO_TRADE, not ACTIONABLE.\"\"\"\n    data = make_buy(action=\"Hold\", model_rating=\"Hold\",\n                    entry_price=None, stop_loss=None, price_target=None,\n                    target_position=None, portfolio=None)\n    result = evaluate(data)\n    if result.verdict == \"APPROVED\":\n        assert result.decision_status == \"NO_TRADE\"\n    else:\n        # If the engine treats a HOLD with missing inputs as NEEDS_REVIEW that is\n        # acceptable; what must never happen is ACTIONABLE.\n        assert result.decision_status != \"ACTIONABLE\"\n",
  "filePath": "<workspace>/code/CS5351/TradingAgents-team-FR-A1/tests/risk_gate/test_verdict_semantics.py"
}

{
  "content": "\"\"\"INV-A1 invariants and boundary enforcement of the risk gate (FR-A1).\n\nBulk deterministic sweep: no APPROVED verdict may lack a stop-loss for an\nactionable BUY, exceed the single-name cap, or claim ACTIONABLE while blocked.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport itertools\n\nimport pytest\n\npytest.importorskip(\n    \"tradingagents.risk_gate\",\n    reason=\"tradingagents.risk_gate not implemented yet (pre-implementation)\",\n)\n\nfrom tests.risk_gate._support import evaluate, make_buy  # noqa: E402\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_invariant_no_approval_without_stop_loss():\n    \"\"\"INV-A1: an actionable BUY is never APPROVED without a stop-loss.\"\"\"\n    for stop in (None, 90.0, 101.0):\n        result = evaluate(make_buy(stop_loss=stop))\n        if result.verdict == \"APPROVED\":\n            assert result.decision_status != \"ACTIONABLE\" or stop is not None\n            assert stop is not None\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_invariant_no_approval_over_single_name_cap():\n    \"\"\"INV-A1: an APPROVED decision never exceeds the 10% single-name cap.\"\"\"\n    for weight in (0.0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.11, 0.25):\n        result = evaluate(make_buy(target_position={\"target_position_weight\": weight}))\n        if result.verdict == \"APPROVED\":\n            assert weight <= 0.10\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_invariant_approved_implies_actionable_or_no_trade():\n    \"\"\"FR-A1 §5.2: APPROVED maps only to ACTIONABLE or NO_TRADE.\"\"\"\n    result = evaluate(make_buy())\n    if result.verdict == \"APPROVED\":\n        assert result.decision_status in (\"ACTIONABLE\", \"NO_TRADE\")\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_invariant_sweep_never_approves_violations():\n    \"\"\"INV-A1: sweep over violations; zero approvals of any violating case.\"\"\"\n    stops = [None, 105.0, 90.0]\n    targets = [95.0, 105.0, 130.0]\n    weights = [0.05, 0.12]\n    approved = 0\n    for stop, target, weight in itertools.product(stops, targets, weights):\n        result = evaluate(\n            make_buy(stop_loss=stop, price_target=target,\n                     target_position={\"target_position_weight\": weight})\n        )\n        violates = (\n            stop is None\n            or target <= 100.0 and target <= stop  # placeholder ordering clarity\n            or weight > 0.10\n            or (stop is not None and stop >= 100.0)\n        )\n        if result.verdict == \"APPROVED\":\n            approved += 1\n            assert not (stop is None or weight > 0.10), (stop, target, weight)\n    assert approved >= 0\n",

  "content": "\"\"\"NFR-A2: audit trail completeness for every evaluation.\n\nEvery evaluation must be auditable with rule IDs and outcomes, a minimal input\nsnapshot, the verdict, policy version and hash, a UTC timestamp, and latency. No\ncredentials or raw prompts are stored.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport pytest\n\npytest.importorskip(\n    \"tradingagents.risk_gate\",\n    reason=\"tradingagents.risk_gate not implemented yet (pre-implementation)\",\n)\n\nfrom tests.risk_gate._support import evaluate, make_buy  # noqa: E402\n\n_FORBIDDEN_SUBSTRINGS = (\"api_key\", \"apikey\", \"secret\", \"password\", \"bearer\", \"authorization\")\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_every_evaluation_has_a_complete_audit_record():\n    \"\"\"NFR-A2: verdict, rule ids, snapshot, policy version+hash, timestamp, latency.\"\"\"\n    result = evaluate(make_buy())\n    assert result.policy_version == \"fr-a1-v1\"\n    assert result.policy_hash\n    assert result.evaluated_at_utc\n    assert result.evaluated_at_utc.endswith(\"Z\") or \"+\" in result.evaluated_at_utc\n    assert isinstance(result.latency_ms, float) and result.latency_ms >= 0.0\n    assert result.input_snapshot is not None\n    assert result.rule_results\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_audit_rule_results_have_ids_and_outcomes():\n    \"\"\"NFR-A2: each rule result carries a rule id and an outcome.\"\"\"\n    result = evaluate(make_buy(stop_loss=None))\n    assert result.rule_results\n    for rr in result.rule_results:\n        assert rr.rule_id\n        assert str(rr.outcome)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_ten_evaluations_all_audited():\n    \"\"\"NFR-A2: 100% audit coverage across repeated evaluations.\"\"\"\n    for _ in range(10):\n        result = evaluate(make_buy())\n        assert result.input_snapshot is not None\n        assert result.policy_version\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_audit_snapshot_has_no_credentials_or_prompts():\n    \"\"\"NFR-A2/NFR-SEC: the input snapshot holds no credentials or raw prompts.\"\"\"\n    result = evaluate(make_buy())\n    blob = repr(result.input_snapshot).lower()\n    for needle in _FORBIDDEN_SUBSTRINGS:\n        assert needle not in blob\n    for key in result.input_snapshot:\n        assert \"prompt\" not in str(key).lower()\n",

{
  "content": "\"\"\"Policy versioning and injectable blacklist (FR-A1 §5.5).\n\nThe policy is versioned (initially ``fr-a1-v1``) with a stable hash that changes\nwhen a threshold changes. The blacklist is deterministic and injectable, and\nticker matching is normalization-consistent.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport pytest\n\npytest.importorskip(\n    \"tradingagents.risk_gate\",\n    reason=\"tradingagents.risk_gate not implemented yet (pre-implementation)\",\n)\n\nfrom tests.risk_gate._support import R5, evaluate, make_buy, violated_ids  # noqa: E402\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_default_policy_version_and_hash():\n    \"\"\"FR-A1 §5.5: default policy is fr-a1-v1 with a non-empty stable hash.\"\"\"\n    rg = __import__(\"tradingagents.risk_gate\", fromlist=[\"RiskPolicy\"])\n    p1 = rg.RiskPolicy()\n    p2 = rg.RiskPolicy()\n    assert p1.version == \"fr-a1-v1\"\n    assert p1.policy_hash\n    assert p1.policy_hash == p2.policy_hash\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_hash_changes_when_a_threshold_changes():\n    \"\"\"FR-A1 §5.5: changing a threshold changes the policy hash.\"\"\"\n    rg = __import__(\"tradingagents.risk_gate\", fromlist=[\"RiskPolicy\"])\n    base = rg.RiskPolicy()\n    changed = rg.RiskPolicy(single_name_cap=0.20)\n    assert base.policy_hash != changed.policy_hash\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_policy_version_reaches_evaluation():\n    \"\"\"FR-A1 §5.5: the evaluation records the policy version and hash.\"\"\"\n    result = evaluate(make_buy())\n    assert result.policy_version == \"fr-a1-v1\"\n    assert result.policy_hash\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"ticker\", [\"AAPL\", \"aapl\", \" Aapl \"])\ndef test_blacklist_matches_after_normalization(ticker):\n    \"\"\"FR-A1 §5.5: blacklist matching is normalization-consistent.\"\"\"\n    rg = __import__(\"tradingagents.risk_gate\", fromlist=[\"RiskPolicy\"])\n    result = evaluate(make_buy(ticker=ticker), policy=rg.RiskPolicy(blacklist=frozenset({\"AAPL\"})))\n    assert result.verdict == \"REJECTED\"\n    assert R5 in violated_ids(result)\n",
  "filePath": "<workspace>/code/CS5351/TradingAgents-team-FR-A1/tests/risk_gate/test_policy_versioning.py"
}

The repository's\nconftest already refuses sockets; here we also assert the engine's module set\ndoes not pull in a network client.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport importlib\nimport sys\nimport time\n\nimport pytest\n\npytest.importorskip(\n    \"tradingagents.risk_gate\",\n    reason=\"tradingagents.risk_gate not implemented yet (pre-implementation)\",\n)\n\nfrom tests.risk_gate._support import evaluate, make_buy  # noqa: E402\n\n_NETWORK_MODULES = (\n    \"requests\",\n    \"urllib3\",\n    \"httpx\",\n    \"curl_cffi\",\n    \"yfinance\",\n    \"langchain_core\",\n    \"langchain_openai\",\n)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_p95_latency_within_two_seconds():\n    \"\"\"NFR-A1: p95 incremental latency ≤ 2000 ms over 1000 evaluations.\"\"\"\n    samples = []\n    for _ in range(1000):\n        start = time.perf_counter()\n        evaluate(make_buy())\n        samples.append((time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000.0)\n    samples.sort()\n    p95 = samples[int(0.95 * (len(samples) - 1))]\n    assert p95 <= 2000.0, f\"p95={p95:.3f}ms exceeds 2000ms\"\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_evaluation_completes_with_no_socket():\n    \"\"\"NFR-A1: evaluation succeeds under the suite's socket refusal.\"\"\"\n    # The autouse socket guard from tests/conftest.py is already active here.\n    result = evaluate(make_buy())\n    assert result.verdict in (\"APPROVED\", \"REJECTED\", \"NEEDS_REVIEW\")\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_engine_module_does_not_depend_on_network_or_llm():\n    \"\"\"NFR-A1: the core engine imports no network or LLM client modules.\"\"\"\n    engine = importlib.import_module(\"tradingagents.risk_gate\")\n    # Modules imported by the engine itself, excluding the test process baseline.\n    source_file = getattr(engine, \"__file__\", \"\") or \"\"\n    assert \"risk_gate\" in source_file\n    for banned in _NETWORK_MODULES:\n        mod = sys.modules.get(banned)\n        # Presence in sys.modules is allowed if another test imported it; the product yields a large\n# deterministic space from which we take exactly 100 cases.\n_STOPS = [None, 100.0, 105.0]                       # missing / equal / wrong-side\n_TARGETS = [None, 95.0, 100.0, 103.0]               # missing / wrong-side / low RR\n_WEIGHTS = [None, 0.12, 0.25, 1.5]                  # unknown / over cap / absurd\n_PORTFOLIOS = [\n    None,                                           # no snapshot\n    {\"valuation_date\": \"2026-01-09\", \"portfolio_value\": 1_000_000.0, \"cash\": 0.0,\n     \"holdings\": [{\"ticker\": \"AAPL\", \"market_value\": 50_000.0, \"sector\": None}]},\n    {\"valuation_date\": \"2026-01-09\", \"portfolio_value\": 1_000_000.0, \"cash\": 0.0,\n     \"holdings\": [{\"ticker\": \"AAPL\", \"market_value\": 50_000.0, \"sector\": \"Technology\"},\n                  {\"ticker\": \"MSFT\", \"market_value\": 400_000.0, \"sector\": \"Technology\"}]},\n]\n\n\ndef _all_cases():\n    cases = []\n    for stop, target, weight, portfolio in itertools.product(\n        _STOPS, _TARGETS, _WEIGHTS, _PORTFOLIOS\n    ):\n        target_position = None if weight is None else {\"target_position_weight\": weight}\n        cases.append(\n            {\n                \"stop_loss\": stop,\n                \"price_target\": target,\n                \"target_position\": target_position,\n                \"portfolio\": portfolio,\n            }\n        )\n    return cases[:100]\n\n\nCASES = _all_cases()\nassert len(CASES) == 100\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"case\", CASES, ids=[f\"invalid_{i:03d}\" for i in range(len(CASES))])\ndef test_invalid_fixture_is_never_approved(case):\n    \"\"\"FR-A1/INV-A1: no invalid fixture is APPROVED; # FR-A1 — Tests & Design Authoring Complete

All approved artifacts are created. No production source, shared CI/governance files, or requirements registry were modified. No dependencies installed, no external APIs, no commits.

## 1. Files created

**Design documentation**
- `docs/architecture/adr/adr-fr-a1-risk-gate.md` — candidates, evaluation, selected design (pure engine + boundary enforcement), human corrections, authority boundary, consequences, reopening conditions, compliance.
- `docs/req/fr-a1-test-plan.md` — proposed interface, rule semantics/applicability, requirement traceability, test matrix, expected outcomes, pending decisions.

**Test suite** (`tests/risk_gate/`)
- `__init__.py`, `conftest.py` (skip-with-reason pre-implementation fixture), `_support.py` (builders + rule IDs)
- `test_rules.py`, `test_boundaries.py`, `test_rule_violations.py`, `test_input_contract.py`, `test_reward_risk_direction.py`, `test_verdict_semantics.py`, `test_trade_scope.py`, `test_invariants.py`, `test_audit_trail.py`, `test_policy_versioning.py`, `test_latency_no_network.py`, `test_projected_exposure.py`, `test_100_invalid_fixtures.py`
- `test_decision_boundary.py`, `test_integration_retention.py` (integration acceptance)

## 2. Final proposed interface

- Enums: `RiskVerdict{APPROVED,REJECTED,NEEDS_REVIEW}`, `DecisionStatus{ACTIONABLE,BLOCKED,PENDING_REVIEW,NO_TRADE}`, `RuleOutcome{PASS,VIOLATED,NOT_APPLICABLE,UNKNOWN}`.
- Rules: `R1_STOP_LOSS_REQUIRED`, `R2_SINGLE_NAME_CAP`, `R3_SECTOR_CONCENTRATION`, `R4_REWARD_RISK`, `R5_BLACKLIST`, `R6_INPUT_INTEGRITY`, positive marker `R0_ALL_RULES_PASSED`.
- Inputs: `RiskInputs` with structured `TargetPosition.target_position_weight` and `PortfolioRiskSnapshot` (valuation_date, portfolio_value, holdings with market_value+sector, cash).
- Outputs: `RuleResult`, `RiskEvaluation` (verdict, decision_status, model_rating, evaluated_rule_ids, triggered_violation_ids, complete rule_results, policy_version/hash, redacted snapshot, UTC timestamp, latency), `RiskAuditRecord`.
- Engine: `evaluate_risk(inputs, policy=None) -> RiskEvaluation`; `RiskPolicy(version="fr-a1-v1", policy_hash, caps 0.10/0.30/1.5, blacklist)`.
- Precedence: `REJECTED > NEEDS_REVIEW > APPROVED`; approved HOLD ⇒ `NO_TRADE`.

- Current MSFT market value: 150,000
- Both holdings in Technology

projected_stock_value = target_weight * portfolio_value

projected_sector_value =
    current_sector_value
    - current_stock_value
    + projected_stock_value

Use correct fixtures for:

triggered_violation_ids contains only VIOLATED rules.

Context\n \n The TradingAgents baseline produces a final decision as Markdown:\n \n - `TraderProposal` (`tradingagents/agents/schemas.py:146`) carries `action`,\n   `reasoning`, `entry_price`, `stop_loss`, and free-text `position_sizing`.\n - `PortfolioDecision` (`tradingagents/agents/schemas.py:221`) carries a 5-tier\n   `rating`, `executive_summary`, `investment_thesis`, `price_target`, `time_horizon`.\n - Both are rendered to Markdown (`render_trader_proposal`, `render_pm_decision`)\n   and the Pydantic objects are **discarded**; only the strings\n   (`trader_investment_plan`, `final_trade_decision`) and `final_rating` reach state.\n - `PortfolioContext` (`tradingagents/portfolio.py:33`) has positions with only\n   `ticker`, `quantity`, `average_price`; no market value, no sector.\n - There is no deterministic final risk gate. `run_rating` passes model output\n   through unchanged (`tradingagents/agents/rating.py:106`).\n \n FR-A1 requires that before any trade decision is output, the system validates\n `TraderProposal` and `PortfolioDecision` against a versioned policy, returning\n `APPROVED` / `REJECTED` / `NEEDS_REVIEW` with rule IDs, and that decisions missing\n a stop-loss or exceeding the single-name cap are never `APPROVED`.\n \n ## 2. Scope\n \n In scope (this ADR and the accompanying test plan):\n \n - FR-A1 core verdict, INV-A1 invariants, NFR-A1 (latency, no network), NFR-A2 (audit).\n \n Out of scope (not approved for implementation in this stage):\n \n - FR-A2 human approval queue. FR-A1 must *emit* `NEEDS_REVIEW` and block automatic\n   execution, but the approval workflow itself is pending separate scope confirmation.\n - FR-A3 advanced/configuration-driven policy thresholds.\n - Features owned by B (evidence), C (token budget), D (structured adapter\n   internals), E (eval harness, CI). FR-A1 depends on D's structured path but does\n   not modify it.\n \n ## 3. Previous feasibility findings (verified against `46bde74`)\n \n All prior read-only findings were re-verified in the current team repository. All\n hold. One additional finding, material to the design: **structured objects are\n discarded after rendering**, so a gate cannot rely on Markdown re-parsing.\n \n ## 4. Architecture candidates\n \n ### A. Guard inside the Portfolio Manager node\n Evaluate inside `portfolio_manager_node`. Rejected: couples deterministic policy to\n an LLM node, poor isolation for NFR-A1/A2, embeds approval logic in agent code.\n \n ### B. Dedicated Risk Gate graph node\n Insert `Portfolio Manager → Risk Gate → END`. Pros: deterministic, isolable,\n first-class audit in state. Cons: requires retaining structured objects; changes\n graph shape and checkpoint signature; and a *separate node* is not by itself a\n safety guarantee.\n \n ### C. Post-graph wrapper in `_run_graph` / `record_decision`\n Cons: the CLI uses `stream_run` and calls `record_decision` itself\n (`cli/run.py:353`), so a wrapper misses the CLI path; verdict is not in streamed\n state.\n \n ### D. Pure engine + mandatory evaluation at the PM output boundary (selected)\n Split into:\n \n - a **pure, injectable engine** (`tradingagents/risk_gate/`) with no LangGraph,\n   no network, no file I/O, no LLM, no dependency on a graph node; and\n - an **integration layer** that guarantees evaluation happens before any public\n   decision is emitted, at the Portfolio Manager output boundary.\n \n The engine is the unit under test; the integration may be a graph node **and/or**\n an invocation inside the manager boundary, but correctness must not depend on\n \"having a separate node\". Publication is gated by the *enforcement point*, not by\n graph topology.\n \n ## 5. Decision\n \n Adopt **D**. Human review corrections (see §6) refine it as follows.\n \n ### 5.1 Authority boundary (safety enforcement)\n \n A risk verdict must affect the *effective* recommendation at the public decision\n boundary:\n \n - The original model rating is preserved separately (`model_rating`).\n - A `REJECTED` or `NEEDS_REVIEW` recommendation must **not** propagate as an\n   actionable final recommendation. At the public boundary it is surfaced using the\n   existing `REVIEW` sentinel semantics (`tradingagents/agents/rating.py:30`).\n - No final recommendation may bypass risk evaluation. Both the programmatic API\n   (`TradingAgentsGraph.propagate` returning a signal) and the CLI stream path\n   (`cli/run.py`) must reflect the gate. Enforcement must be at a boundary that\n   cannot publish before evaluation; if a graph node cannot guarantee that, the\n   pure engine is invoked at the PM output boundary instead.\n \n ### 5.2 Verdict and actionability (kept distinct)\n \n - `risk_verdict ∈ {APPROVED, REJECTED, NEEDS_REVIEW}`.\n - `decision_status ∈ {ACTIONABLE, BLOCKED, PENDING_REVIEW, NO_TRADE}`:\n   - `APPROVED` + actionable trade → `ACTIONABLE`\n   - `REJECTED` → `BLOCKED`\n   - `NEEDS_REVIEW` → `PENDING_REVIEW`\n   - `APPROVED` + `HOLD` → `NO_TRADE` (an approved HOLD is not ACTIONABLE)\n - Aggregation precedence: `REJECTED > NEEDS_REVIEW > APPROVED`. All applicable\n   rule results are collected (no first-fail short circuit).\n - Every evaluation produces a complete per-rule result set with rule identifiers,\n-  including successful evaluations. `triggered_violation_ids` is kept separate from\n-  `evaluated_rule_ids`.\n+  including successful evaluations. Rule outcomes are `PASS`, `VIOLATED`,\n+  `NOT_APPLICABLE`, or `UNKNOWN`. `UNKNOWN` (insufficient input to decide) is **not**\n+  the same as `VIOLATED` (a rule was broken): `triggered_violation_ids` contains\n+  only `VIOLATED` rule ids, while `evaluated_rule_ids` lists every rule considered.\n+  (For a missing stop-loss, `R1` is `VIOLATED` while `R4` may be `UNKNOWN`.)\n \n+### 5.2a Three separate concepts at the boundary\n+\n+The system keeps three values distinct and never collapses them:\n+\n+1. `model_rating` — the Portfolio Manager's own rating, preserved verbatim\n+   (`Buy`/`Overweight`/`Hold`/`Underweight`/`Sell`/`REVIEW`).\n+2. `risk_verdict` — `APPROVED` / `REJECTED` / `NEEDS_REVIEW`, from the gate only.\n+3. **effective public signal** — what the rest of the system may act on. Intentional safety changes vs regression\n \n - `[SAFETY]` items intentionally change observable behavior at the decision\n   boundary (non-APPROVED directions become `REVIEW`/blocked). These are not\n   regressions.\n - `[PRESERVE]` items must remain identical; failing ones indicate unintended\n   regression and must not be \"fixed\" by weakening assertions.\n \n-## 7. Pending scope decisions (proposed tests recorded separately)\n+## 7.         "patch": "Index: tests/risk_gate/test_100_invalid_fixtures.py\n===================================================================\n--- tests/risk_gate/test_100_invalid_fixtures.py\t\n+++ tests/risk_gate/test_100_invalid_fixtures.py\t\n@@ -1,72 +1,181 @@\n \"\"\"100 deterministic invalid fixtures with zero approvals (FR-A1, INV-A1).\n \n-Fixtures are generated in code from the cartesian product of rule violations and\n-malformed shapes, so there is no proliferation of redundant JSON files. Exactly\n-100 cases are exercised; none may be APPROVED, and each must carry a rule ID.\n+Cases are generated in code (no redundant JSON files) from meaningful,\n+reproducible variations that exercise all five risk rules plus input-integrity\n+failures and the blacklist. Exactly 100 cases are exercised; none may be\n+APPROVED, and each must record at least one non-PASS rule outcome (VIOLATED or\n+UNKNOWN). Each case carries the requirement/rule it targets for readability.\n \"\"\"\n \n from __future__ import annotations\n \n import itertools\n \n import pytest\n \n-pytest.importorskip(\n-    \"tradingagents.risk_gate\",\n-    reason=\"tradingagents.risk_gate not implemented yet (pre-implementation)\",\n+from tests.risk_gate._support import (\n+    evaluate,\n+    make_buy,\n+    make_portfolio,\n+    make_target,\n+    outcomes,\n )\n \n-from tests.risk_gate._support import evaluate, make_buy  # noqa: E402\n+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n+# Reusable inconsistent-but-valid-shape books\n+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n \n-# Each axis contributes one class of invalid input; the product yields a large\n-# deterministic space from which we take exactly 100 cases.\n-_STOPS = [None, 100.0, 105.0]                       # missing / equal / wrong-side\n-_TARGETS = [None, 95.0, 100.0, 103.0]               # missing / wrong-side / low RR\n-_WEIGHTS = [None, 0.12, 0.25, 1.5]                  # unknown / over cap / absurd\n-_PORTFOLIOS = [\n-    None,                                           # no snapshot\n-    {\"valuation_date\": \"2026-01-09\", \"portfolio_value\": 1_000_000.0, \"cash\": 0.0,\n-     \"holdings\": [{\"ticker\": \"AAPL\", \"market_value\": 50_000.0, \"sector\": None}]},\n-    {\"valuation_date\": \"2026-01-09\", \"portfolio_value\": 1_000_000.0, \"cash\": 0.0,\n-     \"holdings\": [{\"ticker\": \"AAPL\", \"market_value\": 50_000.0, \"sector\": \"Technology\"},\n-                  {\"ticker\": \"MSFT\", \"market_value\": 400_000.0, \"sector\": \"Technology\"}]},\n+\n+def _tech_book(msft, aapl, cash):\n+    return make_portfolio(\n+        holdings=[\n+            {\"ticker\": \"AAPL\", \"market_value\": aapl, \"sector\": \"Technology\"},\n+            {\"ticker\": \"MSFT\", \"market_value\": msft, \"sector\": \"Technology\"},\n+        ],\n+        cash=cash,\n+        portfolio_value=aapl + msft + cash,\n+    )\n+\n+\n+# R1: missing stop. R4 becomes UNKNOWN (ratio unprovable) -> not a violation.\n+_R1_CASES = [(\"R1\", {\"stop_loss\": None})]\n+\n+# R2: single-name over cap (weight > 0.10), all else valid.\n+_R2_CASES = [(\"R2\", {\"target_position\": make_target(w)})\n+             for w in (0.1001, 0.11, 0.15, 0.25, 0.50)]\n+\n+# R3: projected sector over 30%. Build a book where buying AAPL (weight 0.05 of\n+# a 1,000,000 book = 50,000) pushes Technology above 30%.\n+_R3_CASES = []\n+for tech_before in (250_000.0, 260_000.0, 280_000.0, 300_000.0):\n+    # projected Technology = tech_before + 50,000 (AAPL unheld)\n+    msft = tech_before\n+    cash = 60_000.0\n+    fin = 1_000_000.0 - (msft + cash)\n+    if tech_before + 50_000.0 > 300_000.0:\n+        _R3_CASES.append((\"R3\", {\"portfolio\": make_portfolio(\n+            holdings=[\n+                {\"ticker\": \"AAPL\", \"market_value\": 0.0, \"sector\": \"Technology\"},\n+                {\"ticker\": \"MSFT\", \"market_value\": msft, \"sector\": \"Technology\"},\n+                {\"ticker\": \"JPM\", \"market_value\": fin, \"sector\": \"Financials\"},\n+            ],\n+            cash=cash, portfolio_value=1_000_000.0)}))\n+\n+# R4: reward-to-risk below 1.5 and wrong-side stops/targets.\n+_R4_CASES = []\n+for stop, target in [\n+    (90.0, 105.0),    # RR 0.5\n+    (90.0, 114.0),    # RR 1.4\n+    (100.0, 130.0),   # stop == entry\n+    (105.0, 130.0),   # stop above entry\n+    (90.0, 100.0),    # target == entry\n+    (90.0, 95.0),     # target below entry\n+]:\n+    _R4_CASES.append((\"R4\", {\"stop_loss\": stop, \"price_target\": target}))\n+\n+# Input integrity: missing/ambiguous/contradictory inputs (UNKNOWN outcomes).\n+_R6_CASES = [\n+    (\"R6\", {\"price_target\": None}),          # R4 unknown\n+    (\"R6\", {\"target_position\": None}),        # R2 unknown\n+    (\"R6\", {\"portfolio\": None}),              # R3 unknown\n+    (\"R6\", {\"action\": \"Buy\", \"model_rating\": \"Sell\"}),  # contradictory\n+    (\"R6\", {\"entry_price\": float(\"nan\")}),    # non-finite\n+    (\"R6\", {\"entry_price\": float(\"inf\")}),    # non-finite\n ]\n+# Unknown sector prevents the sector rule from being decided.\n+_R6_CASES.append((\"R6\", {\"portfolio\": make_portfolio(\n+    holdings=[{\"ticker\": \"AAPL\", \"market_value\": 20_000.0, \"sector\": None},\n+              {\"ticker\": \"MSFT\", \"market_value\": 150_000.0, \"sector\": \"Technology\"}],\n+    cash=830_000.0, portfolio_value=1_000_000.0)}))\n+# Inconsistent book: holdings + cash != portfolio_value.\n+_R6_CASES.append((\"R6\", {\"portfolio\": make_portfolio(\n+    holdings=[{\"ticker\": \"AAPL\", \"market_value\": 20_000.0, \"sector\": \"Technology\"},\n+              {\"ticker\": \"MSFT\", \"market_value\": 150_000.0, \"sector\": \"Technology\"}],\n+    cash=10_000.0, portfolio_value=1_000_000.0)}))\n+# Stale valuation date.\n+_R6_CASES.append((\"R6\", {\"portfolio\": make_portfolio(\n+    holdings=[{\"ticker\": \"AAPL\", \"market_value\": 20_000.0, \"sector\": \"Technology\"},\n+              {\"ticker\": \"MSFT\", \"market_value\": 150_000.0, \"sector\": \"Technology\"}],\n+    cash=830_000.0, portfolio_value=1_000_000.0, valuation_date=\"2020-01-01\")}))\n \n+# R5: blacklist. These need a policy argument, so they are handled separately.\n+_R5_TICKERS = [\"AAPL\", \"MSFT\", \"TSLA\"]\n \n-def _all_cases():\n+\n+def _base_cases():\n     cases = []\n-    for stop, target, weight, portfolio in itertools.product(\n-        _STOPS, _TARGETS, _WEIGHTS, _PORTFOLIOS\n-    ):\n-        target_position = None if weight is None else {\"target_position_weight\": weight}\n-        cases.append(\n-            {\n-                \"stop_loss\": stop,\n-                \"price_target\": target,\n-                \"target_position\": target_position,\n-                \"portfolio\": portfolio,\n-            }\n-        )\n-    return cases[:100]\n+    cases += _R1_CASES\n+    cases += _R2_CASES\n+    cases += _R3_CASES\n+    cases += _R4_CASES\n+    cases += _R6_CASES\n+    return cases\n \n \n-CASES = _all_cases()\n+def _expand_to_100(base):\n+    \"\"\"Deterministically expand the targeted cases to exactly 100.\n+\n+    Cross-products of violations are meaningful invalid cases. The expansion is a\n+    fixed ordered product (no randomness), so every run reproduces the same 100\n+    cases. Single-rule cases come first for readability.\n+    \"\"\"\n+    cases = list(base)\n+\n+    # Two-dimension crosses first, then a three-way cross if still short.\n+    for (rule_a, a), (rule_b, b) in itertools.product(_R2_CASES, _R4_CASES):\n+        cases.append((f\"{rule_a}+{rule_b}\", {**a, **b}))\n+    for (rule_a, a), (rule_b, b) in itertools.product(_R4_CASES, _R3_CASES):\n+        cases.append((f\"{rule_a}+{rule_b}\", {**a, **b}))\n+\n+    if len(cases) < 100:\n+        for (r1, a), (r2, b), (r3, c) in itertools.product(_R2_CASES, _R4_CASES, _R6_CASES):\n+            cases.append((f\"{r1}+{r2}+{r3}\", {**a, **b, **c}))\n+\n+    # Deduplicate by serialized payload while preserving order, then take 100.\n+    seen, unique = set(), []\n+    for rule, case in cases:\n+        key = repr(sorted(case.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[0]))\n+        if key not in seen:\n+            seen.add(key)\n+            unique.append((rule, case))\n+    assert len(unique) >= 100, f\"only {len(unique)} unique invalid cases generated\"\n+    return unique[:100]\n+\n+\n+CASES = _expand_to_100(_base_cases())\n assert len(CASES) == 100\n \n \n @pytest.mark.unit\n-@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"case\", CASES, ids=[f\"invalid_{i:03d}\" for i in range(len(CASES))])\n-def test_invalid_fixture_is_never_approved(case):\n-    \"\"\"FR-A1/INV-A1: no invalid fixture is APPROVED; each carries rule IDs.\"\"\"\n+@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n+    \"target_rule, case\",\n+    CASES,\n+    ids=[f\"{rule}_{i:03d}\" for i, (rule, _case) in enumerate(CASES)],\n+)\n+def test_invalid_fixture_is_never_approved(target_rule, case):\n+    \"\"\"FR-A1/INV-A1: no invalid fixture is APPROVED; a rule is VIOLATED or UNKNOWN.\"\"\"\n     result = evaluate(make_buy(**case))\n-    assert result.verdict != \"APPROVED\", case\n-    assert result.triggered_violation_ids, case\n+    assert result.verdict != \"APPROVED\", (target_rule, case)\n+    assert result.decision_status != \"ACTIONABLE\", (target_rule, case)\n+    non_pass = {rid for rid, out in outcomes(result).items() if out in (\"VIOLATED\", \"UNKNOWN\")}\n+    assert non_pass, (target_rule, case)\n     assert set(result.triggered_violation_ids) <= set(result.evaluated_rule_ids)\n \n \n @pytest.mark.unit\n def test_zero_approvals_across_all_invalid_fixtures():\n-    \"\"\"FR-A1: aggregate check — 0 of 100 invalid fixtures approved.\"\"\"\n-    approvals = [i for i, case in enumerate(CASES)\n+    \"\"\"FR-A1: aggregate — 0 of 100 invalid fixtures approved.\"\"\"\n+    approvals = [i for i, (_rule, case) in enumerate(CASES)\n                  if evaluate(make_buy(**case)).verdict == \"APPROVED\"]\n     assert approvals == [], f\"invalid fixtures approved: {approvals}\"\n+\n+\n+@pytest.mark.unit\n+@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"ticker\", _R5_TICKERS)\n+def test_blacklisted_fixtures_are_never_approved(ticker):\n+    \"\"\"FR-A1 R5: a blacklisted ticker among the fixtures is never approved.\"\"\"\n+    rg = __import__(\"tradingagents.risk_gate\", fromlist=[\"RiskPolicy\"])\n+    policy = rg.RiskPolicy(blacklist=frozenset({ticker}))\n+    result = evaluate(make_buy(ticker=ticker), policy=policy)\n+    assert result.verdict == \"REJECTED\"\n+    assert result.decision_status == \"BLOCKED\"\n",

        "deletions": 44,

cap is inclusive\n-        (0.3000001, False),\n-        (0.31, False),\n+        (250_000.0, True),    # 25%\n+        (299_999.0, True),    # just below\n+        (300_000.0, True),    # exactly 30% (inclusive)\n+        (300_001.0, False),   #         "patch": "Index: tests/risk_gate/test_invariants.py\n===================================================================\n--- tests/risk_gate/test_invariants.py\t\n+++ tests/risk_gate/test_invariants.py\t\n@@ -1,69 +1,64 @@\n \"\"\"INV-A1 invariants and boundary enforcement of the risk gate (FR-A1).\n \n Bulk deterministic sweep: no APPROVED verdict may lack a stop-loss for an\n actionable BUY, exceed the single-name cap, or claim ACTIONABLE while blocked.\n \"\"\"\n \n from __future__ import annotations\n \n import itertools\n \n import pytest\n \n-pytest.importorskip(\n-    \"tradingagents.risk_gate\",\n-    reason=\"tradingagents.risk_gate not implemented yet (pre-implementation)\",\n-)\n+from tests.risk_gate._support import evaluate, make_buy, make_target\n \n-from tests.risk_gate._support import evaluate, make_buy  # noqa: E402\n \n-\n @pytest.mark.unit\n def test_invariant_no_approval_without_stop_loss():\n     \"\"\"INV-A1: an actionable BUY is never APPROVED without a stop-loss.\"\"\"\n     for stop in (None, 90.0, 101.0):\n         result = evaluate(make_buy(stop_loss=stop))\n-        if result.verdict == \"APPROVED\":\n-            assert result.decision_status != \"ACTIONABLE\" or stop is not None\n+        if result.verdict == \"APPROVED\" and result.decision_status == \"ACTIONABLE\":\n             assert stop is not None\n+    # The concrete violation case must not be approved at all.\n+    assert evaluate(make_buy(stop_loss=None)).verdict != \"APPROVED\"\n \n \n @pytest.mark.unit\n def test_invariant_no_approval_over_single_name_cap():\n     \"\"\"INV-A1: an APPROVED decision never exceeds the 10% single-name cap.\"\"\"\n     for weight in (0.0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.11, 0.25):\n-        result = evaluate(make_buy(target_position={\"target_position_weight\": weight}))\n+        result = evaluate(make_buy(target_position=make_target(weight)))\n         if result.verdict == \"APPROVED\":\n             assert weight <= 0.10\n \n \n @pytest.mark.unit\n def test_invariant_approved_implies_actionable_or_no_trade():\n     \"\"\"FR-A1 §5.2: APPROVED maps only to ACTIONABLE or NO_TRADE.\"\"\"\n     result = evaluate(make_buy())\n     if result.verdict == \"APPROVED\":\n         assert result.decision_status in (\"ACTIONABLE\", \"NO_TRADE\")\n \n \n @pytest.mark.unit\n def test_invariant_sweep_never_approves_violations():\n-    \"\"\"INV-A1: sweep over violations; zero approvals of any violating case.\"\"\"\n+    \"\"\"INV-A1: sweep over invalid cases; zero approvals of any violating case.\"\"\"\n     stops = [None, 105.0, 90.0]\n     targets = [95.0, 105.0, 130.0]\n     weights = [0.05, 0.12]\n \n     def violates(stop, target, weight):\n-        #         "file": "tests/risk_gate/test_latency_no_network.py",
        "patch": "Index: tests/risk_gate/test_latency_no_network.py\n===================================================================\n--- tests/risk_gate/test_latency_no_network.py\t\n+++ tests/risk_gate/test_latency_no_network.py\t\n@@ -1,70 +1,92 @@\n-\"\"\"NFR-A1: pure engine latency and zero network / LLM dependency.\n+\"\"\"NFR-A1: core engine latency and zero network / LLM dependency.\n \n-The core risk engine must add no perceptible latency (p95 ≤ 2 s incremental) and\n-must not import or call network, file-I/O, or LLM modules. The repository's\n-conftest already refuses sockets; here we also assert the engine's module set\n-does not pull in a network client.\n+The pure risk engine must add no perceptible latency (p95 ≤ 2 s) and must not\n+depend on network, file I/O, or an LLM. The runtime socket guard from the\n+repository conftest is already active; this module additionally installs its own\n+guard for the duration of the latency loop and performs a structural check that\n+the engine package does not import network/LLM client modules.\n+\n+The measured p95 is printed in the assertion message so the number is reported,\n+and the core evaluation latency is distinguished from any integration overhead.\n \"\"\"\n \n from __future__ import annotations\n \n-import importlib\n+import socket\n+import subprocess\n import sys\n+import textwrap\n import time\n \n import pytest\n \n-pytest.importorskip(\n-    \"tradingagents.risk_gate\",\n-    reason=\"tradingagents.risk_gate not implemented yet (pre-implementation)\",\n-)\n+from tests.risk_gate._support import evaluate, make_buy\n \n-from tests.risk_gate._support import evaluate, make_buy  # noqa: E402\n \n-_NETWORK_MODULES = (\n-    \"requests\",\n-    \"urllib3\",\n-    \"httpx\",\n-    \"curl_cffi\",\n-    \"yfinance\",\n-    \"langchain_core\",\n-    \"langchain_openai\",\n-)\n-\n-\n @pytest.mark.unit\n-def test_p95_latency_within_two_seconds():\n-    \"\"\"NFR-A1: p95 incremental latency ≤ 2000 ms over 1000 evaluations.\"\"\"\n+def test_p95_core_evaluation_latency_within_two_seconds(capsys):\n+    \"\"\"NFR-A1: core-evaluation p95 ≤ 2000 ms over 1000 evaluations (measured).\"\"\"\n     samples = []\n     for _ in range(1000):\n         start = time.perf_counter()\n         evaluate(make_buy())\n         samples.append((time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000.0)\n     samples.sort()\n     p95 = samples[int(0.95 * (len(samples) - 1))]\n-    assert p95 <= 2000.0, f\"p95={p95:.3f}ms exceeds 2000ms\"\n+    p50 = samples[len(samples) // 2]\n+    print(f\"\\ncore evaluation latency: p50={p50:.4f}ms p95={p95:.4f}ms n={len(samples)}\")\n+    assert p95 <= 2000.0, f\"core p95={p95:.4f}ms exceeds 2000ms\"\n \n \n @pytest.mark.unit\n-def test_evaluation_completes_with_no_socket():\n-    \"\"\"NFR-A1: evaluation succeeds under the suite's socket refusal.\"\"\"\n-    # The autouse socket guard from tests/conftest.py is already active here.\n+def test_evaluation_runs_under_a_runtime_socket_guard(monkeypatch):\n+    \"\"\"NFR-A1: evaluation completes while every socket call refuses to connect.\"\"\"\n+    def refuse(*a, **k):\n+        raise AssertionError(\"risk gate attempted a network call\")\n+\n+    monkeypatch.setattr(socket.socket, \"connect\", refuse)\n+    monkeypatch.setattr(socket.socket, \"connect_ex\", refuse)\n+    monkeypatch.setattr(socket, \"getaddrinfo\", refuse)\n     result = evaluate(make_buy())\n     assert result.verdict in (\"APPROVED\", \"REJECTED\", \"NEEDS_REVIEW\")\n \n \n @pytest.mark.unit\n-def test_engine_module_does_not_depend_on_network_or_llm():\n-    \"\"\"NFR-A1: the core engine imports no network or LLM client modules.\"\"\"\n-    engine = importlib.import_module(\"tradingagents.risk_gate\")\n-    # Modules imported by the engine itself, excluding the test process baseline.\n-    source_file = getattr(engine, \"__file__\", \"\") or \"\"\n-    assert \"risk_gate\" in source_file\n-    for banned in _NETWORK_MODULES:\n-        mod = sys.modules.get(banned)\n-        # Presence in sys.modules is allowed if another test imported it; the\n-        # guarantee we test is that importing risk_gate alone does not require\n-        # these. Import it in a fresh subprocess-style check is out of scope for\n-        # a unit test, so assert the engine exposes no client attribute.\n-        if mod is not None:\n-            assert not hasattr(engine, banned)\n+def test_engine_imports_no_network_or_llm_module():\n+    \"\"\"NFR-A1: importing the engine alone pulls in no network or LLM client.\n+\n+    A subprocess imports ``tradingagents.risk_gate`` and reports whether any\n+    banned module is present, so a prior test's imports cannot mask the check.\n+    \"\"\"\n+    banned = [\"requests\", \"urllib3\", \"httpx\", \"curl_cffi\", \"yfinance\",\n+              \"langchain_core\", \"langchain_openai\", \"openai\"]\n+    code = textwrap.dedent(\n+        f\"\"\"\n+        import sys, json, importlib\n+        importlib.import_module(\"tradingagents.risk_gate\")\n+        banned = {banned!r}\n+        print(json.dumps([m for m in banned if m in sys.modules]))\n+        \"\"\"\n+    )\n+    proc = subprocess.run(\n+        [sys.executable, \"-c\", code],\n+        capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60,\n+    )\n+    assert proc.returncode == 0, proc.stderr\n+    loaded = __import__(\"json\").loads(proc.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1])\n+    assert loaded == [], f\"engine imported banned modules: {loaded}\"\n+\n+\n+@pytest.mark.unit\n+def test_core_latency_excludes_integration_overhead():\n+    \"\"\"NFR-A1/§11: core latency is measured on the pure engine only.\n+\n+    Integration overhead (graph/node wrapping) is covered by the integration\n+    tests. This asserts the pure evaluate loop is fast in isolation, so a p95\n+    regression can be attributed to the core rather than to graph plumbing.\n+    \"\"\"\n+    start = time.perf_counter()\n+    for _ in range(200):\n+        evaluate(make_buy())\n+    elapsed_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000.0 / 200\n+    assert elapsed_ms <= 2000.0, f\"core mean={elapsed_ms:.4f}ms\"\n",
        "additions": 64,
        "deletions": 42,
        "status": "modified"

        "patch": "Index: tests/risk_gate/test_policy_versioning.py\n===================================================================\n--- tests/risk_gate/test_policy_versioning.py\t\n+++ tests/risk_gate/test_policy_versioning.py\t\n@@ -1,55 +1,50 @@\n \"\"\"Policy versioning and injectable blacklist (FR-A1 §5.5).\n \n The policy is versioned (initially ``fr-a1-v1``) with a stable hash that changes\n when a threshold changes. The blacklist is deterministic and injectable, and\n ticker matching is normalization-consistent.\n \"\"\"\n \n from __future__ import annotations\n \n import pytest\n \n-pytest.importorskip(\n-    \"tradingagents.risk_gate\",\n-    reason=\"tradingagents.risk_gate not implemented yet (pre-implementation)\",\n-)\n+from tests.risk_gate._support import R5, evaluate, make_buy, violated_ids\n \n-from tests.risk_gate._support import R5, evaluate, make_buy, violated_ids  # noqa: E402\n \n-\n @pytest.mark.unit\n def test_default_policy_version_and_hash():\n     \"\"\"FR-A1 §5.5: default policy is fr-a1-v1 with a non-empty stable hash.\"\"\"\n     rg = __import__(\"tradingagents.risk_gate\", fromlist=[\"RiskPolicy\"])\n     p1 = rg.RiskPolicy()\n     p2 = rg.RiskPolicy()\n     assert p1.version == \"fr-a1-v1\"\n-    assert p1.policy_hash\n+    assert p1.policy_hash and len(p1.policy_hash) >= 16\n     assert p1.policy_hash == p2.policy_hash\n \n \n @pytest.mark.unit\n def test_hash_changes_when_a_threshold_changes():\n     \"\"\"FR-A1 §5.5: changing a threshold changes the policy hash.\"\"\"\n     rg = __import__(\"tradingagents.risk_gate\", fromlist=[\"RiskPolicy\"])\n     base = rg.RiskPolicy()\n     changed = rg.RiskPolicy(single_name_cap=0.20)\n     assert base.policy_hash != changed.policy_hash\n \n \n @pytest.mark.unit\n def test_policy_version_reaches_evaluation():\n     \"\"\"FR-A1 §5.5: the evaluation records the policy version and hash.\"\"\"\n     result = evaluate(make_buy())\n     assert result.policy_version == \"fr-a1-v1\"\n     assert result.policy_hash\n \n \n @pytest.mark.unit\n @pytest.mark.parametrize(\"ticker\", [\"AAPL\", \"aapl\", \" Aapl \"])\n def test_blacklist_matches_after_normalization(ticker):\n     \"\"\"FR-A1 §5.5: blacklist matching is normalization-consistent.\"\"\"\n     rg = __import__(\"tradingagents.risk_gate\", fromlist=[\"RiskPolicy\"])\n     result = evaluate(make_buy(ticker=ticker), policy=rg.RiskPolicy(blacklist=frozenset({\"AAPL\"})))\n     assert result.verdict == \"REJECTED\"\n     assert R5 in violated_ids(result)\n",

        "patch": "Index: tests/risk_gate/test_projected_exposure.py\n===================================================================\n--- tests/risk_gate/test_projected_exposure.py\t\n+++ tests/risk_gate/test_projected_exposure.py\t\n@@ -1,66 +1,107 @@\n-\"\"\"Projected-exposure calculations (FR-A1 §5.3).\n+\"\"\"Projected post-trade exposure calculations (FR-A1 §5.3).\n \n-Single-name weight comes from the explicit structured ``target_position_weight``.\n-Sector exposure is the projected share of the sector after the trade, computed\n-from the snapshot's market values (never average cost). These tests pin the\n-denominator and aggregation used by R2/R3.\n+Under the documented cash-funded long assumption:\n+\n+    projected_stock_value  = target_weight * portfolio_value\n+    projected_sector_value = current_sector_value - current_stock_value\n+                             + projected_stock_value\n+\n+Exposure uses market values, never average cost. The target stock's sector is\n+supplied explicitly on ``target_position`` when the stock is not already held;\n+it is never inferred from prose or fetched over the network. 300k of 1M in Technology = 30% -> allowed (inclusive).\n-    assert evaluate(data).verdict == \"APPROVED\"\n+    # AAPL unheld; projected Technology = 200,000 + 50,000 = 250,000 = 25% <= 30%.\n+    result = evaluate(make_buy(portfolio=portfolio, target_position=make_target(0.05)))\n+    assert result.verdict == \"APPROVED\"\n \n \n @pytest.mark.unit\n def test_sector_exposure_uses_market_value_not_cost():\n-    \"\"\"FR-A1 §5.3: exposure uses market values; average cost is never substituted.\"\"\"\n-    # projected Technology = 300,000 + 50,000 = 350,000 = 35% > 30%.\n+    result = evaluate(make_buy(portfolio=portfolio))\n     assert result.verdict == \"REJECTED\"\n+    assert R3 in violated_ids(result)\n \n \n @pytest.mark.unit\n+def test_increase_that_crosses_sector_limit_is_rejected():\n+    \"\"\"FR-A1 §5.3: a purchase that crosses 30% is rejected even if under before.\"\"\"\n+    portfolio = make_portfolio(\n+        holdings=[\n+            {\"ticker\": \"AAPL\", \"market_value\": 0.0, \"sector\": \"Technology\"},\n+            {\"ticker\": \"MSFT\", \"market_value\": 280_000.0, \"sector\": \"Technology\"},\n+            {\"ticker\": \"JPM\", \"market_value\": 660_000.0, \"sector\": \"Financials\"},\n+        ],\n+        cash=60_000.0,\n+        portfolio_value=1_000_000.0,\n+    )\n+    #
