It is\n written before production implementation so the tests can be reviewed. Tests\n reference the requirement/invariant they enforce. Intentional safety-related\n behavior changes are marked `[SAFETY]`; everything else must remain an existing\n behavior (`[PRESERVE]`).\n \n ## 1. Proposed interface (contract under review)\n \n The tests are written against this interface. It is expected to match the\n eventual implementation; production code is not written yet.\n \n ### 1.1 Package `tradingagents.risk_gate`\n \n Modules (proposed): `models.py`, `policy.py`, `engine.py`, `sizing.py`,\n `portfolio_snapshot.py`, `node.py` (integration). The core engine modules have no\n network, no file I/O, no LLM imports.\n \n ### 1.2 Enumerations\n \n ```python\n class RiskVerdict(StrEnum):\n     APPROVED = \"APPROVED\"\n     REJECTED = \"REJECTED\"\n     NEEDS_REVIEW = \"NEEDS_REVIEW\"\n \n class DecisionStatus(StrEnum):\n     ACTIONABLE = \"ACTIONABLE\"\n     BLOCKED = \"BLOCKED\"\n     PENDING_REVIEW = \"PENDING_REVIEW\"\n     NO_TRADE = \"NO_TRADE\"\n \n class RuleOutcome(StrEnum):\n     PASS = \"PASS\"\n     VIOLATED = \"VIOLATED\"\n     NOT_APPLICABLE = \"NOT_APPLICABLE\"\n     UNKNOWN = \"UNKNOWN\"\n ```\n \n ### 1.3 Rule identifiers\n \n | ID | Meaning |\n |---|---|\n | `R1_STOP_LOSS_REQUIRED` | Long actionable BUY must carry a stop-loss |\n | `R2_SINGLE_NAME_CAP` | Projected single-name weight ≤ 10% (0.10) |\n | `R3_SECTOR_CONCENTRATION` | Projected sector exposure ≤ 30% (0.30) |\n | `R4_REWARD_RISK` | Direction-aware reward-to-risk ≥ 1.5 and ordering stop<entry<target |\n | `R5_BLACKLIST` | Ticker not on the deterministic blacklist |\n | `R6_INPUT_INTEGRITY` | Structured inputs present, consistent, unambiguous |\n | `R0_ALL_RULES_PASSED` | Positive marker so every verdict carries a rule ID |\n \n `R0` is a synthetic \"pass\" entry: every evaluation carries at least one rule ID,\n satisfying \"100% of verdicts carry a rule identifier\" (`requirements.yaml:28`),\n including clean approvals.\n \n ### 1.4 Input models\n \n ```python\n class TargetPosition(BaseModel):\n     target_position_weight: float | None   # projected post-trade single-name weight, 0..1\n     sector: str | None = None               # target stock's sector, required when not held\n \n class Holding(BaseModel):\n     ticker: str\n     market_value: float          # current market value; never average cost\n     sector: str | None\n \n class PortfolioRiskSnapshot(BaseModel):\n     valuation_date: str          # ISO date; must be consistent with the run's trade_date\n     portfolio_value: float       # total portfolio value used for weight denominators\n     cash: float                  # cash available to fund a cash-funded long\n     holdings: list[Holding]\n     # consistency: cash + Σ holdings.market_value == portfolio_value\n \n class RiskInputs(BaseModel):\n     ticker: str\n     trade_date: str\n     action: str | None           # TraderProposal.action, if structured output produced it\n     entry_price: float | None\n     stop_loss: float | None\n     price_target: float | None   # PortfolioDecision.price_target\n     model_rating: str | None     # PortfolioDecision.rating, verbatim\n     target_position: TargetPosition | None\n     portfolio: PortfolioRiskSnapshot | None\n ```\n \n **Projected exposure (cash-funded long, documented for v1):**\n `projected_stock_value = target_position_weight * portfolio_value`;\n `projected_sector_value = current_sector_value - current_stock_value +\n projected_stock_value`. A genuine BUY increases the position and the purchase\n (`projected_stock_value - current_stock_value`) is affordable from `cash`. Missing\n target sector for an unheld stock, or an inconsistent snapshot, makes the affected\n rule `UNKNOWN` → `NEEDS_REVIEW`, never `APPROVED`.\n \n ### 1.5 Output models\n \n ```python\n class RuleResult(BaseModel):\n     rule_id: str\n     outcome: RuleOutcome\n     detail: str                      # deterministic; no PII/credentials\n     observed: float | None = None\n     threshold: float | None = None\n \n class RiskEvaluation(BaseModel):\n     verdict: RiskVerdict\n     decision_status: DecisionStatus\n     model_rating: str | None\n     evaluated_rule_ids: list[str]        # every rule considered\n     triggered_violation_ids: list[str]   # only VIOLATED rule ids\n     rule_results: list[RuleResult]       # complete per-rule results\n     policy_version: str\n     policy_hash: str\n     input_snapshot: dict                 # minimal, redacted snapshot\n     evaluated_at_utc: str                # ISO8601 UTC\n     latency_ms: float\n \n class RiskAuditRecord(BaseModel):\n     audit_id: str\n     evaluation: RiskEvaluation\n ```\n \n ### 1.6 Engine entry points\n \n ```python\n def evaluate_risk(inputs: RiskInputs, policy: RiskPolicy | None = None) -> RiskEvaluation: ...\n \n class RiskPolicy:\n     version: str          # \"fr-a1-v1\"\n     policy_hash: str      # stable hash of the constants\n     single_name_cap: float = 0.10\n     sector_cap: float = 0.30\n     min_reward_risk: float = 1.5\n     blacklist: frozenset[str] = frozenset()\n ```\n \n `evaluate_risk` is pure and deterministic. Ticker normalization uses\n `tradingagents.dataflows.symbols.normalize_symbol`.\n \n ## 2. Rule semantics and applicability\n \n Precedence for the final verdict: `REJECTED > NEEDS_REVIEW > APPROVED`.\n \n **UNKNOWN is not VIOLATED.** `triggered_violation_ids` lists only rules whose\n outcome is `VIOLATED`; `evaluated_rule_ids` lists every rule considered. When a\n rule cannot be decided for lack of input it is `UNKNOWN` (→ `NEEDS_REVIEW`), not a\n violation. Example: a missing stop-loss makes `R1` `VIOLATED` while `R4` is\n `UNKNOWN` (the ratio cannot be computed).\n \n **Three separate concepts at the boundary:** `model_rating` (the PM's own rating,\n preserved), `risk_verdict` (from the gate), and the *effective public signal*\n (a non-`APPROVED` actionable direction surfaces as the existing `REVIEW`\n sentinel). `final_rating`/`run_rating` keep their baseline meaning — the **model**\n rating — and are not redefined; the gate produces the effective public signal\n separately so blocked recommendations cannot escape as an actionable BUY.\n \n | Rule | Applies when | Violated → | Unknown/inapplicable → |\n |---|---|---|---|\n | R1 stop-loss | long actionable BUY (action Buy) | REJECTED | — |\n | R2 single-name | BUY with a resolvable weight | REJECTED (>0.10) | NEEDS_REVIEW (R2 UNKNOWN: missing weight) |\n | R3 sector | BUY with a resolvable snapshot | REJECTED (>0.30) | NEEDS_REVIEW (R3 UNKNOWN: unknown sector/value) |\n | R4 reward-risk | BUY with entry/stop/target | REJECTED (ratio<1.5 or bad ordering) | NEEDS_REVIEW (R4 UNKNOWN: missing leg) |\n | R5 blacklist | any ticker | REJECTED (on list) | — (list always known) |\n | R6 input integrity | always | — | NEEDS_REVIEW (R6 UNKNOWN: missing/contradictory/inconsistent) |\n \n BUY: all of R1–R5 apply. HOLD: no actionable trade; approved HOLD → `NO_TRADE`\n (R4 `NOT_APPLICABLE` is a pending decision). SELL/short without explicit\n existing-position and trade data → not `APPROVED` (mandatory); exact risk-reducing\n criteria are pending team confirmation. The sector cap applies to the **affected\n sector** of the target stock in v1 (scope pending confirmation).\n \n ## 3. Requirement traceability\n \n | Requirement | Contract element | Test file |\n |---|---|---|\n | FR-A1 verdict + rule IDs | `evaluate_risk`, `rule_results` | `test_rules.py`, `test_verdict_semantics.py` |\n | FR-A1 5 injected violations 5/5 blocked | R1–R5 fixtures | `test_rule_violations.py` |\n | FR-A1 100 invalid fixtures 0 approvals | fixture generator | `test_100_invalid_fixtures.py` |\n | INV-A1 no approval without stop / over cap | invariants | `test_invariants.py` |\n | NFR-A1 p95 ≤ 2 s, 0 network | pure engine + runtime/structural guard | `test_latency_no_network.py` |\n | NFR-A2 audit completeness | `RiskAuditRecord` | `test_audit_trail.py` |\n | §5.1 verdict affects recommendation | boundary enforcement | `test_decision_boundary.py` |\n | §5.2 NO_TRADE for approved HOLD | `DecisionStatus` | `test_verdict_semantics.py` |\n | §5.3 structured weight/snapshot | `TargetPosition`, `PortfolioRiskSnapshot` | `test_input_contract.py` |\n | §5.4 trade scope | applicability | `test_trade_scope.py` |\n | §5.5 policy version/hash | `RiskPolicy` | `test_policy_versioning.py` |\n | Structured retention (API+CLI) | state keys | `test_integration_retention.py` |\n \n ## 4. Test matrix\n \n All tests are `@pytest.mark.unit`, offline (the repo's `conftest.py` already\n blocks sockets), parameterized deterministically. Files live under `tests/risk_gate/`.\n \n ### 4.1 Rule-level (`test_rules.py`)\n \n - R1: BUY missing stop → REJECTED, id `R1_STOP_LOSS_REQUIRED`.\n - R2: weight 0.12 → REJECTED; weight 0.10 → PASS; weight 0.099 → PASS.\n - R3: sector 0.35 → REJECTED; 0.30 → PASS.\n - R4: long RR 2.0 → PASS; RR 0.5 → REJECTED; short direction-aware.\n - R5: blacklisted ticker → REJECTED; normalization for `aapl`/`AAPL`.\n - Valid BUY (all in bounds) → APPROVED, `R0_ALL_RULES_PASSED` present.\n - Wrong-side stop (long stop ≥ entry) → REJECTED; wrong-side target → REJECTED.\n \n ### 4.2 Exact boundaries (`test_boundaries.py`)\n \n-- 10% weight: `0.10` PASS, next representable above → REJECTED.\n+- 10% weight: `0.10` PASS, next representable above → REJECTED. The fixture holds a\n+  positive AAPL position, so a target weight of `0.0` (and a target equal to the\n+  held value) is **not approved** — a genuine BUY must increase the position.\n - 30% **projected post-trade** sector: `0.30` PASS (inclusive), just over REJECTED.\n - 1.5 RR: exactly `1.5` PASS; `1.4999...` REJECTED.\n \n ### 4.3 Injected violations (`test_rule_violations.py`)\n \n Five individually isolated fixtures, each asserting the expected rule id is\n `VIOLATED` and verdict `REJECTED`, with the *other* rules not violated: missing\n stop (R1; R4 may be UNKNOWN), single-name 12% (R2), projected sector 40% (R3),\n RR 0.5 (R4), blacklist (R5).\n \n ### 4.4 Malformed / missing inputs (`test_input_contract.py`)\n \n - Missing target position/weight → NEEDS_REVIEW, R2 `UNKNOWN`, PENDING_REVIEW.\n - Missing portfolio/sector → NEEDS_REVIEW, R3 `UNKNOWN`.\n - Missing target price → NEEDS_REVIEW, R4 `UNKNOWN`.\n - NaN/inf prices → NEEDS_REVIEW, never ACTIONABLE.\n - Contradictory proposal/decision direction → NEEDS_REVIEW (R6 `UNKNOWN`).\n - Inconsistent snapshot (holdings+cash ≠ portfolio_value), stale valuation date,\n   unaffordable purchase → NEEDS_REVIEW, never ACTIONABLE.\n \n ### 4.5 Verdict semantics (`test_verdict_semantics.py`)\n \n - Precedence REJECTED > NEEDS_REVIEW > APPROVED.\n - All applicable rules collected (no first-fail).\n - UNKNOWN is distinct from VIOLATED; `triggered_violation_ids` lists only VIOLATED.\n - `triggered_violation_ids` ⊆ `evaluated_rule_ids`; both present for clean runs.\n - Approved HOLD → `NO_TRADE`; approved BUY → `ACTIONABLE`; rejected → `BLOCKED`;\n   needs-review → `PENDING_REVIEW`; model rating preserved on reject.\n \n ### 4.6 Trade scope (`test_trade_scope.py`)\n \n Mandatory (hard assertions, not xfail): HOLD never ACTIONABLE; SELL/short without\n explicit position+trade data never APPROVED; ambiguous direction never APPROVED.\n A `test_proposed_*` records the pending SELL-with-data expectation separately.\n \n ### 4.7 Invariants (`test_invariants.py`)\n \n - APPROVED ⇒ stop-loss present for actionable BUY.\n - APPROVED ⇒ weight ≤ 0.10.\n - APPROVED ⇒ decision_status in {ACTIONABLE, NO_TRADE}.\n - Sweep over deterministic grid: no APPROVED violates INV-A1.\n \n ### 4.8 100 invalid fixtures (`test_100_invalid_fixtures.py`)\n \n Deterministically generated in code (no redundant JSON files) from meaningful,\n-reproducible cases spanning **all five rules plus input-integrity failures**,\n-including blacklist via a separate parametrization. Exactly 100 cases; assert\n-**0 of 100 APPROVED**, each with ≥1 non-`PASS` outcome, none ACTIONABLE.\n+reproducible cases spanning **all five rules plus input-integrity failures**.\n+Blacklist cases are **inside the actual 100** (not a separate test). Each case\n+declares the rule it targets and the outcome that rule must record:\n \n+- `VIOLATED` cases assert the expected rule id is present with `VIOLATED` and is in\n+  `triggered_violation_ids`.\n+- `UNKNOWN` (input-integrity) cases assert the referenced rule is `UNKNOWN` and is\n+  **not** falsely recorded as `VIOLATED`.\n+- Aggregate: **0 of 100 APPROVED**, none ACTIONABLE; all of R1–R5 and an\n+  input-integrity `UNKNOWN` outcome are represented; cases are distinct.\n+\n ### 4.9 Audit (`test_audit_trail.py`)\n \n - Required *values* verified (policy hash length, UTC timestamp format, latency,\n   snapshot non-empty and value-bearing), not mere key presence.\n - 10 evaluations → 100% audit coverage with identical version/hash.\n - No credentials or raw prompt fields.\n \n ### 4.10 Policy versioning (`test_policy_versioning.py`)\n \n - `version == \"fr-a1-v1\"`; `policy_hash` stable; distinct hash when a threshold\n   changes; version/hash recorded in evaluation.\n \n ### 4.11 Latency / no network (`test_latency_no_network.py`)\n \n - 1000 evaluations; measured **core** p95 ≤ 2000 ms; the measured p50/p95 is\n   reported in the test output. Core latency is distinguished from integration\n   overhead (graph wiring is covered separately).\n - A runtime socket guard (every connect/`getaddrinfo` refuses) is installed for the\n   evaluation loop; a subprocess structural check asserts importing the engine\n   alone pulls in no network/LLM module.\n \n ### 4.12 Integration acceptance (`test_integration_retention.py`, `test_decision_boundary.py`)\n \n-`[SAFETY]`/`[PRESERVE]` marked, real graph/CLI behavioral tests (not existence\n-checks). Sector tests verify **projected\n post-trade** exposure under the documented cash-funded assumption, not merely the\n current holdings.\n \"\"\"\n \n from __future__ import annotations\n \n import pytest\n \n from tests.risk_gate._support import (\n     R2,\n     R3,\n     R4,\n     evaluate,\n     make_buy,\n     make_target,\n     violated_ids,\n )\n \n # A fixed book for sector tests: portfolio 1,000,000, MSFT 150,000 technology,\n # and a non-technology holding filling the rest. The target stock is AAPL,\n # currently unheld, so projected Technology = MSFT + projected AAPL value.\n _BOOK_BASE = 1_000_000.0\n \n \n def _sector_book(projected_tech_total):\n     \"\"\"Build a cash-funded book where, after buying AAPL at weight 0.05\n     (50,000), Technology equals ``projected_tech_total``.\n \n     AAPL is unheld (0); MSFT carries the rest of Technology. here weight is the explicit projected weight.\n-    \"\"\"\n+    \"\"\"FR-A1: single-name cap is inclusive at 10% and a BUY must increase the holding.\"\"\"\n     result = evaluate(make_buy(target_position=make_target(weight)))\n     assert (result.verdict == \"APPROVED\") is approved\n-    if not approved:\n+    if not approved and weight > 0.10:\n         assert R2 in violated_ids(result)\n \n \n @pytest.mark.unit\n @pytest.mark.parametrize(\n     \"projected_tech_total, approved\",\n     [\n         (250_000.0, True),    # 25%\n         (299_999.0, True),    # just below\n         (300_000.0, True),    # exactly 30% (inclusive)\n         (300_001.0, False),   # just over\n         (350_000.0, False),   # 35%\n     ],\n     ids=[\"below\", \"just_below\", \"exactly_30pct\", \"just_over\", \"over\"],\n )\n def test_sector_cap_boundary(projected_tech_total, approved):\n     \"\"\"FR-A1: sector cap is inclusive at 30% on projected post-trade exposure.\"\"\"\n     data = make_buy(portfolio=_sector_book(projected_tech_total))\n     result = evaluate(data)\n     assert (result.verdict == \"APPROVED\") is approved\n     if not approved:\n         assert R3 in violated_ids(result)\n \n \n @pytest.mark.unit\n @pytest.mark.parametrize(\n     \"target, approved\",\n     [\n         (115.0, True),      # RR 1.5 exactly (reward 15 / risk 10)\n         (114.9999, False),  # just below\n         (130.0, True),      # comfortably above\n     ],\n     ids=[\"exactly_1_5\", \"just_below\", \"above\"],\n )\n def test_reward_risk_boundary(target, approved):\n     \"\"\"FR-A1: reward-to-risk floor is inclusive at 1.5.\"\"\"\n     result = evaluate(make_buy(stop_loss=90.0, price_target=target))\n     assert (result.verdict == \"APPROVED\") is approved\n     if not approved:\n         assert R4 in violated_ids(result)\n",

115: def _expand_to_100(base):
116:     """Deterministically expand the targeted cases to exactly 100.
117: 
118:     Cross-products of violations are meaningful invalid cases. The expansion is a
119:     fixed ordered product (no randomness), so every run reproduces the same 100
120:     cases. Single-rule cases come first for readability.

123: 
124:     # Two-dimension crosses first, then a three-way cross if still short.
125:     for (rule_a, a), (rule_b, b) in itertools.product(_R2_CASES, _R4_CASES):

134:     # Deduplicate by serialized payload while preserving order, then take 100.
135:     seen, unique = set(), []
136:     for rule, case in cases:
137:         key = repr(sorted(case.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[0]))
138:         if key not in seen:
139:             seen.add(key)
140:             unique.append((rule, case))
141:     assert len(unique) >= 100, f"only {len(unique)} unique invalid cases generated"
142:     return unique[:100]

_case(\"r6_contradictory_dir\", {\"action\": \"Buy\", \"model_rating\": \"Sell\"}, R6, \"UNKNOWN\"),\n    _case(\"r6_entry_nan\", {\"entry_price\": float(\"nan\")}, R6, \"UNKNOWN\"),\n    _case(\"r6_entry_inf\", {\"entry_price\": float(\"inf\")}, R6, \"UNKNOWN\"),\n    _case(\"r6_unknown_sector\", {\"portfolio\": make_portfolio(\n        holdings=[{\"ticker\": \"AAPL\", \"market_value\": 20_000.0, \"sector\": None},\n                  {\"ticker\": \"MSFT\", \"market_value\": 150_000.0, \"sector\": \"Technology\"}],\n        cash=830_000.0, portfolio_value=1_000_000.0)}, R3, \"UNKNOWN\"),\n    _case(\"r6_inconsistent_book\", {\"portfolio\": make_portfolio(\n        holdings=[{\"ticker\": \"AAPL\", \"market_value\": 20_000.0, \"sector\": \"Technology\"},\n                  {\"ticker\": \"MSFT\", \"market_value\": 150_000.0, \"sector\": \"Technology\"}],\n        cash=10_000.0, portfolio_value=1_000_000.0)}, R6, \"UNKNOWN\"),\n    _case(\"r6_stale_valuation\", {\"portfolio\": make_portfolio(\n        holdings=[{\"ticker\": \"AAPL\", \"market_value\": 20_000.0, \"sector\": \"Technology\"},\n                  {\"ticker\": \"MSFT\", \"market_value\": 150_000.0, \"sector\": \"Technology\"}],\n        cash=830_000.0, portfolio_value=1_000_000.0, valuation_date=\"2020-01-01\")},\n        R6, \"UNKNOWN\"),\n    _case(\"r6_affordability\", {\"target_position\": make_target(0.20),\n                               \"portfolio\": make_portfolio(\n                                   holdings=[{\"ticker\": \"AAPL\", \"market_value\": 20_000.0,\n                                              \"sector\": \"Technology\"},\n                                             {\"ticker\": \"MSFT\", \"market_value\": 150_000.0,\n                                              \"sector\": \"Technology\"}],\n                                   cash=10_000.0, portfolio_value=180_000.0)},\n          R6, \"UNKNOWN\"),\n]\n\n\ndef _base():\n    return _R1 + _R2 + _R3 + _R4 + _R5 + _R6\n\n\ndef _dedupe(cases):\n    seen, unique = set(), []\n    for c in cases:\n        key = repr((c[\"label\"], sorted(c[\"kwargs\"].items(), key=lambda kv: kv[0]),\n                    sorted(c[\"blacklist\"]) if c[\"blacklist\"] else None))\n        if key not in seen:\n            seen.add(key)\n            unique.append(c)\n    return unique\n\n\ndef _expand_to_100(base):\n    \"\"\"Deterministic expansion to exactly 100 distinct cases.\n\n    Two-way crosses (R2 x R4, R4 x R3, R5 x R4) are meaningful multi-violation\n    fixtures; the product is fixed (no randomness) so every run reproduces the\n    same 100. Single-rule cases come first for readability.\n    \"\"\"\n    cases = list(base)\n\n    for a, b in itertools.product(_R2, _R4):\n        cases.append(_case(f\"{a['label']}+{b['label']}\",\n                           {**a[\"kwargs\"], **b[\"kwargs\"]}, R2, \"VIOLATED\"))\n    for a, b in itertools.product(_R4, _R3):\n        cases.append(_case(f\"{a['label']}+{b['label']}\",\n                           {**a[\"kwargs\"], **b[\"kwargs\"]}, R3, \"VIOLATED\"))\n    for a, b in itertools.product(_R5, _R4):\n        cases.append(_case(f\"{a['label']}+{b['label']}\",\n                           {**a[\"kwargs\"], **b[\"kwargs\"]}, R5, \"VIOLATED\",\n                           blacklist=a[\"blacklist\"]))\n\n    if len(cases) < 100:\n        for a, b, c in itertools.product(_R2, _R4, _R6):\n            cases.append(_case(f\"{a['label']}+{b['label']}+{c['label']}\",\n                               {**a[\"kwargs\"], **b[\"kwargs\"], **c[\"kwargs\"]},\n                               R2, \"VIOLATED\"))\n\n    unique = _dedupe(cases)\n    assert len(unique) >= 100, f\"only {len(unique)} unique invalid cases generated\"\n    return unique[:100]\n\n\nCASES = _expand_to_100(_base())\nassert len(CASES) == 100\nassert any(c[\"rule\"] == R5 for c in CASES), \"blacklist must be in the 100\"\nassert any(c[\"outcome\"] == \"UNKNOWN\" for c in CASES), \"input-integrity must be in the 100\"\n\n\ndef _policy(case):\n    if case[\"blacklist\"] is None:\n        return None\n    rg = __import__(\"tradingagents.risk_gate\", fromlist=[\"RiskPolicy\"])\n    return rg.RiskPolicy(blacklist=case[\"blacklist\"])\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    \"case\",\n    CASES,\n    ids=[f\"{c['label']}_{i:03d}\" for i, c in enumerate(CASES)],\n)\ndef test_invalid_fixture_is_never_approved(case):\n    \"\"\"FR-A1/INV-A1: no invalid fixture is APPROVED; expected rule outcome holds.\"\"\"\n    result = evaluate(make_buy(**case[\"kwargs\"]), policy=_policy(case))\n    label = case[\"label\"]\n\n    assert result.verdict != \"APPROVED\", (label, case[\"kwargs\"])\n    assert result.decision_status != \"ACTIONABLE\", (label, case[\"kwargs\"])\n\n    outs = outcomes(result)\n    assert outs.get(case[\"rule\"]) == case[\"outcome\"], (label, outs)\n\n    if case[\"outcome\"] == \"VIOLATED\":\n        assert case[\"rule\"] in violated_ids(result), label\n        assert case[\"rule\"] in result.triggered_violation_ids, label\n    else:  # UNKNOWN must not be falsely recorded as VIOLATED\n        assert case[\"rule\"] not in violated_ids(result), label\n        assert case[\"rule\"] not in result.triggered_violation_ids, label\n\n    assert set(result.triggered_violation_ids) <= set(result.evaluated_rule_ids)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_zero_approvals_across_all_invalid_fixtures():\n    \"\"\"FR-A1: aggregate — 0 of 100 invalid fixtures approved.\"\"\"\n    approvals = [\n        c[\"label\"] for c in CASES\n        if evaluate(make_buy(**c[\"kwargs\"]), policy=_policy(c)).verdict == \"APPROVED\"\n    ]\n    assert approvals == [], f\"invalid fixtures approved: {approvals}\"\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_all_rules_and_integrity_are_represented():\n    \"\"\"FR-A1: the 100 cases cover R1-R5 and input-integrity UNKNOWN outcomes.\"\"\"\n    rules = {c[\"rule\"] for c in CASES}\n    assert {R1, R2, R3, R4, R5}.issubset(rules), rules\n    assert any(c[\"rule\"] == R6 or c[\"outcome\"] == \"UNKNOWN\" for c in CASES)\n",

246: ## 10. Pending team-confirmation decisions
247: 
248: Recorded here and mirrored in the test plan; production must not assume them.
249: 
250: - **D-scope-1 (sector cap scope):** affected sector only (v1 default) vs all sectors.

252:   explicit existing-position and trade data. Until confirmed, unsupported SELL and
253:   ambiguous direction are never `APPROVED`; HOLD is never `ACTIONABLE`.
254: - **D-scope-3 (HOLD rule exemptions):** whether `R4` is `NOT_APPLICABLE` for HOLD.
255: 
256: ## 9. Compliance
257: 
258: - This is new implementation work; the inherited TradingAgents baseline is
259:   explicitly not counted as the team's contribution beyond the integration points

262:   implementation, per the course's safety-critical process.

Proposed production files:\n\n- `tradingagents/risk_gate/__init__.py` (public exports)\n- `tradingagents/risk_gate/models.py` (enums, rule result, evaluation, audit, inputs)\n- `tradingagents/risk_gate/policy.py` (versioned `fr-a1-v1` policy + stable hash)\n- `tradingagents/risk_gate/sizing.py` (projected-weight derivation/validation)\n- `tradingagents/risk_gate/portfolio_snapshot.py` (consistency + projected exposure)\n- `tradingagents/risk_gate/engine.py` (pure `evaluate_risk` implementing R1–R6)\n\nStructural constraints for the core (verified by tests, not prose only):\n\n- No network, no file I/O, no LLM, no LangGraph import in the core modules.\n- Deterministic, pure: same inputs → same evaluation (timestamps/latency aside).\n- `triggered_violation_ids` ⊂ `evaluated_rule_ids`; only `VIOLATED` in the former.\n- Precedence `REJECTED > NEEDS_REVIEW > APPROVED`; no `APPROVED` for any\n  non-increasive, unaffordable, inconsistent, or over-cap decision.\n- Malformed numeric inputs (`NaN`/`inf`) cannot validate into an approved result.\n- Every evaluation yields complete per-rule results and an audit record.\n\nCore-only verification command:\n\n```\npytest tests/risk_gate -q \\\n  --ignore=tests/risk_gate/test_integration_retention.py \\\n  --ignore=tests/risk_gate/test_decision_boundary.py\n```\n\n### Stage 2 — integration (separate review and approval)\n\nAdds `tradingagents/risk_gate/node.py` and edits `state.py`, `trader.py`,\n`portfolio_manager.py`, `setup.py`, and `trading_graph.py` (state keys, structured\nretention, checkpoint marker, state-log fields). # Corrections Complete — Final Core Approval Checkpoint

All remaining core-test defects corrected. No production code, shared requirements, CI, or commits touched. No external APIs, no credentials, no dependency installs.

## Corrections applied

**1. Inconsistent fixtures fixed**
- `test_boundaries.py`: the 10% boundary now treats `0.0` and a target equal to the held value as **not approved** (a genuine BUY must increase the positive AAPL holding). Only genuinely increasing weights ≤ 0.10 pass.
- `test_input_contract.py`: affordability fixture rebuilt as a consistent book (AAPL 20,000 + MSFT 150,000 + cash 10,000 = 180,000) with target weight 0.20 → projected 36,000, a genuine **+16,000** increase that the 10,000 cash cannot fund. Positive fixtures remain affordable and internally consistent.

**2. 100 invalid fixtures finalized**
- Blacklist cases are now **inside the actual 100** (AAPL/MSFT/TSLA), not a separate test.
- Each of the 100 carries a declared target rule and expected outcome. `VIOLATED` cases assert the rule id is present with `VIOLATED` and in `triggered_violation_ids`; `UNKNOWN` (input-integrity) cases assert the rule is `UNKNOWN` and **not** falsely `VIOLATED`. Cases are distinct and reproducible (fixed, non-random expansion).

**3. Core contract preserved/confirmed**
- All five rules (R1–R5) plus R6 input integrity; explicit structured inputs; `REJECTED > NEEDS_REVIEW > APPROVED`; complete per-rule audit; pure core (no network/file-I/O/LLM). NaN/inf cannot yield an approved recommendation. v1 scope (cash-funded long BUY, affected-sector concentration, HOLD never actionable, unsupported SELL/short never approved) encoded as hard assertions. Pending policy decisions recorded explicitly in ADR §12 and test plan §7.

**4. Core vs integration separated**
- ADR §11 and test plan §8 define Stage 1 (core engine only, new `tradingagents/risk_gate/` files, no graph/agent/CLI/reporting/rating/memory/checkpoint changes) and Stage 2 (integration). `test_integration_retention.py` and `test_decision_boundary.py` are explicitly marked **NOT approved** for the core stage and excluded from the core-only command.

**5. Docs updated** to match (boundary no-increase rule, affordability fixture, blacklist-in-100, UNKNOWN-not-VIOLATED, staging, file-write scope, container constraints, reopening conditions).

## Exact corrected test files (this turn)
- `tests/risk_gate/test_boundaries.py` (no-increase boundary)
- `tests/risk_gate/test_input_contract.py` (affordability fixture)
- `tests/risk_gate/test_100_invalid_fixtures.py` (blacklist in 100, expected rule/outcome, UNKNOWN≠VIOLATED, no metadata-only pass)

## Final core public interface
`RiskVerdict{APPROVED,REJECTED,NEEDS_REVIEW}`, `DecisionStatus{ACTIONABLE,BLOCKED,PENDING_REVIEW,NO_TRADE}`, `RuleOutcome{PASS,VIOLATED,NOT_APPLICABLE,UNKNOWN}`. `RuleResult`, `RiskEvaluation` (verdict, decision_status, model_rating, evaluated_rule_ids, triggered_violation_ids, rule_results, policy_version/hash, redacted snapshot, UTC timestamp, latency), `RiskAuditRecord`. Inputs: `RiskInputs`, `TargetPosition{target_position_weight,sector}`, `PortfolioRiskSnapshot{valuation_date,portfolio_value,cash,holdings}`. Engine: `evaluate_risk(inputs, policy=None)`; `RiskPolicy(version="fr-a1-v1", policy_hash, 0.10/0.30/1.5, blacklist)`.

## Proposed core-stage production files (Stage 1 only)
`tradingagents/risk_gate/` → `__init__.py`, `models.py`, `policy.py`, `sizing.py`, `portfolio_snapshot.py`, `engine.py`. No edits to existing source.

## Core-only test command
```
pytest tests/risk_gate -q \
  --ignore=tests/risk_gate/test_integration_retention.py \
  --ignore=tests/risk_gate/test_decision_boundary.py
```

## Remaining integration tasks (Stage 2, separate approval)
Add `node.py`; edit `state.py`, `trader.py`, `portfolio_manager.py`, `setup.py`, `trading_graph.py` (structured retention, boundary enforcement, checkpoint marker, state-log fields); approve/enable the 10 integration tests.

| integration files collect | 0 | **10 collected** (not approved) |

Regression suite not rerun (recently passed 1412). Skipped not conflated with failed: all collected core tests genuinely fail pre-implementation.

## Git summary
No tracked-file changes; new untracked files only: `docs/architecture/adr/adr-fr-a1-risk-gate.md`, `docs/req/fr-a1-test-plan.md`, `tests/risk_gate/` (19 files).

STOP — awaiting your explicit approval to implement the Stage 1 core engine.

never average cost\n     sector: str | None\n \n class PortfolioRiskSnapshot(BaseModel):\n     valuation_date: str          # ISO date; must be consistent with the run's trade_date\n     portfolio_value: float       # total portfolio value used for weight denominators\n     cash: float                  # cash available to fund a cash-funded long\n     holdings: list[Holding]\n     # consistency: cash + Σ holdings.market_value == portfolio_value\n \n class RiskInputs(BaseModel):\n     ticker: str\n     trade_date: str\n     action: str | None           # TraderProposal.action, if structured output produced it\n     entry_price: float | None\n     stop_loss: float | None\n     price_target: float | None   # PortfolioDecision.price_target\n     model_rating: str | None     # PortfolioDecision.rating, verbatim\n     target_position: TargetPosition | None\n     portfolio: PortfolioRiskSnapshot | None\n ```\n \n **Projected exposure (cash-funded long, documented for v1):**\n `projected_stock_value = target_position_weight * portfolio_value`;\n `projected_sector_value = current_sector_value - current_stock_value +\n projected_stock_value`. A genuine BUY increases the position and the purchase\n (`projected_stock_value - current_stock_value`) is affordable from `cash`. Missing\n target sector for an unheld stock, or an inconsistent snapshot, makes the affected\n rule `UNKNOWN` → `NEEDS_REVIEW`, never `APPROVED`.\n \n ### 1.5 Output models\n \n ```python\n class RuleResult(BaseModel):\n     rule_id: str\n     outcome: RuleOutcome\n     detail: str                      # deterministic; no PII/credentials\n     observed: float | None = None\n     threshold: float | None = None\n \n class RiskEvaluation(BaseModel):\n     verdict: RiskVerdict\n     decision_status: DecisionStatus\n     model_rating: str | None\n     evaluated_rule_ids: list[str]        # every rule considered\n     triggered_violation_ids: list[str]   # only VIOLATED rule ids\n     rule_results: list[RuleResult]       # complete per-rule results\n     policy_version: str\n     policy_hash: str\n     input_snapshot: dict                 # minimal, redacted snapshot\n     evaluated_at_utc: str                # ISO8601 UTC\n     latency_ms: float\n \n class RiskAuditRecord(BaseModel):\n     audit_id: str\n     evaluation: RiskEvaluation\n ```\n \n ### 1.6 Engine entry points\n \n ```python\n def evaluate_risk(inputs: RiskInputs, policy: RiskPolicy | None = None) -> RiskEvaluation: ...\n \n class RiskPolicy:\n     version: str          # \"fr-a1-v1\"\n     policy_hash: str      # stable hash of the constants\n     single_name_cap: float = 0.10\n     sector_cap: float = 0.30\n     min_reward_risk: float = 1.5\n     blacklist: frozenset[str] = frozenset()\n ```\n \n `evaluate_risk` is pure and deterministic. Ticker normalization uses\n `tradingagents.dataflows.symbols.normalize_symbol`.\n \n ## 2. Rule semantics and applicability\n \n Precedence for the final verdict: `REJECTED > NEEDS_REVIEW > APPROVED`.\n \n **UNKNOWN is not VIOLATED.** `triggered_violation_ids` lists only rules whose\n outcome is `VIOLATED`; `evaluated_rule_ids` lists every rule considered. When a\n rule cannot be decided for lack of input it is `UNKNOWN` (→ `NEEDS_REVIEW`), not a\n violation. Example: a missing stop-loss makes `R1` `VIOLATED` while `R4` is\n `UNKNOWN` (the ratio cannot be computed).\n \n **Three separate concepts at the boundary:** `model_rating` (the PM's own rating,\n preserved), `risk_verdict` (from the gate), and the *effective public signal*\n (a non-`APPROVED` actionable direction surfaces as the existing `REVIEW`\n sentinel). `final_rating`/`run_rating` keep their baseline meaning — the **model**\n rating — and are not redefined; the gate produces the effective public signal\n separately so blocked recommendations cannot escape as an actionable BUY.\n \n | Rule | Applies when | Violated → | Unknown/inapplicable → |\n |---|---|---|---|\n | R1 stop-loss | long actionable BUY (action Buy) | REJECTED | — |\n | R2 single-name | BUY with a resolvable weight | REJECTED (>0.10) | NEEDS_REVIEW (R2 UNKNOWN: missing weight) |\n | R3 sector | BUY with a resolvable snapshot | REJECTED (>0.30) | NEEDS_REVIEW (R3 UNKNOWN: unknown sector/value) |\n | R4 reward-risk | BUY with entry/stop/target | REJECTED (ratio<1.5 or bad ordering) | NEEDS_REVIEW (R4 UNKNOWN: missing leg) |\n | R5 blacklist | any ticker | REJECTED (on list) | — (list always known) |\n | R6 input integrity | always | — | NEEDS_REVIEW (R6 UNKNOWN: missing/contradictory/inconsistent) |\n \n BUY: all of R1–R5 apply. HOLD: no actionable trade; approved HOLD → `NO_TRADE`\n (R4 `NOT_APPLICABLE` is a pending decision). SELL/short without explicit\n existing-position and trade data → not `APPROVED` (mandatory); exact risk-reducing\n criteria are pending team confirmation. The sector cap applies to the **affected\n sector** of the target stock in v1 (scope pending confirmation).\n \n ## 3. Requirement traceability\n \n | Requirement | Contract element | Test file |\n |---|---|---|\n | FR-A1 verdict + rule IDs | `evaluate_risk`, `rule_results` | `test_rules.py`, `test_verdict_semantics.py` |\n | FR-A1 5 injected violations 5/5 blocked | R1–R5 fixtures | `test_rule_violations.py` |\n | FR-A1 100 invalid fixtures 0 approvals | fixture generator | `test_100_invalid_fixtures.py` |\n | INV-A1 no approval without stop / over cap | invariants | `test_invariants.py` |\n | NFR-A1 p95 ≤ 2 s, 0 network | pure engine + runtime/structural guard | `test_latency_no_network.py` |\n | NFR-A2 audit completeness | `RiskAuditRecord` | `test_audit_trail.py` |\n | §5.1 verdict affects recommendation | boundary enforcement | `test_decision_boundary.py` |\n | §5.2 NO_TRADE for approved HOLD | `DecisionStatus` | `test_verdict_semantics.py` |\n | §5.3 structured weight/snapshot | `TargetPosition`, `PortfolioRiskSnapshot` | `test_input_contract.py` |\n | §5.4 trade scope | applicability | `test_trade_scope.py` |\n | §5.5 policy version/hash | `RiskPolicy` | `test_policy_versioning.py` |\n | Structured retention (API+CLI) | state keys | `test_integration_retention.py` |\n \n ## 4. Test matrix\n \n All tests are `@pytest.mark.unit`, offline (the repo's `conftest.py` already\n blocks sockets), parameterized deterministically. Files live under `tests/risk_gate/`.\n \n ### 4.1 Rule-level (`test_rules.py`)\n \n - R1: BUY missing stop → REJECTED, id `R1_STOP_LOSS_REQUIRED`.\n - R2: weight 0.12 → REJECTED; weight 0.10 → PASS; weight 0.099 → PASS.\n - R3: sector 0.35 → REJECTED; 0.30 → PASS.\n - R4: long RR 2.0 → PASS; RR 0.5 → REJECTED; short direction-aware.\n - R5: blacklisted ticker → REJECTED; normalization for `aapl`/`AAPL`.\n - Valid BUY (all in bounds) → APPROVED, `R0_ALL_RULES_PASSED` present.\n - Wrong-side stop (long stop ≥ entry) → REJECTED; wrong-side target → REJECTED.\n \n ### 4.2 Exact boundaries (`test_boundaries.py`)\n \n - 10% weight: `0.10` PASS, next representable above → REJECTED. The fixture holds a\n   positive AAPL position, so a target weight of `0.0` (and a target equal to the\n   held value) is **not approved** — a genuine BUY must increase the position.\n - 30% **projected post-trade** sector: `0.30` PASS (inclusive), just over REJECTED.\n - 1.5 RR: exactly `1.5` PASS; `1.4999...` REJECTED.\n \n ### 4.3 Injected violations (`test_rule_violations.py`)\n \n Five individually isolated fixtures, each asserting the expected rule id is\n `VIOLATED` and verdict `REJECTED`, with the *other* rules not violated: missing\n stop (R1; R4 may be UNKNOWN), single-name 12% (R2), projected sector 40% (R3),\n RR 0.5 (R4), blacklist (R5).\n \n ### 4.4 Malformed / missing inputs (`test_input_contract.py`)\n \n - Missing target position/weight → NEEDS_REVIEW, R2 `UNKNOWN`, PENDING_REVIEW.\n - Missing portfolio/sector → NEEDS_REVIEW, R3 `UNKNOWN`.\n - Missing target price → NEEDS_REVIEW, R4 `UNKNOWN`.\n - NaN/inf prices → NEEDS_REVIEW, never ACTIONABLE.\n - Contradictory proposal/decision direction → NEEDS_REVIEW (R6 `UNKNOWN`).\n - Inconsistent snapshot (holdings+cash ≠ portfolio_value), stale valuation date,\n   unaffordable purchase → NEEDS_REVIEW, never ACTIONABLE.\n \n ### 4.5 Verdict semantics (`test_verdict_semantics.py`)\n \n - Precedence REJECTED > NEEDS_REVIEW > APPROVED.\n - All applicable rules collected (no first-fail).\n - UNKNOWN is distinct from VIOLATED; `triggered_violation_ids` lists only VIOLATED.\n - `triggered_violation_ids` ⊆ `evaluated_rule_ids`; both present for clean runs.\n - Approved HOLD → `NO_TRADE`; approved BUY → `ACTIONABLE`; rejected → `BLOCKED`;\n   needs-review → `PENDING_REVIEW`; model rating preserved on reject.\n \n ### 4.6 Trade scope (`test_trade_scope.py`)\n \n Mandatory (hard assertions, not xfail): HOLD never ACTIONABLE; SELL/short without\n explicit position+trade data never APPROVED; ambiguous direction never APPROVED.\n A `test_proposed_*` records the pending SELL-with-data expectation separately.\n \n ### 4.7 Invariants (`test_invariants.py`)\n \n - APPROVED ⇒ stop-loss present for actionable BUY.\n - APPROVED ⇒ weight ≤ 0.10.\n - APPROVED ⇒ decision_status in {ACTIONABLE, NO_TRADE}.\n - Sweep over deterministic grid: no APPROVED violates INV-A1.\n \n ### 4.8 100 invalid fixtures (`test_100_invalid_fixtures.py`)\n \n-Deterministically generated in code (no redundant JSON files) from meaningful,\n-reproducible cases spanning **all five rules plus input-integrity failures**.\n-Blacklist cases are **inside the actual 100** (not a separate test). {
  "content": "\"\"\"100 deterministic invalid fixtures with zero approvals (FR-A1, INV-A1).\n\nCases are simple, independent, reproducible parameterized descriptors (no fragile\ndictionary-merging cross-products). Exactly 100 **distinct** fixtures are\nexercised, covering R1-R6 including blacklist violations. Distinctness is\ndetermined by the actual input payload and the policy (blacklist), excluding the\nhuman-readable label.\n\nEach case declares the rule it targets and the outcome that rule must record\n(``VIOLATED`` or ``UNKNOWN``). The test asserts the *expected outcome against the\nactual fixture values*:\n- the verdict is never APPROVED and the decision is never ACTIONABLE;\n- the expected rule id is present with the expected outcome;\n- a ``VIOLATED`` expectation is in ``triggered_violation_ids``;\n- an ``UNKNOWN`` expectation is NOT falsely recorded as ``VIOLATED``;\n- ``triggered_violation_ids`` is a subset of ``evaluated_rule_ids``.\n\nEvery blacklist case explicitly blacklists the analyzed ticker (AAPL).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom tests.risk_gate._support import (\n    R1,\n    R2,\n    R3,\n    R4,\n    R5,\n    R6,\n    evaluate,\n    make_buy,\n    make_portfolio,\n    make_target,\n    outcomes,\n    violated_ids,\n)\n\n\ndef _case(label, kwargs, rule, outcome, blacklist=None):\n    \"\"\"One invalid fixture descriptor.\n\n    ``rule``/``outcome`` are the expected result for the targeted rule;\n    ``blacklist`` (when set) injects that ticker set into the policy. Every\n    blacklist case MUST include the analyzed ticker (AAPL) so R5 applies.\n    \"\"\"\n    return {\n        \"label\": label,\n        \"kwargs\": kwargs,\n        \"rule\": rule,\n        \"outcome\": outcome,\n        \"blacklist\": blacklist,\n    }\n\n\n# A consistent 1,000,000 book used by the affordability fixture. R2 (0.05 <= 0.10)\n# and R3 (Technology 20% <= 30%) pass; only affordability blocks approval.\n_AFFORDABILITY_PORTFOLIO = make_portfolio(\n    holdings=[\n        {\"ticker\": \"AAPL\", \"market_value\": 20_000.0, \"sector\": \"Technology\"},\n        {\"ticker\": \"MSFT\", \"market_value\": 150_000.0, \"sector\": \"Technology\"},\n        {\"ticker\": \"JPM\", \"market_value\": 300_000.0, \"sector\": \"Financials\"},\n        {\"ticker\": \"XOM\", \"market_value\": 300_000.0, \"sector\": \"Energy\"},\n        {\"ticker\": \"PG\", \"market_value\": 220_000.0, \"sector\": \"Consumer Staples\"},\n    ],\n    cash=10_000.0,\n    portfolio_value=1_000_000.0,\n)\n\n# A consistent book where the analyzed ticker (AAPL) is unheld, used by R3 cases.\ndef _sector_book(tech_value):\n    \"\"\"AAPL unheld; Technology = ``tech_value`` (MSFT); cash funds the 50,000 buy.\"\"\"\n    cash = 60_000.0\n    fin = 1_000_000.0 - (tech_value + cash)\n    return make_portfolio(\n        holdings=[\n            {\"ticker\": \"AAPL\", \"market_value\": 0.0, \"sector\": \"Technology\"},\n            {\"ticker\": \"MSFT\", \"market_value\": tech_value, \"sector\": \"Technology\"},\n            {\"ticker\": \"JPM\", \"market_value\": fin, \"sector\": \"Financials\"},\n        ],\n        cash=cash,\n        portfolio_value=1_000_000.0,\n    )\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Single-rule and input-integrity bases (each case independent)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n# R1: missing stop -> R1 VIOLATED; R4 becomes UNKNOWN (not falsely VIOLATED).\n_R1 = [\n    _case(\"r1_missing_stop\", {\"stop_loss\": None}, R1, \"VIOLATED\"),\n]\n\n# R2: single-name over the 10% cap. VALID_BUY holds AAPL 20,000 of 1,000,000;\n# weights above 0.10 are over the cap (and all are genuine increases).\n_R2 = [\n    _case(f\"r2_weight_{w:.4f}\", {\"target_position\": make_target(w)}, R2, \"VIOLATED\")\n    for w in (0.1001, 0.11, 0.15, 0.25, 0.50)\n]\n\n# R3: projected sector over 30%. AAPL is unheld; target weight 0.05 of a\n# 1,000,000 book = 50,000; Technology = tech_value + projected AAPL.\n_R3 = [\n    _case(f\"r3_tech_{int(tech)}\", {\"portfolio\": _sector_book(tech)}, R3, \"VIOLATED\")\n    for tech in (260_000.0, 280_000.0, 300_000.0)  # projected 31%, 33%, 35%\n]\n\n# R4: reward-to-risk below 1.5 and wrong-side stops/targets.\n_R4 = [\n    _case(f\"r4_stop{int(s)}_target{int(t)}\", {\"stop_loss\": s, \"price_target\": t}, R4, \"VIOLATED\")\n    for s, t in [\n        (90.0, 105.0),    # RR 0.5\n        (90.0, 114.0),    # RR 1.4\n        (100.0, 130.0),   # stop == entry\n        (105.0, 130.0),   # stop above entry\n        (90.0, 100.0),    # target == entry\n        (90.0, 95.0),     # target below entry\n    ]\n]\n\n# R5: blacklist. Each case blacklists the analyzed ticker (AAPL).\n_R5 = [\n    _case(\"r5_blacklist_aapl\", {}, R5, \"VIOLATED\", blacklist=frozenset({\"AAPL\"})),\n    _case(\"r5_blacklist_aapl_and_peer\", {}, R5, \"VIOLATED\",\n          blacklist=frozenset({\"AAPL\", \"MSFT\"})),\n    _case(\"r5_blacklist_multi\", {}, R5, \"VIOLATED\",\n          blacklist=frozenset({\"AAPL\", \"TSLA\", \"NVDA\"})),\n]\n\n# R6: input integrity. These resolve to NEEDS_REVIEW with the referenced rule\n# UNKNOWN; the assertion checks the rule is not falsely VIOLATED.\n_R6 = [\n    _case(\"r6_missing_target\", {\"price_target\": None}, R4, \"UNKNOWN\"),\n    _case(\"r6_missing_weight\", {\"target_position\": None}, R2, \"UNKNOWN\"),\n    _case(\"r6_missing_portfolio\", {\"portfolio\": None}, R3, \"UNKNOWN\"),\n    _case(\"r6_contradictory_dir\", {\"action\": \"Buy\", \"model_rating\": \"Sell\"}, R6, \"UNKNOWN\"),\n    _case(\"r6_entry_nan\", {\"entry_price\": float(\"nan\")}, R6, \"UNKNOWN\"),\n    _case(\"r6_entry_inf\", {\"entry_price\": float(\"inf\")}, R6, \"UNKNOWN\"),\n    _case(\"r6_unknown_sector\", {\"portfolio\": make_portfolio(\n        holdings=[{\"ticker\": \"AAPL\", \"market_value\": 20_000.0, \"sector\": None},\n                  {\"ticker\": \"MSFT\", \"market_value\": 150_000.0, \"sector\": \"Technology\"}],\n        cash=830_000.0, portfolio_value=1_000_000.0)}, R3, \"UNKNOWN\"),\n    _case(\"r6_inconsistent_book\", {\"portfolio\": make_portfolio(\n        holdings=[{\"ticker\": \"AAPL\", \"market_value\": 20_000.0, \"sector\": \"Technology\"},\n                  {\"ticker\": \"MSFT\", \"market_value\": 150_000.0, \"sector\": \"Technology\"}],\n        cash=10_000.0, portfolio_value=1_000_000.0)}, R6, \"UNKNOWN\"),\n    _case(\"r6_stale_valuation\", {\"portfolio\": make_portfolio(\n        holdings=[{\"ticker\": \"AAPL\", \"market_value\": 20_000.0, \"sector\": \"Technology\"},\n                  {\"ticker\": \"MSFT\", \"market_value\": 150_000.0, \"sector\": \"Technology\"}],\n        cash=830_000.0, portfolio_value=1_000_000.0, valuation_date=\"2020-01-01\")},\n        R6, \"UNKNOWN\"),\n    _case(\"r6_affordability\",\n          {\"target_position\": make_target(0.05), \"portfolio\": _AFFORDABILITY_PORTFOLIO},\n          R6, \"UNKNOWN\"),\n]\n\n\ndef _payload_key(case):\n    \"\"\"Distinctness key: the actual input payload plus the policy, not the label.\"\"\"\n    kwargs = case[\"kwargs\"]\n    # Represent the payload canonically; dict values (nested portfolio/target)\n    # are normalised to a stable string so equal payloads dedupe regardless of key\n    # order. NaN/inf are represented distinctly via repr.\n    items = tuple(\n        sorted((k, repr(v)) for k, v in kwargs.items())\n    )\n    blacklist = tuple(sorted(case[\"blacklist\"])) if case[\"blacklist\"] else None\n    return (items, blacklist)\n\n\ndef _build_cases():\n    \"\"\"Assemble single-rule cases and add independent multi-rule cases to reach 100.\n\n    Multi-rule cases are explicit combinations (not a fragile merge of arbitrary\n    dicts): a weight-over-cap case combined with an independent stop/target\n    violation always targets R2 as VIOLATED because the target_position fully\n    specifies the weight and the stop/target fields do not overlap it.\n    \"\"\"\n    cases = list(_R1) + list(_R2) + list(_R3) + list(_R4) + list(_R5) + list(_R6)\n\n    # Independent combinations that add distinct payloads without merge collisions.\n    # (a) over-cap weight + each R4 stop/target case (target_position is R2's own key,\n    #     stop/target are R4's keys -> no overwrite).\n    for i, r2 in enumerate(_R2):\n        for j, r4 in enumerate(_R4):\n            merged = dict(r2[\"kwargs\"])\n            merged.update(r4[\"kwargs\"])\n            cases.append(_case(f\"r2xr4_{i}_{j}\", merged, R2, \"VIOLATED\"))\n    # (b) sector-over + each R4 case (portfolio from R3, stop/target from R4).\n    for i, r3 in enumerate(_R3):\n        for j, r4 in enumerate(_R4):\n            merged = dict(r3[\"kwargs\"])\n            merged.update(r4[\"kwargs\"])\n            cases.append(_case(f\"r3xr4_{i}_{j}\", merged, R3, \"VIOLATED\"))\n    # (c) blacklist + each R4 case (blacklist from R5; AAPL is the analyzed ticker).\n    for i, r5 in enumerate(_R5):\n        for j, r4 in enumerate(_R4):\n            merged = dict(r4[\"kwargs\"])\n            cases.append(_case(f\"r5xr4_{i}_{j}\", merged, R5, \"VIOLATED\",\n                               blacklist=r5[\"blacklist\"]))\n\n    # Deduplicate by actual payload + policy, preserving first occurrence order.\n    seen, unique = set(), []\n    for case in cases:\n        key = _payload_key(case)\n        if key in seen:\n            continue\n        seen.add(key)\n        unique.append(case)\n    return unique\n\n\n_ALL = _build_cases()\nassert len(_ALL) >= 100, f\"only {len(_ALL)} distinct invalid cases generated\"\nCASES = _ALL[:100]\nassert len(CASES) == 100\nassert len({_payload_key(c) for c in CASES}) == 100, \"the 100 fixtures must be distinct\"\nassert any(c[\"rule\"] == R5 for c in CASES), \"blacklist must be in the 100\"\nassert any(c[\"outcome\"] == \"UNKNOWN\" for c in CASES), \"input-integrity must be in the 100\"\nassert {R1, R2, R3, R4, R5}.issubset({c[\"rule\"] for c in CASES})\n\n\ndef _policy(case):\n    if case[\"blacklist\"] is None:\n        return None\n    rg = __import__(\"tradingagents.risk_gate\", fromlist=[\"RiskPolicy\"])\n    return rg.RiskPolicy(blacklist=case[\"blacklist\"])\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    \"case\",\n    CASES,\n    ids=[f\"{c['label']}_{i:03d}\" for i, c in enumerate(CASES)],\n)\ndef test_invalid_fixture_is_never_approved(case):\n    \"\"\"FR-A1/INV-A1: no invalid fixture is APPROVED; expected rule outcome holds.\"\"\"\n    result = evaluate(make_buy(**case[\"kwargs\"]), policy=_policy(case))\n    label = case[\"label\"]\n\n    assert result.verdict != \"APPROVED\", (label, case[\"kwargs\"])\n    assert result.decision_status != \"ACTIONABLE\", (label, case[\"kwargs\"])\n\n    outs = outcomes(result)\n    assert outs.get(case[\"rule\"]) == case[\"outcome\"], (label, outs)\n\n    if case[\"outcome\"] == \"VIOLATED\":\n        assert case[\"rule\"] in violated_ids(result), label\n        assert case[\"rule\"] in result.triggered_violation_ids, label\n    else:  # UNKNOWN must not be falsely recorded as VIOLATED\n        assert case[\"rule\"] not in violated_ids(result), label\n        assert case[\"rule\"] not in result.triggered_violation_ids, label\n\n    assert set(result.triggered_violation_ids) <= set(result.evaluated_rule_ids)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_zero_approvals_across_all_invalid_fixtures():\n    \"\"\"FR-A1: aggregate — 0 of 100 invalid fixtures approved.\"\"\"\n    approvals = [\n        c[\"label\"] for c in CASES\n        if evaluate(make_buy(**c[\"kwargs\"]), policy=_policy(c)).verdict == \"APPROVED\"\n    ]\n    assert approvals == [], f\"invalid fixtures approved: {approvals}\"\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_blacklist_cases_blacklist_the_analyzed_ticker():\n    \"\"\"FR-A1 R5: every blacklist fixture includes the analyzed ticker (AAPL).\"\"\"\n    blacklist_cases = [c for c in CASES if c[\"blacklist\"] is not None]\n    assert blacklist_cases, \"at least one blacklist case must be present\"\n    analyzed = make_buy()[\"ticker\"].upper()\n    for case in blacklist_cases:\n        normalized = {t.upper() for t in case[\"blacklist\"]}\n        assert analyzed in normalized, (case[\"label\"], case[\"blacklist\"])\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_all_rules_and_integrity_are_represented():\n    \"\"\"FR-A1: the 100 cases cover R1-R5 and input-integrity UNKNOWN outcomes.\n\n    Also exercises the engine on a representative case, so this cannot pass\n    while the gate is missing.\n    \"\"\"\n    rules = {c[\"rule\"] for c in CASES}\n    assert {R1, R2, R3, R4, R5}.issubset(rules), rules\n    assert any(c[\"rule\"] == R6 or c[\"outcome\"] == \"UNKNOWN\" for c in CASES)\n    result = evaluate(make_buy(**CASES[0][\"kwargs\"]), policy=_policy(CASES[0]))\n    assert result.verdict in (\"APPROVED\", \"REJECTED\", \"NEEDS_REVIEW\")\n",

never average cost\n     sector: str | None\n \n class PortfolioRiskSnapshot(BaseModel):\n     valuation_date: str          # ISO date; must be consistent with the run's trade_date\n     portfolio_value: float       # total portfolio value used for weight denominators\n     cash: float                  # cash available to fund a cash-funded long\n     holdings: list[Holding]\n     # consistency: cash + Σ holdings.market_value == portfolio_value\n \n class RiskInputs(BaseModel):\n     ticker: str\n     trade_date: str\n     action: str | None           # TraderProposal.action, if structured output produced it\n     entry_price: float | None\n     stop_loss: float | None\n     price_target: float | None   # PortfolioDecision.price_target\n     model_rating: str | None     # PortfolioDecision.rating, verbatim\n     target_position: TargetPosition | None\n     portfolio: PortfolioRiskSnapshot | None\n ```\n \n **Projected exposure (cash-funded long, documented for v1):**\n `projected_stock_value = target_position_weight * portfolio_value`;\n `projected_sector_value = current_sector_value - current_stock_value +\n projected_stock_value`. A genuine BUY increases the position and the purchase\n (`projected_stock_value - current_stock_value`) is affordable from `cash`. Missing\n target sector for an unheld stock, or an inconsistent snapshot, makes the affected\n rule `UNKNOWN` → `NEEDS_REVIEW`, never `APPROVED`.\n \n ### 1.5 Output models\n \n ```python\n class RuleResult(BaseModel):\n     rule_id: str\n     outcome: RuleOutcome\n     detail: str                      # deterministic; no PII/credentials\n     observed: float | None = None\n     threshold: float | None = None\n \n class RiskEvaluation(BaseModel):\n     verdict: RiskVerdict\n     decision_status: DecisionStatus\n     model_rating: str | None\n     evaluated_rule_ids: list[str]        # every rule considered\n     triggered_violation_ids: list[str]   # only VIOLATED rule ids\n     rule_results: list[RuleResult]       # complete per-rule results\n     policy_version: str\n     policy_hash: str\n     input_snapshot: dict                 # minimal, redacted snapshot\n     evaluated_at_utc: str                # ISO8601 UTC\n     latency_ms: float\n \n class RiskAuditRecord(BaseModel):\n     audit_id: str\n     evaluation: RiskEvaluation\n ```\n \n ### 1.6 Engine entry points\n \n ```python\n def evaluate_risk(inputs: RiskInputs, policy: RiskPolicy | None = None) -> RiskEvaluation: ...\n \n class RiskPolicy:\n     version: str          # \"fr-a1-v1\"\n     policy_hash: str      # stable hash of the constants\n     single_name_cap: float = 0.10\n     sector_cap: float = 0.30\n     min_reward_risk: float = 1.5\n     blacklist: frozenset[str] = frozenset()\n ```\n \n `evaluate_risk` is pure and deterministic. Ticker normalization uses\n `tradingagents.dataflows.symbols.normalize_symbol`.\n \n ## 2. Rule semantics and applicability\n \n Precedence for the final verdict: `REJECTED > NEEDS_REVIEW > APPROVED`.\n \n **UNKNOWN is not VIOLATED.** `triggered_violation_ids` lists only rules whose\n outcome is `VIOLATED`; `evaluated_rule_ids` lists every rule considered. When a\n rule cannot be decided for lack of input it is `UNKNOWN` (→ `NEEDS_REVIEW`), not a\n violation. Example: a missing stop-loss makes `R1` `VIOLATED` while `R4` is\n `UNKNOWN` (the ratio cannot be computed).\n \n **Three separate concepts at the boundary:** `model_rating` (the PM's own rating,\n preserved), `risk_verdict` (from the gate), and the *effective public signal*\n (a non-`APPROVED` actionable direction surfaces as the existing `REVIEW`\n sentinel). `final_rating`/`run_rating` keep their baseline meaning — the **model**\n rating — and are not redefined; the gate produces the effective public signal\n separately so blocked recommendations cannot escape as an actionable BUY.\n \n | Rule | Applies when | Violated → | Unknown/inapplicable → |\n |---|---|---|---|\n | R1 stop-loss | long actionable BUY (action Buy) | REJECTED | — |\n | R2 single-name | BUY with a resolvable weight | REJECTED (>0.10) | NEEDS_REVIEW (R2 UNKNOWN: missing weight) |\n | R3 sector | BUY with a resolvable snapshot | REJECTED (>0.30) | NEEDS_REVIEW (R3 UNKNOWN: unknown sector/value) |\n | R4 reward-risk | BUY with entry/stop/target | REJECTED (ratio<1.5 or bad ordering) | NEEDS_REVIEW (R4 UNKNOWN: missing leg) |\n | R5 blacklist | any ticker | REJECTED (on list) | — (list always known) |\n | R6 input integrity | always | — | NEEDS_REVIEW (R6 UNKNOWN: missing/contradictory/inconsistent) |\n \n BUY: all of R1–R5 apply. HOLD: no actionable trade; approved HOLD → `NO_TRADE`\n (R4 `NOT_APPLICABLE` is a pending decision). SELL/short without explicit\n existing-position and trade data → not `APPROVED` (mandatory); exact risk-reducing\n criteria are pending team confirmation. The sector cap applies to the **affected\n sector** of the target stock in v1 (scope pending confirmation).\n \n+**As-implemented rule ownership (no semantic change, just allocation):**\n+- R2 checks the weight cap and the *genuine increase* clause (UNKNOWN when the\n+  buy does not increase the position).\n+- R3 checks projected affected-sector exposure (UNKNOWN when a holding lacks a\n+  sector, or the target sector is unknown).\n+- R6 checks input integrity that spans rules: contradictory/ambiguous direction,\n+  non-finite decision prices, an inconsistent or stale portfolio snapshot, and an\n+  unaffordable cash-funded purchase. In v1, an unsupported short/SELL is recorded\n+  by R6 as UNKNOWN (pending team confirmation), so it cannot be approved.\n+- Decision numeric fields are representable as `inf`/`nan` at the model layer so a\n+  malformed value degrades to UNKNOWN (NEEDS_REVIEW); it can never become a usable\n+  number or an approval.\n+\n ## 3. Requirement traceability\n \n | Requirement | Contract element | Test file |\n |---|---|---|\n | FR-A1 verdict + rule IDs | `evaluate_risk`, `rule_results` | `test_rules.py`, `test_verdict_semantics.py` |\n | FR-A1 5 injected violations 5/5 blocked | R1–R5 fixtures | `test_rule_violations.py` |\n | FR-A1 100 invalid fixtures 0 approvals | fixture generator | `test_100_invalid_fixtures.py` |\n | INV-A1 no approval without stop / over cap | invariants | `test_invariants.py` |\n | NFR-A1 p95 ≤ 2 s, 0 network | pure engine + runtime/structural guard | `test_latency_no_network.py` |\n | NFR-A2 audit completeness | `RiskAuditRecord` | `test_audit_trail.py` |\n | §5.1 verdict affects recommendation | boundary enforcement | `test_decision_boundary.py` |\n | §5.2 NO_TRADE for approved HOLD | `DecisionStatus` | `test_verdict_semantics.py` |\n | §5.3 structured weight/snapshot | `TargetPosition`, `PortfolioRiskSnapshot` | `test_input_contract.py` |\n | §5.4 trade scope | applicability | `test_trade_scope.py` |\n | §5.5 policy version/hash | `RiskPolicy` | `test_policy_versioning.py` |\n | Structured retention (API+CLI) | state keys | `test_integration_retention.py` |\n \n ## 4. Test matrix\n \n All tests are `@pytest.mark.unit`, offline (the repo's `conftest.py` already\n blocks sockets), parameterized deterministically. Files live under `tests/risk_gate/`.\n \n ### 4.1 Rule-level (`test_rules.py`)\n \n - R1: BUY missing stop → REJECTED, id `R1_STOP_LOSS_REQUIRED`.\n - R2: weight 0.12 → REJECTED; weight 0.10 → PASS; weight 0.099 → PASS.\n - R3: sector 0.35 → REJECTED; 0.30 → PASS.\n - R4: long RR 2.0 → PASS; RR 0.5 → REJECTED; short direction-aware.\n - R5: blacklisted ticker → REJECTED; normalization for `aapl`/`AAPL`.\n - Valid BUY (all in bounds) → APPROVED, `R0_ALL_RULES_PASSED` present.\n - Wrong-side stop (long stop ≥ entry) → REJECTED; wrong-side target → REJECTED.\n \n ### 4.2 Exact boundaries (`test_boundaries.py`)\n \n - 10% weight: `0.10` PASS, next representable above → REJECTED. The fixture holds a\n   positive AAPL position, so a target weight of `0.0` (and a target equal to the\n   held value) is **not approved** — a genuine BUY must increase the position.\n - 30% **projected post-trade** sector: `0.30` PASS (inclusive), just over REJECTED.\n - 1.5 RR: exactly `1.5` PASS; `1.4999...` REJECTED.\n \n ### 4.3 Injected violations (`test_rule_violations.py`)\n \n Five individually isolated fixtures, each asserting the expected rule id is\n `VIOLATED` and verdict `REJECTED`, with the *other* rules not violated: missing\n stop (R1; R4 may be UNKNOWN), single-name 12% (R2), projected sector 40% (R3),\n RR 0.5 (R4), blacklist (R5).\n \n ### 4.4 Malformed / missing inputs (`test_input_contract.py`)\n \n - Missing target position/weight → NEEDS_REVIEW, R2 `UNKNOWN`, PENDING_REVIEW.\n - Missing portfolio/sector → NEEDS_REVIEW, R3 `UNKNOWN`.\n - Missing target price → NEEDS_REVIEW, R4 `UNKNOWN`.\n - NaN/inf prices → NEEDS_REVIEW, never ACTIONABLE.\n - Contradictory proposal/decision direction → NEEDS_REVIEW (R6 `UNKNOWN`).\n - Inconsistent snapshot (holdings+cash ≠ portfolio_value), stale valuation date,\n   unaffordable purchase → NEEDS_REVIEW, never ACTIONABLE.\n \n ### 4.5 Verdict semantics (`test_verdict_semantics.py`)\n \n - Precedence REJECTED > NEEDS_REVIEW > APPROVED.\n - All applicable rules collected (no first-fail).\n - UNKNOWN is distinct from VIOLATED; `triggered_violation_ids` lists only VIOLATED.\n - `triggered_violation_ids` ⊆ `evaluated_rule_ids`; both present for clean runs.\n - Approved HOLD → `NO_TRADE`; approved BUY → `ACTIONABLE`; rejected → `BLOCKED`;\n   needs-review → `PENDING_REVIEW`; model rating preserved on reject.\n \n ### 4.6 Trade scope (`test_trade_scope.py`)\n \n Mandatory (hard assertions, not xfail): HOLD never ACTIONABLE; SELL/short without\n explicit position+trade data never APPROVED; ambiguous direction never APPROVED.\n A `test_proposed_*` records the pending SELL-with-data expectation separately.\n \n ### 4.7 Invariants (`test_invariants.py`)\n \n - APPROVED ⇒ stop-loss present for actionable BUY.\n - APPROVED ⇒ weight ≤ 0.10.\n - APPROVED ⇒ decision_status in {ACTIONABLE, NO_TRADE}.\n - Sweep over deterministic grid: no APPROVED violates INV-A1.\n \n ### 4.8 100 invalid fixtures (`test_100_invalid_fixtures.py`)\n \n Simple, independent, reproducible parameterized cases (no fragile dictionary-\n merging cross-products that could overwrite `target_position` or other inputs).\n Exactly 100 **distinct** fixtures are exercised; distinctness is keyed on the\n actual input payload and the policy (blacklist), excluding the case label.\n \n Cases span **all five rules plus input-integrity failures** (R1–R6). Every\n blacklist fixture explicitly blacklists the analyzed ticker (AAPL), so R5 applies.\n Each case declares the rule it targets and the outcome that rule must record:\n \n - `VIOLATED` cases assert the expected rule id is present with `VIOLATED` and is in\n   `triggered_violation_ids`.\n - `UNKNOWN` (input-integrity) cases assert the referenced rule is `UNKNOWN` and is\n   **not** falsely recorded as `VIOLATED`.\n - Aggregate: **0 of 100 APPROVED**, none ACTIONABLE; all of R1–R5 plus an\n   input-integrity `UNKNOWN` outcome are represented; the 100 are distinct.\n - A dedicated test asserts every blacklist fixture includes the analyzed ticker.\n \n The affordability fixture uses a consistent 1,000,000 book (cash 10,000, AAPL\n 20,000, MSFT 150,000, others 820,000 across several non-Technology sectors); target\n weight 0.05 → projected AAPL 50,000 (+30,000 increase) but only 10,000 cash, so R2\n (0.05 ≤ 0.10) and R3 (Technology 20%) pass and affordability is the only blocker,\n yielding `NEEDS_REVIEW` under the `REJECTED > NEEDS_REVIEW > APPROVED` precedence.\n \n ### 4.9 Audit (`test_audit_trail.py`)\n \n - Required *values* verified (policy hash length, UTC timestamp format, latency,\n   snapshot non-empty and value-bearing), not mere key presence.\n - 10 evaluations → 100% audit coverage with identical version/hash.\n - No credentials or raw prompt fields.\n \n ### 4.10 Policy versioning (`test_policy_versioning.py`)\n \n - `version == \"fr-a1-v1\"`; `policy_hash` stable; distinct hash when a threshold\n   changes; version/hash recorded in evaluation.\n \n ### 4.11 Latency / no network (`test_latency_no_network.py`)\n \n - 1000 evaluations; measured **core** p95 ≤ 2000 ms; the measured p50/p95 is\n   reported in the test output. Core latency is distinguished from integration\n   overhead (graph wiring is covered separately).\n - A runtime socket guard (every connect/`getaddrinfo` refuses) is installed for the\n   evaluation loop; a subprocess structural check asserts importing the engine\n   alone pulls in no network/LLM module.\n \n ### 4.12 Integration acceptance (`test_integration_retention.py`, `test_decision_boundary.py`)\n \n **These are NOT approved for the core stage.** They are retained for the later\n integration stage and will require separate review and approval before integration.\n They exercise graph/CLI/checkpoint code and are expected to fail (RED) until that\n stage. `[SAFETY]`/`[PRESERVE]` marked, real graph/CLI behavioral tests (not\n existence checks).\n \n - Programmatic API: **unconditional** assertions for REJECTED and for NEEDS_REVIEW —\n   expected `risk_verdict`, effective public signal `REVIEW`, preserved\n   `model_rating`, and `decision_status` (`BLOCKED`/`PENDING_REVIEW`).\n - CLI stream path: a real `run_analysis` drive with a scripted streamed REJECTED\n   BUY verifies the decision recorded downstream is not an actionable BUY\n   (effective signal `REVIEW`, `decision_status` BLOCKED, `model_rating` kept).\n - Structured objects retained in state without Markdown parsing (`[SAFETY]`).\n - Audit persistence: state log records `risk_verdict` and `policy_version`\n   (`[SAFETY]`).\n - Checkpoint safety: the run signature carries a `risk_gate` **marker**, and a\n   pre-gate checkpoint cannot resume into a gated graph — asserted structurally on\n   the marker list, not by searching a hash for a word (`[SAFETY]`).\n - Existing rendered strings and `run_rating` (model rating) unchanged (`[PRESERVE]`).\n \n ## 5. Expected outcomes before implementation\n \n Because production code is absent, the risk-gate tests import the engine at test\n execution time and fail (RED) with `ModuleNotFoundError: tradingagents.risk_gate`.\n There is **no module-level importorskip and no production stub**. Test files are\n collected before implementation; individual tests fail for real, proving they\n exercise the gate. Collection succeeds; failures are the honest pre-implementation\n state, never counted as passes. The existing regression suite must be unaffected\n (`[PRESERVE]`).\n \n ## 6. Intentional safety changes vs regression\n \n - `[SAFETY]` items intentionally change observable behavior at the decision\n   boundary (non-APPROVED directions become `REVIEW`/blocked). These are not\n   regressions.\n - `[PRESERVE]` items must remain identical; failing ones indicate unintended\n   regression and must not be \"fixed\" by weakening assertions.\n \n ## 7. Pending scope decisions (recorded separately)\n \n Mandatory safety behavior is encoded as hard assertions, not non-strict xfail.\n Genuinely unresolved policy extensions are recorded as `test_proposed_*` or here:\n \n - P1 HOLD applicability of R4 (proposed: `NOT_APPLICABLE`).\n - P2 SELL risk-reducing criteria and required explicit data (mandatory:\n   unsupported SELL never approved).\n - P3 Blacklist source (proposed: injectable policy).\n - P4 FR-A2 boundary: NEEDS_REVIEW blocked from automatic execution.\n - P5 Sector snapshot additive contract details.\n - P6 Sector-cap scope: affected sector (v1 default) vs all sectors.\n \n ## 8.
