def render_report(ticker: str, final_state: dict, settings: dict | None, parts) -> str:
    """The report page: title and rating, what produced the run, contents, sections."""
    md = _markdown()
    rating = run_rating(final_state) if final_state.get("final_trade_decision") else ""
    tone = _TONE.get(rating, "review")
    date = final_state.get("trade_date", "")

    title = f'<span class="ticker">{escape(ticker)}</span>'
    if rating:
        title += f' <span class="rating {tone}">{escape(rating)}</span>'
    details = "".join(
        f'<div class="{"note" if label == "Memory log" else "detail"}">'
        f"<dt>{escape(label)}</dt><dd>{value}</dd></div>"

```text
I have a complete picture. Key architecture insight:

- **Publication points** using `run_rating(final_state)`: `propagate` return signal, `_log_state` (`final_rating` in the state log), `record_decision` → memory rating, `reporting._header` ("- Rating:"), `report_html`, and CLI's `is_review(run_rating(...))` warning. All read `final_rating` (the model rating).
- The cleanest single authoritative boundary that covers graph streaming **and** every consumer is the **Portfolio Manager output boundary**: the PM node itself runs the gate and sets `final_rating` to the effective signal (`REVIEW` when not approved) while preserving the model rating in a separate field. This avoids a second evaluation in a separate node and guarantees no consumer sees an unapproved BUY.

Let me verify one more thing: the offline scripted model's structured-output mapping and whether `PortfolioDecision.price_target`/`TraderProposal` fields are available for building risk inputs, plus how `create_run_state` passes portfolio_context.
```

## 12. Pending team-confirmation decisions

Recorded here and mirrored in the test plan; production must not assume them.

- **D-scope-1 (sector cap scope):** affected sector only (v1 default) vs all sectors.
- **D-scope-2 (SELL/short):** criteria for treating a SELL as risk-reducing with
  explicit existing-position and trade data. Until confirmed, unsupported SELL and
  ambiguous direction are never `APPROVED`; HOLD is never `ACTIONABLE`.
- **D-scope-3 (HOLD rule exemptions):** whether `R4` is `NOT_APPLICABLE` for HOLD.
- **D-scope-4 (blacklist source):** injectable policy (v1 default) vs config; adding
  a config-driven source is FR-A3 scope and is not implemented here.

It\nrevises the Stage 2 description in §11 based on inspection of the actual\npublication and streaming behavior in `46bde74`.\n\n### 13.1 Where a recommendation is published\n\nEvery consumer derives the *effective* public signal from\n`run_rating(final_state)` (which reads `final_rating`):\n\n- `TradingAgentsGraph._run_graph` returns `run_rating(final_state)` as the signal.\n- `_log_state` writes `final_rating` into the state log.\n- `record_decision` writes the memory-log rating tag.\n- `reporting._header` writes `- Rating: …`; `report_html` renders it as a badge.\n- The CLI's post-run notice uses `is_review(run_rating(final_state))`.\n\nGraph streaming (`stream_run`) emits per-node deltas; the Portfolio Manager is the\nlast node and `record_decision` is called only after the stream ends.\n\n### 13.2 Selected boundary: Portfolio Manager output adapter (not a separate node)\n\nThe gate is invoked **once**, inside the Portfolio Manager node, at its output\nboundary, because that node is the single point where both structured objects exist\nand after which *every* publication path consumes `final_rating`. A separate graph\nnode would add a second evaluation surface and require every consumer path to be\naudited again; the PM boundary is the smallest single authoritative decision\nboundary and covers API and CLI-merge identically.\n\nThe adapter:\n- retains `trader_proposal` and `portfolio_decision` in state (structured, no\n  Markdown re-parsing);\n- builds `RiskInputs` from the structured objects plus a caller-supplied\n  `PortfolioRiskSnapshot`/`TargetPosition`;\n- runs `evaluate_risk(policy)` exactly once;\n- preserves the model rating in `model_rating` and writes `final_rating` =\n  effective public signal (`REVIEW` when `risk_verdict != APPROVED`, else the model\n  rating), plus `risk_verdict`, `decision_status`, `risk_evaluation`;\n- persists the audit record into the state log (append-only) without changing the\n  rendered strings consumers already read.\n\nThis is a **revision** of §11's \"adds `node.py`\" — the boundary adapter replaces the\nseparate node for v1, keeping one evaluation.\n\n### 13.3 Input availability (additive, caller-facing)\n\nA new additive config key `risk_portfolio` (a dict matching\n`PortfolioRiskSnapshot` + optional `target_position`) supplies the structured\nsnapshot and target weight. It is passed through `config` to the adapter so both\n`propagate()` and the CLI can supply it. When absent, inputs are incomplete and\nthe gate fails closed (NEEDS_REVIEW), never approving on missing data. The adapter\nnever parses Markdown sizing nor invents market values/prices/sectors. The\nreachable APPROVED path for an in-bounds BUY is exercised offline by supplying the\nsnapshot; this prevents \"everything is NEEDS_REVIEW\" by construction.\n\nBoth structured decisions are required: a missing/invalid Trader `action` **and** a\nmissing/invalid final `PortfolioDecision.rating` each make R6 UNKNOWN (already\nimplemented for the rating; the adapter must also treat a missing action as\nincomplete rather than letting the rating alone define direction silently).\n\n### 13.4 Exact files and interfaces affected (Stage 2 coding, later)\n\n- `tradingagents/agents/state.py` — additive keys: `trader_proposal`,\n  `portfolio_decision`, `model_rating`, `risk_verdict`, `decision_status`,\n  `risk_evaluation`.\n- `tradingagents/agents/trader/trader.py` — return `trader_proposal` alongside the\n  unchanged rendered string.\n- `tradingagents/agents/managers/portfolio_manager.py` — return\n  `portfolio_decision`; invoke the gate adapter; set `final_rating` to the\n  effective signal only through the adapter.\n- `tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py` — pass `risk_portfolio` config to the PM\n  adapter; add a `risk_gate` layout marker to `_run_signature`; persist the audit\n  record in `_log_state`; guard `record_decision` so an audit-persistence failure\n  cannot leave an actionable signal.\n- `tradingagents/risk_gate/adapter.py` (new) — pure wiring from structured objects\n  + snapshot to `RiskInputs`, and the gate call. No graph import in the engine.\n\nNo changes to `rating.py`, `reporting.py`, `report_html.py`, `cli/*`,\n`memory/*`, or `checkpoint.py` semantics are required: they consume `final_rating`,\nwhich the adapter sets to the effective signal, and `model_rating` is preserved for\nevidence.\n\n### 13.5 Safe pre-gate checkpoint behavior\n\nThe `risk_gate` marker in `_run_signature` changes the thread id, so a checkpoint\nsaved before the gate cannot resume into a gated graph; it starts fresh and is\nevaluated. This is the behavior the checkpoint test asserts (actual resume, not a\nhash substring).\n\n### 13.6 Intentional behavior changes vs regressions\n\nIntentional (safety): `final_rating` (and therefore the propagate signal, state\nlog `final_rating`, memory rating tag, report rating header, HTML badge, and CLI\nnotice) becomes `REVIEW` for REJECTED/NEEDS_REVIEW while `model_rating` retains the\nmodel's own value. Rendered decision text is unchanged. Everything else is a\nregression if it changes.\nEOF\necho done"
}

## 8. Staged implementation: core vs integration

Stage 1 (next, on approval) implements **only the independent risk engine** under
`tradingagents/risk_gate/` (pure, no network/file-I/O/LLM) and its **core** tests.
It does **not** modify graph, agent, CLI, reporting, rating, memory, or checkpoint
code. The core-only test command is:

```
pytest tests/risk_gate -q \
  --ignore=tests/risk_gate/test_integration_retention.py \
  --ignore=tests/risk_gate/test_decision_boundary.py
```

Stage 2 (later, separate approval) performs integration and the API/CLI/checkpoint
acceptance tests (`test_integration_retention.py`, `test_decision_boundary.py`).
Those tests are **not approved** for the core stage and must not be claimed as
such. Proposed core-stage production files are enumerated in the ADR.

````

from contextlib import contextmanager
from contextvars import Context, ContextVar, copy_context
from copy import deepcopy

import tradingagents.default_config as default_config

# Use default config but allow it to be overridden
_config: dict | None = None

# The config of the run in progress. A graph binds its own for the length of a
# run, so the data tools it calls read that graph's vendors even when several
# graphs share a process. LangGraph carries the context into tool calls.
_run_config: ContextVar[dict | None] = ContextVar("tradingagents_run_config", default=None)


def initialize_config():
    """Initialize the configuration with default values."""
    global _config
    if _config is None:
        _config = deepcopy(default_config.DEFAULT_CONFIG)


def _merge(base: dict, config: dict) -> dict:
    """Merge ``config`` into ``base``: dict-valued keys one level deep, scalars replaced."""
    for key, value in deepcopy(config).items():
        if isinstance(value, dict) and isinstance(base.get(key), dict):
            base[key].update(value)
        else:
            base[key] = value
    return base


def set_config(config: dict):
    """Update the configuration with custom values.

    Dict-valued keys (e.g. ``data_vendors``) are merged one level deep so a
    partial update like ``{"data_vendors": {"core_stock_apis": "alpha_vantage"}}``
    keeps the other nested keys from the default; scalar keys are replaced.
    """
    initialize_config()

@contextmanager
def run_config(config: dict):
    """Serve ``config``, over the defaults, to every read made inside the block."""
    token = _run_config.set(_merge(deepcopy(default_config.DEFAULT_CONFIG), config))
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        _run_config.reset(token)


def run_config_context(config: dict) -> Context:
    """A context serving ``config``, over the defaults, to every read run in it.

    For a run that yields between steps, where a ``run_config`` block would
    stay open in the caller's context while it holds the results.
    """
    context = copy_context()
    context.run(_run_config.set, _merge(deepcopy(default_config.DEFAULT_CONFIG), config))
    return context


def get_config() -> dict:
    """Get the configuration of the run in progress, else the process-wide one."""
    scoped = _run_config.get()
    if scoped is not None:
        return deepcopy(scoped)
    if _config is None:
        initialize_config()
    return deepcopy(_config)


initialize_config()

def test_a_streamed_run_reads_its_own_graph_config(tmp_path, monkeypatch, offline):
    """The CLI streams the run; a process-wide config set elsewhere must not reach
    its tools, and the graph's config must not reach the caller between steps."""
    from tradingagents.dataflows.config import get_config, set_config

    graph = _graph(tmp_path, monkeypatch, ScriptedModel(), output_language="French")
    set_config({"output_language": "German"})
    seen = []
    monkeypatch.setitem(router.VENDOR_METHODS["get_stock_data"], "yfinance",
                        lambda *a, **k: seen.append(get_config()["output_language"]) or "prices")

    between = [get_config()["output_language"]
               for _ in graph.stream_run(graph.create_run_state("NVDA", TRADE_DATE), **graph.propagator.get_graph_args())]

    assert seen and set(seen) == {"French"}
    assert set(between) == {"German"}


class LoopingModel(ScriptedModel):
    """Calls a tool on every turn it is offered one (#1420)."""

    tool_turns: list = Field(default_factory=list)    # shared across bound copies
    last_turns: list = Field(default_factory=list)    # histories of the turns offered no tools

    def _generate(self, messages, stop=None, run_manager=None, **kwargs) -> ChatResult:
        if not self.tools:
            self.last_turns.append(messages)
            return super()._generate(messages, stop, run_manager, **kwargs)
        self.tool_turns.append(1)
        tool = self.tools[0]
        call = {"name": tool.name, "id": f"call_{len(self.tool_turns)}",
                "args": {k: v for k, v in ARGS.items()
                         if k in tool.tool_call_schema.model_json_schema()["properties"]}}
        return ChatResult(generations=[ChatGeneration(message=AIMessage(content="", tool_calls=[call]))])


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_an_analyst_that_keeps_calling_tools_writes_its_report_at_the_limit(tmp_path, monkeypatch, offline):
    """A model that does not stop calling tools must not end the run (#1420)."""
    model = LoopingModel(structured=True)
    graph = _graph(tmp_path, monkeypatch, model, max_tool_rounds=3)

    final_state, rating = graph.propagate("NVDA", TRADE_DATE)

    assert len(model.tool_turns) == 3 * 3   # three tool-using analysts, three rounds each
    for key in ("market_report", "news_report", "fundamentals_report"):
        assert final_state[key] == TEXT
    assert rating == "Overweight"


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_the_last_turn_is_offered_no_tools_and_reads_its_tool_results_as_text(tmp_path, monkeypatch, offline):
    """Offered tools, a model may call one whatever it is told; a history holding
    tool calls may be refused by a provider when no tools are bound."""
    model = LoopingModel(structured=True)
    graph = _graph(tmp_path, monkeypatch, model, max_tool_rounds=2)

    graph.propagate("NVDA", TRADE_DATE)

    wrap_ups = [h for h in model.last_turns if isinstance(h[-1], HumanMessage) and "tool round" in h[-1].content]
    assert len(wrap_ups) == 3
    for history in wrap_ups:
        assert not any(isinstance(m, ToolMessage) or getattr(m, "tool_calls", None) for m in history)
        assert any("returned]" in str(m.content) for m in history)
        assert "tool rounds are spent" in history[0].content   # the system prompt lists no tools


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_a_tool_limit_the_recursion_limit_cannot_hold_is_refused(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="max_tool_rounds"):
        _graph(tmp_path, monkeypatch, ScriptedModel(), max_tool_rounds=60, max_recur_limit=100)


class TimedModel(ScriptedModel):
    """ScriptedModel that records each call's graph step, prompt and timing."""

    seen: list = Field(default_factory=list)    # shared across bound copies

    def _generate(self, messages, stop=None, run_manager=None, **kwargs) -> ChatResult:
        step = (run_manager.metadata or {}).get("langgraph_node") if run_manager else None
        started = time.monotonic()
        if step in {"Market Analyst", "agent"} or step == "Memory Log":
            time.sleep(0.2)                     # long enough to see what overlaps
        result = super()._generate(messages, stop, run_manager, **kwargs)
        prompt = "\n".join(str(m.content) for m in messages)
        self.seen.append((step, prompt, started, time.monotonic()))
        return result


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_past_decisions_settle_alongside_the_analysts(tmp_path, monkeypatch, offline):
    from tradingagents.memory import settlement

    model = TimedModel()
    graph = _graph(tmp_path, monkeypatch, model)
    graph.memory_log.store_decision("NVDA", "2025-12-31", "Rating: Buy\n\nBuy NVDA.")
    closes = pd.Series([100.0 + i for i in range(10)], index=pd.bdate_range("2026-01-02", periods=10))
    monkeypatch.setattr(settlement, "get_closes", lambda *a, **k: closes)

    graph.propagate("NVDA", TRADE_DATE)

    reflections = [c for c in model.seen if c[0] == "Memory Log"]
    assert len(reflections) == 1                # settled once, inside the run
    analyst_turns = [c for c in model.seen if c[0] == "agent"]
    assert reflections[0][2] < max(c[3] for c in analyst_turns), "settled before the analysts, not alongside"
    settled = next(e for e in graph.memory_log.load_entries() if e["date"] == "2025-12-31")
    assert not settled["pending"]
    lessons = graph.memory_log.get_past_context("NVDA", as_of=TRADE_DATE)
    assert lessons
    pm_prompt = next(c[1] for c in model.seen if c[0] == "Portfolio Manager")
    assert lessons in pm_prompt


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_a_settlement_failure_is_noted_and_the_run_goes_on(tmp_path, monkeypatch, offline):
    """The analysts have spent their tokens by the time the join waits on settlement."""
    from tradingagents.reporting import write_report_tree

    graph = _graph(tmp_path, monkeypatch, ScriptedModel(structured=True))

    def locked():
        raise OSError("memory log is locked")

    monkeypatch.setattr(graph, "settle_all_pending", locked)
    final_state, rating = graph.propagate("NVDA", TRADE_DATE)

    assert rating == "Overweight"
    assert "could not be settled" in final_state["memory_note"]
    report = write_report_tree(final_state, "NVDA", tmp_path / "report").read_text()
    assert "Memory log: Past decisions could not be settled" in report

@pytest.mark.unit
def test_the_memory_step_reads_lessons_as_of_the_trade_date_and_settles_once(tmp_path, monkeypatch, offline):
    """A past-dated run reads only lessons known by its date (#1251); a resumed run
    that re-runs the step settles nothing twice."""
    from tradingagents.memory import settlement

    graph = _graph(tmp_path, monkeypatch, ScriptedModel(structured=True))
    graph.memory_log.store_decision("NVDA", "2025-12-31", "Rating: Buy\n\nBuy NVDA.")
    closes = pd.Series([100.0 + i for i in range(10)], index=pd.bdate_range("2026-01-02", periods=10))
    monkeypatch.setattr(settlement, "get_closes", lambda *a, **k: closes)
    asked = []
    real = graph.memory_log.get_past_context
    monkeypatch.setattr(graph.memory_log, "get_past_context",
                        lambda ticker, as_of=None, **k: asked.append(as_of) or real(ticker, as_of=as_of, **k))
    state = {"company_of_interest": "NVDA", "trade_date": "2026-01-20"}

    graph._memory_step(state)
    log_after_first = (tmp_path / "log.md").read_text()
    graph._memory_step(state)

    assert asked == ["2026-01-20", "2026-01-20"]
    assert (tmp_path / "log.md").read_text() == log_after_first

```text
For the audit-persistence-failure test: the point is that a persistence failure must not leave an actionable signal. Testing via `pytest.raises(OSError)` already shows the run fails. But to be meaningful it should assert that after the failure no actionable BUY was recorded/published. Since `_log_state` runs inside `record_decision` before memory store, a raise prevents completion. That's acceptable but let me make it also assert `propagate` doesn't return an actionable signal (it raises). I'll leave as-is since it does raise — but add an explicit guard that the run did not return an actionable signal.

Actually the current form is fine and meaningful. Let me leave (2). For (3) `test_existing_full_run_still_reaches_a_decision` is a `[PRESERVE]` check that legitimately passes on baseline — that's expected, not a false safety pass. I'll keep it.

Now run the integration tests again to confirm the tightened counts.

Stage 2 integration preparation is complete. Tests and FR-A1 docs only; no production code changed.

# FR-A1 Stage 2 — Integration Preparation Report

## 1. Selected integration architecture
**Portfolio Manager output-boundary adapter** (single authoritative evaluation), not a separate graph node. Rationale (from inspecting actual publication/streaming):
- Every consumer derives the effective signal from `run_rating(final_state)` → `final_rating`: the `propagate` return signal, `_log_state` (`final_rating`), `record_decision` → memory rating tag, `reporting._header`, `report_html`, and the CLI `is_review(run_rating(...))` notice.
- The PM node is the last graph node and the only point where both structured objects exist; `record_decision` runs only after the stream ends.
- A separate node would add a second evaluation surface and require auditing every consumer again. The PM boundary covers API and CLI-merge identically with one evaluation. This is a documented revision of ADR §11's earlier "add `node.py`".

## 2. Input availability (additive, caller-facing)
New additive config key `risk_portfolio` = `{ snapshot: PortfolioRiskSnapshot, target_position: {target_weight, sector} }`, passed to the adapter via `get_config()`. Absent → incomplete inputs → **fail closed (NEEDS_REVIEW)**. Present and in-bounds → **APPROVED** (the reachable path is exercised offline; the suite does not degenerate into all-REVIEW). No Markdown sizing parsing, no invented values/sectors. Both structured decisions are required; an invalid final rating already yields R6 UNKNOWN, and the adapter must treat a missing/invalid Trader action as incomplete too.

## 3. Revised integration tests (real graph, real engine — verdict not mocked)
- `test_decision_boundary.py` (5 tests): A) valid BUY+complete snapshot → APPROVED/ACTIONABLE with signal = model rating; A) missing stop → REJECTED + `REVIEW`; A) missing snapshot → NEEDS_REVIEW + `REVIEW`; B) real `run_analysis` merge → exact `REVIEW` (asserts `run_rating == RATING_REVIEW`, not "REVIEW or BLOCKED"); C) streamed steps show no unapproved actionable BUY before evaluation. Model rating preserved in `model_rating`.
- `test_integration_retention.py` (18 tests): structured retention, free-text fallback cannot bypass, validation→non-actionable+audit; audit fields (rule ids/outcomes, snapshot, verdict, policy v/hash, UTC), numeric exposure inputs, no credentials, all three verdicts audited, persistence-failure cannot leave actionable signal; model evidence vs signal, blocked BUY not authorized in report header/memory, rendered strings preserved; real checkpoint resume re-evaluates; integration overhead measured separately + zero extra network.

## 4. Course compliance — docs updated
- `docs/architecture/adr/adr-fr-a1-risk-gate.md` §13 (new): selected architecture + rationale, publication points, input contract, exact affected files/interfaces, checkpoint behavior, intentional changes vs regressions, and the §11 revision.
- `docs/req/fr-a1-test-plan.md` §9 (new): proposed adapter interface, full integration test matrix, pre-integration expectations, requirement→integration-test traceability. Prior decisions preserved.

## 5. Results (actual, exit codes)
| Command | Exit | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `ruff check tradingagents/risk_gate tests/risk_gate` | **0** | All checks passed |
| `pytest tests/risk_gate --collect-only -q` | **0** | **219 collected** |
| integration tests (2 files) | **1** | **21 failed, 2 passed** — expected RED (adapter/state keys absent) |
| core (excl. 2 integration files) | **0** | **195 passed, 1 xpassed** (unchanged) |
| `pytest -q --ignore=tests/risk_gate` | **0** | **1412 passed, 1 skipped** |

The 2 passing integration tests: `test_existing_full_run_still_reaches_a_decision` (intentional `[PRESERVE]` baseline check) and `test_audit_persistence_failure_cannot_leave_actionable_signal` (the run correctly raises before completing) — neither hides missing integration.

## 6. Exact proposed production file scope (Stage 2 coding, later)
- `tradingagents/risk_gate/adapter.py` (new): `build_inputs(...)`, `apply_gate(...)` — reads structured objects + `risk_portfolio`, invokes `evaluate_risk` once.
- `tradingagents/agents/state.py`: additive keys `trader_proposal`, `portfolio_decision`, `model_rating`, `risk_verdict`, `decision_status`, `risk_evaluation`.
- `tradingagents/agents/trader/trader.py`: return `trader_proposal` alongside unchanged string.
- `tradingagents/agents/managers/portfolio_manager.py`: return `portfolio_decision`; call adapter; set `final_rating` = effective signal via adapter.
- `tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py`: pass `risk_portfolio` to config; add `risk_gate` layout marker to `_run_signature`; persist audit in `_log_state`; guard so an audit-persistence failure cannot leave an actionable signal.
- No changes to `rating.py`, `reporting.py`, `report_html.py`, `cli/*`, `memory/*`, `checkpoint.py` semantics.

## 7. Implementation plan (on approval)
1. Add adapter (pure wiring) + unit-covered via existing core. 2. Extend state keys. 3. Trader/PM return structured objects; PM calls adapter once. 4. `trading_graph`: config passthrough, checkpoint marker, audit persistence + failure guard. 5. Turn integration tests green; re-run core (195) and regression (1412) to prove no weakening.

Invariants preserved: single evaluation; model rating preserved separately; effective signal `REVIEW` for non-approved; fail-closed on missing inputs; zero network/LLM in core; 195 core tests unweakened.

STOP — awaiting human approval before integration coding.

Versioned policy and hash; injectable blacklist; audit fields; core purity;\n    persistence at integration layer.\n 7. Consequences\n \n Positive:\n \n - Deterministic, offline-testable safety gate with first-class audit.\n - Clear separation of model rating from risk judgment and actionability.\n - Fail-closed on missing evidence; no silent weakening of INV-A1.\n \n Negative / costs:\n \n - Requires retaining structured objects in state (additive; source files must add\n   state keys and return the Pydantic objects alongside unchanged strings).\n - Requires a structured portfolio risk snapshot contract (additive input surface).\n - Bumping the graph layout marker in `_run_signature` invalidates older checkpoints\n   (they restart fresh) — intentional and safer.\n - Integration must cover both entry paths to avoid divergence.\n \n Neutral:\n \n - Rendered Markdown, memory log, and existing `final_rating`/`run_rating`\n   semantics remain the **model** rating; the gate adds adjacent fields. The\n   *effective public signal* is derived separately from `risk_verdict`, so blocked\n   recommendations surface as `REVIEW` without redefining `run_rating` itself.\n \n ## 9. Compliance\n \n - This is new implementation work; the inherited TradingAgents baseline is\n   explicitly not counted as the team's contribution beyond the integration points\n   documented above.\n - Architecture decision and verification evidence are recorded before production\n   implementation, per the course's safety-critical process.\n \n ## 10. Reopening conditions\n \n Reopen this ADR if any of the following are established by test evidence:\n \n - Deterministic projected sector exposure cannot be computed from available\n   structured data offline, and the team declines the additive portfolio snapshot.\n - The enforcement boundary proves unable to cover both API and CLI without a\n   network or LLM dependency.\n - Team confirmation changes HOLD/SELL applicability in a way that alters rule sets.\n - Team confirmation changes the sector-cap scope (affected sector vs all sectors).\n - Any change would weaken INV-A1 or an approved requirement.\n \n ## 11. Staged rollout: core first, integration later\n \n To keep the safety-critical core reviewable and isolated, implementation is split.\n \n ### Stage 1 — independent risk engine (the only stage approved next)\n \n Writes **only** new files under `tradingagents/risk_gate/` and their core tests.\n Does **not** modify graph, agent, CLI, reporting, rating, memory, or checkpoint\n code. Proposed production files:\n \n - `tradingagents/risk_gate/__init__.py` (public exports)\n - `tradingagents/risk_gate/models.py` (enums, rule result, evaluation, audit, inputs)\n - `tradingagents/risk_gate/policy.py` (versioned `fr-a1-v1` policy + stable hash)\n - `tradingagents/risk_gate/sizing.py` (projected-weight derivation/validation)\n - `tradingagents/risk_gate/portfolio_snapshot.py` (consistency + projected exposure)\n - `tradingagents/risk_gate/engine.py` (pure `evaluate_risk` implementing R1–R6)\n \n Structural constraints for the core (verified by tests, not prose only):\n \n - No network, no file I/O, no LLM, no LangGraph import in the core modules.\n - Deterministic, pure: same inputs → same evaluation (timestamps/latency aside).\n - `triggered_violation_ids` ⊂ `evaluated_rule_ids`; only `VIOLATED` in the former.\n - Precedence `REJECTED > NEEDS_REVIEW > APPROVED`; no `APPROVED` for any\n   non-increasive, unaffordable, inconsistent, or over-cap decision.\n - Malformed numeric inputs (`NaN`/`inf`) cannot validate into an approved result.\n - Every evaluation yields complete per-rule results and an audit record.\n \n Core-only verification command:\n \n ```\n pytest tests/risk_gate -q \\\n   --ignore=tests/risk_gate/test_integration_retention.py \\\n   --ignore=tests/risk_gate/test_decision_boundary.py\n ```\n \n ### Stage 2 — integration (separate review and approval)\n \n Adds `tradingagents/risk_gate/node.py` and edits `state.py`, `trader.py`,\n `portfolio_manager.py`, `setup.py`, and `trading_graph.py` (state keys, structured\n retention, checkpoint marker, state-log fields). Stage 2 integration architecture (revised decision)\n \n This section records the integration decision **before** integration coding. It\n revises the Stage 2 description in §11 based on inspection of the actual\n publication and streaming behavior in `46bde74`.\n \n ### 13.1 Where a recommendation is published\n \n Every consumer derives the *effective* public signal from\n `run_rating(final_state)` (which reads `final_rating`):\n \n - `TradingAgentsGraph._run_graph` returns `run_rating(final_state)` as the signal.\n - `_log_state` writes `final_rating` into the state log.\n - `record_decision` writes the memory-log rating tag.\n - `reporting._header` writes `- Rating: …`; `report_html` renders it as a badge.\n - The CLI's post-run notice uses `is_review(run_rating(final_state))`.\n \n Graph streaming (`stream_run`) emits per-node deltas; the Portfolio Manager is the\n last node and `record_decision` is called only after the stream ends.\n \n ### 13.2 Selected boundary: Portfolio Manager output adapter (not a separate node)\n \n The gate is invoked **once**, inside the Portfolio Manager node, at its output\n boundary, because that node is the single point where both structured objects exist\n and after which *every* publication path consumes `final_rating`. A separate graph\n node would add a second evaluation surface and require every consumer path to be\n audited again; the PM boundary is the smallest single authoritative decision\n boundary and covers API and CLI-merge identically.\n \n The adapter:\n - retains `trader_proposal` and `portfolio_decision` in state (structured, no\n   Markdown re-parsing);\n - builds `RiskInputs` from the structured objects plus a caller-supplied\n   `PortfolioRiskSnapshot`/`TargetPosition`;\n - runs `evaluate_risk(policy)` exactly once;\n - preserves the model rating in `model_rating` and writes `final_rating` =\n   effective public signal (`REVIEW` when `risk_verdict != APPROVED`, else the model\n   rating), plus `risk_verdict`, `decision_status`, `risk_evaluation`;\n - persists the audit record into the state log (append-only) without changing the\n   rendered strings consumers already read.\n \n This is a **revision** of §11's \"adds `node.py`\" — the boundary adapter replaces the\n separate node for v1, keeping one evaluation.\n \n ### 13.3 Input availability (additive, caller-facing)\n \n A new additive config key `risk_portfolio` (a dict matching\n `PortfolioRiskSnapshot` + optional `target_position`) supplies the structured\n snapshot and target weight. It is passed through `config` to the adapter so both\n `propagate()` and the CLI can supply it. When absent, inputs are incomplete and\n the gate fails closed (NEEDS_REVIEW), never approving on missing data. The adapter\n never parses Markdown sizing nor invents market values/prices/sectors. The\n reachable APPROVED path for an in-bounds BUY is exercised offline by supplying the\n snapshot; this prevents \"everything is NEEDS_REVIEW\" by construction.\n \n Both structured decisions are required: a missing/invalid Trader `action` **and** a\n missing/invalid final `PortfolioDecision.rating` each make R6 UNKNOWN (already\n implemented for the rating; the adapter must also treat a missing action as\n incomplete rather than letting the rating alone define direction silently).\n \n ### 13.4 Exact files and interfaces affected (Stage 2 coding, later)\n \n - `tradingagents/agents/state.py` — additive keys: `trader_proposal`,\n   `portfolio_decision`, `model_rating`, `risk_verdict`, `decision_status`,\n   `risk_evaluation`.\n - `tradingagents/agents/trader/trader.py` — return `trader_proposal` alongside the\n   unchanged rendered string.\n - `tradingagents/agents/managers/portfolio_manager.py` — return\n   `portfolio_decision`; invoke the gate adapter; set `final_rating` to the\n   effective signal only through the adapter.\n - `tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py` — pass `risk_portfolio` config to the PM\n   adapter; add a `risk_gate` layout marker to `_run_signature`; persist the audit\n   record in `_log_state`; guard `record_decision` so an audit-persistence failure\n   cannot leave an actionable signal.\n - `tradingagents/risk_gate/adapter.py` (new) — pure wiring from structured objects\n   + snapshot to `RiskInputs`, and the gate call. No graph import in the engine.\n \n No changes to `rating.py`, `reporting.py`, `report_html.py`, `cli/*`,\n `memory/*`, or `checkpoint.py` semantics are required: they consume `final_rating`,\n which the adapter sets to the effective signal, and `model_rating` is preserved for\n evidence.\n \n ### 13.5 Safe pre-gate checkpoint behavior\n \n The `risk_gate` marker in `_run_signature` changes the thread id, so a checkpoint\n saved before the gate cannot resume into a gated graph; it starts fresh and is\n evaluated. This is the behavior the checkpoint test asserts (actual resume, not a\n hash substring).\n \n ### 13.6 Intentional behavior changes vs regressions\n \n Intentional (safety): `final_rating` (and therefore the propagate signal, state\n log `final_rating`, memory rating tag, report rating header, HTML badge, and CLI\n notice) becomes `REVIEW` for REJECTED/NEEDS_REVIEW while `model_rating` retains the\n model's own value. Rendered decision text is unchanged. Everything else is a\n regression if it changes.\n+\n+## 14. Stage 2 revision: audit-before-publish (from final test review)\n+\n+The output-boundary adapter (§13.2) computes the verdict before the PM node returns,\n+so no consumer can see an actionable BUY that was not evaluated. The final review\n+identified a narrower gap: **on-disk audit durability relative to publication**.\n+\n+### 14.1 Decision\n+\n+The gate must establish the durable audit **before** an actionable (`APPROVED`)\n+signal is released. Two facts constrain this:\n+\n+- The state log is written by `record_decision` *after* the stream ends; the PM\n+  node return (and any streamed `final_rating`) precedes it.\n+- A streamed `final_rating == \"Buy\"` could therefore be observed before the audit\n+  is on disk if persistence happened only in `record_decision`.\n+\n+To guarantee safety without adding a second evaluation:\n+\n+1. The adapter computes the verdict (once) and, for `APPROVED` only, **persists the\n+   audit record durably before returning** the state update that sets\n+   `final_rating` to an actionable rating. It is\n written before production implementation so the tests can be reviewed. Tests\n reference the requirement/invariant they enforce. Intentional safety-related\n behavior changes are marked `[SAFETY]`; everything else must remain an existing\n behavior (`[PRESERVE]`).\n \n ## 1. Proposed interface (contract under review)\n \n The tests are written against this interface. It is expected to match the\n eventual implementation; production code is not written yet.\n \n ### 1.1 Package `tradingagents.risk_gate`\n \n Modules (proposed): `models.py`, `policy.py`, `engine.py`, `sizing.py`,\n `portfolio_snapshot.py`, `node.py` (integration). The core engine modules have no\n network, no file I/O, no LLM imports.\n \n ### 1.2 Enumerations\n \n ```python\n class RiskVerdict(StrEnum):\n     APPROVED = \"APPROVED\"\n     REJECTED = \"REJECTED\"\n     NEEDS_REVIEW = \"NEEDS_REVIEW\"\n \n class DecisionStatus(StrEnum):\n     ACTIONABLE = \"ACTIONABLE\"\n     BLOCKED = \"BLOCKED\"\n     PENDING_REVIEW = \"PENDING_REVIEW\"\n     NO_TRADE = \"NO_TRADE\"\n \n class RuleOutcome(StrEnum):\n     PASS = \"PASS\"\n     VIOLATED = \"VIOLATED\"\n     NOT_APPLICABLE = \"NOT_APPLICABLE\"\n     UNKNOWN = \"UNKNOWN\"\n ```\n \n ### 1.3 Rule identifiers\n \n | ID | Meaning |\n |---|---|\n | `R1_STOP_LOSS_REQUIRED` | Long actionable BUY must carry a stop-loss |\n | `R2_SINGLE_NAME_CAP` | Projected single-name weight ≤ 10% (0.10) |\n | `R3_SECTOR_CONCENTRATION` | Projected sector exposure ≤ 30% (0.30) |\n | `R4_REWARD_RISK` | Direction-aware reward-to-risk ≥ 1.5 and ordering stop<entry<target |\n | `R5_BLACKLIST` | Ticker not on the deterministic blacklist |\n | `R6_INPUT_INTEGRITY` | Structured inputs present, consistent, unambiguous |\n | `R0_ALL_RULES_PASSED` | Positive marker so every verdict carries a rule ID |\n \n `R0` is a synthetic \"pass\" entry: every evaluation carries at least one rule ID,\n satisfying \"100% of verdicts carry a rule identifier\" (`requirements.yaml:28`),\n including clean approvals.\n \n ### 1.4 Input models\n \n ```python\n class TargetPosition(BaseModel):\n     target_position_weight: float | None   # projected post-trade single-name weight, 0..1\n     sector: str | None = None               # target stock's sector, required when not held\n \n class Holding(BaseModel):\n     ticker: str\n     market_value: float          # current market value; never average cost\n     sector: str | None\n \n class PortfolioRiskSnapshot(BaseModel):\n     valuation_date: str          # ISO date; must be consistent with the run's trade_date\n     portfolio_value: float       # total portfolio value used for weight denominators\n     cash: float                  # cash available to fund a cash-funded long\n     holdings: list[Holding]\n     # consistency: cash + Σ holdings.market_value == portfolio_value\n \n class RiskInputs(BaseModel):\n     ticker: str\n     trade_date: str\n     action: str | None           # TraderProposal.action, if structured output produced it\n     entry_price: float | None\n     stop_loss: float | None\n     price_target: float | None   # PortfolioDecision.price_target\n     model_rating: str | None     # PortfolioDecision.rating, verbatim\n     target_position: TargetPosition | None\n     portfolio: PortfolioRiskSnapshot | None\n ```\n \n **Projected exposure (cash-funded long, documented for v1):**\n `projected_stock_value = target_position_weight * portfolio_value`;\n `projected_sector_value = current_sector_value - current_stock_value +\n projected_stock_value`. A genuine BUY increases the position and the purchase\n (`projected_stock_value - current_stock_value`) is affordable from `cash`. Missing\n target sector for an unheld stock, or an inconsistent snapshot, makes the affected\n rule `UNKNOWN` → `NEEDS_REVIEW`, never `APPROVED`.\n \n ### 1.5 Output models\n \n ```python\n class RuleResult(BaseModel):\n     rule_id: str\n     outcome: RuleOutcome\n     detail: str                      # deterministic; no PII/credentials\n     observed: float | None = None\n     threshold: float | None = None\n \n class RiskEvaluation(BaseModel):\n     verdict: RiskVerdict\n     decision_status: DecisionStatus\n     model_rating: str | None\n     evaluated_rule_ids: list[str]        # every rule considered\n     triggered_violation_ids: list[str]   # only VIOLATED rule ids\n     rule_results: list[RuleResult]       # complete per-rule results\n     policy_version: str\n     policy_hash: str\n     input_snapshot: dict                 # minimal, redacted snapshot\n     evaluated_at_utc: str                # ISO8601 UTC\n     latency_ms: float\n \n class RiskAuditRecord(BaseModel):\n     audit_id: str\n     evaluation: RiskEvaluation\n ```\n \n ### 1.6 Engine entry points\n \n ```python\n def evaluate_risk(inputs: RiskInputs, policy: RiskPolicy | None = None) -> RiskEvaluation: ...\n \n class RiskPolicy:\n     version: str          # \"fr-a1-v1\"\n     policy_hash: str      # stable hash of the constants\n     single_name_cap: float = 0.10\n     sector_cap: float = 0.30\n     min_reward_risk: float = 1.5\n     blacklist: frozenset[str] = frozenset()\n ```\n \n `evaluate_risk` is pure and deterministic. Ticker normalization uses\n `tradingagents.dataflows.symbols.normalize_symbol`.\n \n ## 2. Rule semantics and applicability\n \n Precedence for the final verdict: `REJECTED > NEEDS_REVIEW > APPROVED`.\n \n **UNKNOWN is not VIOLATED.** `triggered_violation_ids` lists only rules whose\n outcome is `VIOLATED`; `evaluated_rule_ids` lists every rule considered. When a\n rule cannot be decided for lack of input it is `UNKNOWN` (→ `NEEDS_REVIEW`), not a\n violation. Example: a missing stop-loss makes `R1` `VIOLATED` while `R4` is\n `UNKNOWN` (the ratio cannot be computed).\n \n **Three separate concepts at the boundary:** `model_rating` (the PM's own rating,\n preserved), `risk_verdict` (from the gate), and the *effective public signal*\n (a non-`APPROVED` actionable direction surfaces as the existing `REVIEW`\n sentinel). `final_rating`/`run_rating` keep their baseline meaning — the **model**\n rating — and are not redefined; the gate produces the effective public signal\n separately so blocked recommendations cannot escape as an actionable BUY.\n \n | Rule | Applies when | Violated → | Unknown/inapplicable → |\n |---|---|---|---|\n | R1 stop-loss | long actionable BUY (action Buy) | REJECTED | — |\n | R2 single-name | BUY with a resolvable weight | REJECTED (>0.10) | NEEDS_REVIEW (R2 UNKNOWN: missing weight) |\n | R3 sector | BUY with a resolvable snapshot | REJECTED (>0.30) | NEEDS_REVIEW (R3 UNKNOWN: unknown sector/value) |\n | R4 reward-risk | BUY with entry/stop/target | REJECTED (ratio<1.5 or bad ordering) | NEEDS_REVIEW (R4 UNKNOWN: missing leg) |\n | R5 blacklist | any ticker | REJECTED (on list) | — (list always known) |\n | R6 input integrity | always | — | NEEDS_REVIEW (R6 UNKNOWN: missing/contradictory/inconsistent) |\n \n BUY: all of R1–R5 apply. HOLD: no actionable trade; approved HOLD → `NO_TRADE`\n (R4 `NOT_APPLICABLE` is a pending decision). SELL/short without explicit\n existing-position and trade data → not `APPROVED` (mandatory); exact risk-reducing\n criteria are pending team confirmation. The sector cap applies to the **affected\n sector** of the target stock in v1 (scope pending confirmation).\n \n **As-implemented rule ownership (no semantic change, just allocation):**\n - R2 checks the weight cap and the *genuine increase* clause (UNKNOWN when the\n   buy does not increase the position).\n - R3 checks projected affected-sector exposure (UNKNOWN when a holding lacks a\n   sector, or the target sector is unknown).\n - R6 checks input integrity that spans rules: contradictory/ambiguous direction,\n   non-finite decision prices, an inconsistent or stale portfolio snapshot, and an\n   unaffordable cash-funded purchase. In v1, an unsupported short/SELL is recorded\n   by R6 as UNKNOWN (pending team confirmation), so it cannot be approved.\n - Decision numeric fields are representable as `inf`/`nan` at the model layer so a\n   malformed value degrades to UNKNOWN (NEEDS_REVIEW); it can never become a usable\n   number or an approval.\n \n ## 3. Requirement traceability\n \n | Requirement | Contract element | Test file |\n |---|---|---|\n | FR-A1 verdict + rule IDs | `evaluate_risk`, `rule_results` | `test_rules.py`, `test_verdict_semantics.py` |\n | FR-A1 5 injected violations 5/5 blocked | R1–R5 fixtures | `test_rule_violations.py` |\n | FR-A1 100 invalid fixtures 0 approvals | fixture generator | `test_100_invalid_fixtures.py` |\n | INV-A1 no approval without stop / over cap | invariants | `test_invariants.py` |\n | NFR-A1 p95 ≤ 2 s, 0 network | pure engine + runtime/structural guard | `test_latency_no_network.py` |\n | NFR-A2 audit completeness | `RiskAuditRecord` | `test_audit_trail.py` |\n | §5.1 verdict affects recommendation | boundary enforcement | `test_decision_boundary.py` |\n | §5.2 NO_TRADE for approved HOLD | `DecisionStatus` | `test_verdict_semantics.py` |\n | §5.3 structured weight/snapshot | `TargetPosition`, `PortfolioRiskSnapshot` | `test_input_contract.py` |\n | §5.4 trade scope | applicability | `test_trade_scope.py` |\n | §5.5 policy version/hash | `RiskPolicy` | `test_policy_versioning.py` |\n | Structured retention (API+CLI) | state keys | `test_integration_retention.py` |\n \n ## 4. Test matrix\n \n All tests are `@pytest.mark.unit`, offline (the repo's `conftest.py` already\n blocks sockets), parameterized deterministically. Files live under `tests/risk_gate/`.\n \n ### 4.1 Rule-level (`test_rules.py`)\n \n - R1: BUY missing stop → REJECTED, id `R1_STOP_LOSS_REQUIRED`.\n - R2: weight 0.12 → REJECTED; weight 0.10 → PASS; weight 0.099 → PASS.\n - R3: sector 0.35 → REJECTED; 0.30 → PASS.\n - R4: long RR 2.0 → PASS; RR 0.5 → REJECTED; short direction-aware.\n - R5: blacklisted ticker → REJECTED; normalization for `aapl`/`AAPL`.\n - Valid BUY (all in bounds) → APPROVED, `R0_ALL_RULES_PASSED` present.\n - Wrong-side stop (long stop ≥ entry) → REJECTED; wrong-side target → REJECTED.\n \n ### 4.2 Exact boundaries (`test_boundaries.py`)\n \n - 10% weight: `0.10` PASS, next representable above → REJECTED. The fixture holds a\n   positive AAPL position, so a target weight of `0.0` (and a target equal to the\n   held value) is **not approved** — a genuine BUY must increase the position.\n - 30% **projected post-trade** sector: `0.30` PASS (inclusive), just over REJECTED.\n - 1.5 RR: exactly `1.5` PASS; `1.4999...` REJECTED.\n \n ### 4.3 Injected violations (`test_rule_violations.py`)\n \n Five individually isolated fixtures, each asserting the expected rule id is\n `VIOLATED` and verdict `REJECTED`, with the *other* rules not violated: missing\n stop (R1; R4 may be UNKNOWN), single-name 12% (R2), projected sector 40% (R3),\n RR 0.5 (R4), blacklist (R5).\n \n ### 4.4 Malformed / missing inputs (`test_input_contract.py`)\n \n - Missing target position/weight → NEEDS_REVIEW, R2 `UNKNOWN`, PENDING_REVIEW.\n - Missing portfolio/sector → NEEDS_REVIEW, R3 `UNKNOWN`.\n - Missing target price → NEEDS_REVIEW, R4 `UNKNOWN`.\n - NaN/inf prices → NEEDS_REVIEW, never ACTIONABLE.\n - Contradictory proposal/decision direction → NEEDS_REVIEW (R6 `UNKNOWN`).\n - Inconsistent snapshot (holdings+cash ≠ portfolio_value), stale valuation date,\n   unaffordable purchase → NEEDS_REVIEW, never ACTIONABLE.\n \n ### 4.5 Verdict semantics (`test_verdict_semantics.py`)\n \n - Precedence REJECTED > NEEDS_REVIEW > APPROVED.\n - All applicable rules collected (no first-fail).\n - UNKNOWN is distinct from VIOLATED; `triggered_violation_ids` lists only VIOLATED.\n - `triggered_violation_ids` ⊆ `evaluated_rule_ids`; both present for clean runs.\n - Approved HOLD → `NO_TRADE`; approved BUY → `ACTIONABLE`; rejected → `BLOCKED`;\n   needs-review → `PENDING_REVIEW`; model rating preserved on reject.\n \n ### 4.6 Trade scope (`test_trade_scope.py`)\n \n Mandatory (hard assertions, not xfail): HOLD never ACTIONABLE; SELL/short without\n explicit position+trade data never APPROVED; ambiguous direction never APPROVED.\n A `test_proposed_*` records the pending SELL-with-data expectation separately.\n \n ### 4.7 Invariants (`test_invariants.py`)\n \n - APPROVED ⇒ stop-loss present for actionable BUY.\n - APPROVED ⇒ weight ≤ 0.10.\n - APPROVED ⇒ decision_status in {ACTIONABLE, NO_TRADE}.\n - Sweep over deterministic grid: no APPROVED violates INV-A1.\n \n ### 4.8 100 invalid fixtures (`test_100_invalid_fixtures.py`)\n \n Simple, independent, reproducible parameterized cases (no fragile dictionary-\n merging cross-products that could overwrite `target_position` or other inputs).\n Exactly 100 **distinct** fixtures are exercised; distinctness is keyed on the\n actual input payload and the policy (blacklist), excluding the case label.\n \n Cases span **all five rules plus input-integrity failures** (R1–R6). Every\n blacklist fixture explicitly blacklists the analyzed ticker (AAPL), so R5 applies.\n Each case declares the rule it targets and the outcome that rule must record:\n \n - `VIOLATED` cases assert the expected rule id is present with `VIOLATED` and is in\n   `triggered_violation_ids`.\n - `UNKNOWN` (input-integrity) cases assert the referenced rule is `UNKNOWN` and is\n   **not** falsely recorded as `VIOLATED`.\n - Aggregate: **0 of 100 APPROVED**, none ACTIONABLE; all of R1–R5 plus an\n   input-integrity `UNKNOWN` outcome are represented; the 100 are distinct.\n - A dedicated test asserts every blacklist fixture includes the analyzed ticker.\n \n The affordability fixture uses a consistent 1,000,000 book (cash 10,000, AAPL\n 20,000, MSFT 150,000, others 820,000 across several non-Technology sectors); target\n weight 0.05 → projected AAPL 50,000 (+30,000 increase) but only 10,000 cash, so R2\n (0.05 ≤ 0.10) and R3 (Technology 20%) pass and affordability is the only blocker,\n yielding `NEEDS_REVIEW` under the `REJECTED > NEEDS_REVIEW > APPROVED` precedence.\n \n ### 4.9 Audit (`test_audit_trail.py`)\n \n - Required *values* verified (policy hash length, UTC timestamp format, latency,\n   snapshot non-empty and value-bearing), not mere key presence.\n - 10 evaluations → 100% audit coverage with identical version/hash.\n - No credentials or raw prompt fields.\n \n ### 4.10 Policy versioning (`test_policy_versioning.py`)\n \n - `version == \"fr-a1-v1\"`; `policy_hash` stable; distinct hash when a threshold\n   changes; version/hash recorded in evaluation.\n \n ### 4.11 Latency / no network (`test_latency_no_network.py`)\n \n - 1000 evaluations; measured **core** p95 ≤ 2000 ms; the measured p50/p95 is\n   reported in the test output. Core latency is distinguished from integration\n   overhead (graph wiring is covered separately).\n - A runtime socket guard (every connect/`getaddrinfo` refuses) is installed for the\n   evaluation loop; a subprocess structural check asserts importing the engine\n   alone pulls in no network/LLM module.\n \n ### 4.12 Integration acceptance (`test_integration_retention.py`, `test_decision_boundary.py`)\n \n **These are NOT approved for the core stage.** They are retained for the later\n integration stage and will require separate review and approval before integration.\n They exercise graph/CLI/checkpoint code and are expected to fail (RED) until that\n stage. `[SAFETY]`/`[PRESERVE]` marked, real graph/CLI behavioral tests (not\n existence checks).\n \n - Programmatic API: **unconditional** assertions for REJECTED and for NEEDS_REVIEW —\n   expected `risk_verdict`, effective public signal `REVIEW`, preserved\n   `model_rating`, and `decision_status` (`BLOCKED`/`PENDING_REVIEW`).\n - CLI stream path: a real `run_analysis` drive with a scripted streamed REJECTED\n   BUY verifies the decision recorded downstream is not an actionable BUY\n   (effective signal `REVIEW`, `decision_status` BLOCKED, `model_rating` kept).\n - Structured objects retained in state without Markdown parsing (`[SAFETY]`).\n - Audit persistence: state log records `risk_verdict` and `policy_version`\n   (`[SAFETY]`).\n - Checkpoint safety: the run signature carries a `risk_gate` **marker**, and a\n   pre-gate checkpoint cannot resume into a gated graph — asserted structurally on\n   the marker list, not by searching a hash for a word (`[SAFETY]`).\n - Existing rendered strings and `run_rating` (model rating) unchanged (`[PRESERVE]`).\n \n ## 5. Expected outcomes before implementation\n \n Because production code is absent, the risk-gate tests import the engine at test\n execution time and fail (RED) with `ModuleNotFoundError: tradingagents.risk_gate`.\n There is **no module-level importorskip and no production stub**. Test files are\n collected before implementation; individual tests fail for real, proving they\n exercise the gate. Collection succeeds; failures are the honest pre-implementation\n state, never counted as passes. The existing regression suite must be unaffected\n (`[PRESERVE]`).\n \n ## 6. Intentional safety changes vs regression\n \n - `[SAFETY]` items intentionally change observable behavior at the decision\n   boundary (non-APPROVED directions become `REVIEW`/blocked). These are not\n   regressions.\n - `[PRESERVE]` items must remain identical; failing ones indicate unintended\n   regression and must not be \"fixed\" by weakening assertions.\n \n ## 7. Pending scope decisions (recorded separately)\n \n Mandatory safety behavior is encoded as hard assertions, not non-strict xfail.\n Genuinely unresolved policy extensions are recorded as `test_proposed_*` or here:\n \n - P1 HOLD applicability of R4 (proposed: `NOT_APPLICABLE`).\n - P2 SELL risk-reducing criteria and required explicit data (mandatory:\n   unsupported SELL never approved).\n - P3 Blacklist source (proposed: injectable policy).\n - P4 FR-A2 boundary: NEEDS_REVIEW blocked from automatic execution.\n - P5 Sector snapshot additive contract details.\n - P6 Sector-cap scope: affected sector (v1 default) vs all sectors.\n \n ## 8. Staged implementation: core vs integration\n \n Stage 1 (next, on approval) implements **only the independent risk engine** under\n `tradingagents/risk_gate/` (pure, no network/file-I/O/LLM) and its **core** tests.\n It does **not** modify graph, agent, CLI, reporting, rating, memory, or checkpoint\n code. Proposed core-stage production files are enumerated in the ADR.\n \n ## 9. def run_analysis(checkpoint: bool | None = None, portfolio=None, flags=None):
    flags = flags or {}
    # With no terminal nothing can answer a prompt: name every question still
    # open before any model is called, rather than stopping at the first one.
    if not (sys.stdin and sys.stdin.isatty()):
        gaps = unattended_gaps(flags)
        if gaps:
            console.print("[red]No terminal to answer the setup questions. Set:[/red]")
            for gap in gaps:
                console.print(f"  {gap}")
            raise typer.Exit(code=1)

    selections = get_user_selections(flags)

    config = _build_run_config(selections, checkpoint)

    stats_handler = StatsCallbackHandler()

    # Normalize analyst selection to predefined order (selection is a 'set', order is fixed)
    selected_set = {analyst.value for analyst in selections["analysts"]}
    selected_analyst_keys = [a for a in ANALYST_ORDER if a in selected_set]
    analyst_execution_plan = build_analyst_execution_plan(selected_analyst_keys)
    analyst_wall_time_tracker = AnalystWallTimeTracker(analyst_execution_plan)

    graph = TradingAgentsGraph(
        selected_analyst_keys,
        config=config,
        debug=True,
        callbacks=[stats_handler],
    )

    message_buffer.init_for_analysis(selected_analyst_keys)

    # Track start time for elapsed display
    start_time = time.time()

    results_dir = _run_directory(config, selections["ticker"], selections["analysis_date"])

def _offer_reports(final_state, graph, ticker, save=None, show=None, html=None):
    """Save the report tree and show it; ``save``/``show``/``html`` answer the questions when given.

    A saved report includes the HTML page unless ``html`` is False. Someone
    answering the save question at the prompt is also asked about the page and
    offered to open it; a run whose flags answer the save question asks neither.
    """
    asked = save is None
    if asked:
        save = typer.prompt("Save report?", default="Y").strip().upper() in ("Y", "YES", "")
    if save:
        # Under results_dir, not the working directory: in Docker the working
        # directory is inside the container and the report goes with it, while
        # results_dir is the mounted volume the rest of the run already writes to.
        save_path = graph.default_report_path(ticker)
        if asked:   # someone at the prompt may pick another folder
            save_path = Path(typer.prompt(
                "Save path (press Enter for default)", default=str(save_path)
            ).strip())
        if html is None:
            html = _yes("Also save it as an HTML page?") if asked else True
        saved = False
        try:
            report_file = graph.save_reports(final_state, ticker, save_path, html=html)
            saved = True
            console.print(f"\n[green]✓ Report saved to:[/green] {save_path.resolve()}")
            console.print(f"  [dim]Complete report:[/dim] {report_file.name}")
        except Exception as e:
            console.print(f"[red]Error saving report: {e}[/red]")
        if saved and html:
            page = (save_path / "complete_report.html").resolve()
            console.print(f"  [dim]HTML report:[/dim] {page.name}")
            if asked:
                _open_page(page)

    if show is None:
        show = typer.prompt("\nDisplay full report on screen?", default="Y").strip().upper() in ("Y", "YES", "")
    if show:
        display_complete_report(final_state)

def analyze(
    ctx: typer.Context,
    checkpoint: bool | None = typer.Option(
        None,
        "--checkpoint/--no-checkpoint",
        help="Enable/disable checkpoint-resume (save state after each node so a "
        "crashed run can resume). Omit to honor TRADINGAGENTS_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED.",
    ),
    clear_checkpoints: bool = typer.Option(
        False,
        "--clear-checkpoints",
        help="Delete all saved checkpoints before running (force fresh start).",
    ),
    portfolio: str = typer.Option(
        None,
        "--portfolio",
        help="JSON file with current holdings and cash, so the trader, risk and "
        "portfolio agents size against your actual position.",
    ),
    ticker: str = typer.Option(None, "--ticker", help="Ticker to analyze, e.g. NVDA or 0700.HK; skips the prompt"),
    date: str = typer.Option(None, "--date", help="Analysis date, YYYY-MM-DD; skips the prompt"),
    analysts: str = typer.Option(
        None, "--analysts", help="Comma-separated analysts, e.g. market,news; skips the prompt"
    ),
    save: bool | None = typer.Option(
        None, "--save/--no-save", help="Save the report under results_dir without asking"
    ),
    show: bool | None = typer.Option(
        None, "--show/--no-show", help="Show the full report at the end without asking"
    ),
    html: bool | None = typer.Option(
        None, "--html/--no-html",
        help="Save the report as one HTML page too, complete_report.html, without asking (default: yes)",
    ),
):
    """Run an analysis. This is what a bare `tradingagents` does.

    Flags answer their questions; with provider, models, depth and language also
    set through TRADINGAGENTS_* variables, the run asks nothing.
    """
    if ctx.invoked_subcommand is not None:
        return
    if clear_checkpoints:
        from tradingagents.graph.checkpointer import clear_all_checkpoints
        n = clear_all_checkpoints(DEFAULT_CONFIG["data_cache_dir"])
        console.print(f"[yellow]Cleared {n} checkpoint(s).[/yellow]")
    portfolio_context = None
    if portfolio:
        try:
            portfolio_context = load_portfolio(portfolio)
        except ValueError as exc:
            console.print(f"[red]{exc}[/red]")
            raise typer.Exit(code=1) from None

    try:
        flags = {"ticker": ticker, "date": date, "analysts": analysts, "save": save, "show": show, "html": html}
        run_analysis(checkpoint=checkpoint, portfolio=portfolio_context, flags=flags)
    except _NO_CONSOLE_ERRORS:
        # A terminal with no console buffer cannot host the interactive prompts.
        # Emit one actionable line on stderr instead of a prompt_toolkit
        # traceback; plain text, since rich may not render here either (#1138).
        typer.echo(
            "Error: no Windows console available. The interactive CLI needs a real "
            "console buffer — run it from Windows Terminal, PowerShell, or cmd.exe "
            "rather than a piped or embedded terminal.",
            err=True,
        )
        raise typer.Exit(code=1) from None

def display_complete_report(final_state):
    """Display the complete analysis report sequentially (avoids truncation)."""
    console.print()
    console.print(Rule("Complete Analysis Report", style="bold green"))

    # I. Analyst Team Reports
    analysts = []
    if final_state.get("market_report"):
        analysts.append(("Market Analyst", final_state["market_report"]))
    if final_state.get("sentiment_report"):
        analysts.append(("Sentiment Analyst", final_state["sentiment_report"]))
    if final_state.get("news_report"):
        analysts.append(("News Analyst", final_state["news_report"]))
    if final_state.get("fundamentals_report"):
        analysts.append(("Fundamentals Analyst", final_state["fundamentals_report"]))
    if analysts:
        console.print(Panel("[bold]I. Analyst Team Reports[/bold]", border_style="cyan"))
        for title, content in analysts:
            console.print(Panel(Markdown(content), title=title, border_style="blue", padding=(1, 2)))

    # II. Research Team Reports
    if final_state.get("investment_debate_state"):
        debate = final_state["investment_debate_state"]
        research = []
        if debate.get("bull_history"):
            research.append(("Bull Researcher", debate["bull_history"]))
        if debate.get("bear_history"):
            research.append(("Bear Researcher", debate["bear_history"]))
        if final_state.get("investment_plan"):
            research.append(("Research Manager", final_state["investment_plan"]))
        if research:
            console.print(Panel("[bold]II. Research Team Decision[/bold]", border_style="magenta"))
            for title, content in research:
                console.print(Panel(Markdown(content), title=title, border_style="blue", padding=(1, 2)))

    # III. Trading Team
    if final_state.get("trader_investment_plan"):
        console.print(Panel("[bold]III. Trading Team Plan[/bold]", border_style="yellow"))
        console.print(Panel(Markdown(final_state["trader_investment_plan"]), title="Trader", border_style="blue", padding=(1, 2)))

    # IV. Risk Management Team
    if final_state.get("risk_debate_state"):
        risk = final_state["risk_debate_state"]
        risk_reports = []
        if risk.get("aggressive_history"):
            risk_reports.append(("Aggressive Analyst", risk["aggressive_history"]))
        if risk.get("conservative_history"):
            risk_reports.append(("Conservative Analyst", risk["conservative_history"]))
        if risk.get("neutral_history"):
            risk_reports.append(("Neutral Analyst", risk["neutral_history"]))
        if risk_reports:
            console.print(Panel("[bold]IV. Risk Management Team Decision[/bold]", border_style="red"))
            for title, content in risk_reports:
                console.print(Panel(Markdown(content), title=title, border_style="blue", padding=(1, 2)))

    # V. Portfolio Manager Decision
    if final_state.get("final_trade_decision"):
        console.print(Panel("[bold]V. Portfolio Manager Decision[/bold]", border_style="green"))
        console.print(Panel(Markdown(final_state["final_trade_decision"]), title="Portfolio Manager", border_style="blue", padding=(1, 2)))

Stage 2 revision: audit-before-publish (from final test review)\n\nThe output-boundary adapter (§13.2) computes the verdict before the PM node returns,\nso no consumer can see an actionable BUY that was not evaluated. The final review\nidentified a narrower gap: **on-disk audit durability relative to publication**.\n\n### 14.1 Decision\n\nThe gate must establish the durable audit **before** an actionable (`APPROVED`)\nsignal is released. Two facts constrain this:\n\n- The state log is written by `record_decision` *after* the stream ends; the PM\n  node return (and any streamed `final_rating`) precedes it.\n- A streamed `final_rating == \"Buy\"` could therefore be observed before the audit\n  is on disk if persistence happened only in `record_decision`.\n\nTo guarantee safety without adding a second evaluation:\n\n1. The adapter computes the verdict (once) and, for `APPROVED` only, **persists the\n   audit record durably before returning** the state update that sets\n   `final_rating` to an actionable rating. For `REJECTED`/`NEEDS_REVIEW` the\n   published value is `REVIEW`, which is already non-actionable, so persistence may\n   occur either before or alongside `_log_state`; the recommendation cannot be\n   acted on regardless.\n2. `_log_state` also records the audit (append-only) for the run manifest.\n3. If durable persistence raises, the adapter **fails closed**: it does not emit an\n   actionable `final_rating`; the run surfaces the failure (or downgrades to\n   `REVIEW` with the failure recorded) rather than approving.\n\nThis keeps a single evaluation and one authoritative boundary. It is a refinement\nof §13.2, not a new architecture.\n\n### 14.2 Audit content (minimum necessary)\n\nThe persisted audit is the `RiskEvaluation`: rule ids + outcomes, the minimal\n`input_snapshot` (including `target_position_weight`, `portfolio_value`, `cash`,\n`target_sector`, prices, action, model rating), derived per-rule `observed`/\n`threshold` values (so R2 weight and R3 projected sector exposure are explainable),\nverdict, `decision_status`, `policy_version`, `policy_hash`, `evaluated_at_utc`,\nand `latency_ms`. No credentials, prompts, or full holdings beyond what explains\nthe two exposure rules.\n\n### 14.3 Consequence for tests\n\n- The streamed-output test must show no actionable BUY is released without a\n  durable audit; a simulated persistence failure must not yield an actionable\n  `final_rating` on the stream.\n- The audit must contain the numeric inputs and derived exposures for R2/R3.\n\n### 14.4 CLI configuration path (documented, not invented)\n\nThere is **no** `risk_portfolio` CLI flag or environment variable today. The\nreachable caller path is programmatic (`TradingAgentsGraph(config={\"risk_portfolio\":\n...})`) and, for the CLI, requires the implementation to thread `risk_portfolio`\nthrough `_build_run_config` (e.g. from a future documented option or config file).\nUntil then the **default CLI path fails closed** (NEEDS_REVIEW → REVIEW). No CLI\noption is added in this stage.\nEOF\necho done"
}

  "newString": "@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_audit_persistence_failure_cannot_leave_actionable_signal(tmp_path, monkeypatch, offline):\n    \"\"\"[SAFETY] If audit persistence fails, an actionable signal must not stand.\"\"\"\n    graph = _graph(tmp_path, monkeypatch, _buy_proposal(), _buy_decision(),\n                   risk_portfolio=RISK_PORTFOLIO)\n\n    def boom(*a, **k):\n        raise OSError(\"disk full\")\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(graph, \"_log_state\", boom)\n    with pytest.raises(OSError):\n        graph.propagate(\"NVDA\", e2e.TRADE_DATE)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_audit_failure_does_not_release_actionable_buy_on_stream(tmp_path, monkeypatch, offline):\n    \"\"\"[SAFETY] A durable-audit failure must not publish an actionable BUY.\n\n    The adapter must establish the durable audit before releasing an APPROVED\n    signal (ADR §14). We simulate the durable store failing; the streamed/published\n    final rating must never be an actionable Buy, and no APPROVED verdict may be\n    surfaced. Fail-closed (REVIEW / raised) both satisfy safety; an emitted\n    `final_rating == \"Buy\"` while persistence failed is the forbidden outcome.\n    \"\"\"\n    graph = _graph(tmp_path, monkeypatch, _buy_proposal(), _buy_decision(),\n                   risk_portfolio=RISK_PORTFOLIO)\n\n    def boom(*a, **k):\n        raise OSError(\"audit store unavailable\")\n\n    # The durable audit sink used by the adapter (proposed) is patched to fail.\n    import tradingagents.risk_gate as rg\n    monkeypatch.setattr(rg, \"_persist_audit\", boom, raising=False)\n\n    released = []\n    try:\n        for _messages, chunk in graph.stream_run(\n                graph.create_run_state(\"NVDA\", e2e.TRADE_DATE), **graph.propagator.get_graph_args()):\n            if chunk and \"final_rating\" in chunk:\n                released.append((chunk.get(\"final_rating\"), chunk.get(\"risk_verdict\")))\n    except OSError:\n        return  # failing the whole run closed is acceptable safety behavior\n\n    for rating, verdict in released:\n        # An actionable Buy may only be released with an APPROVED verdict AND a\n        # durably written audit; since persistence failed, it never may.\n        assert not (rating == \"Buy\" and verdict == \"APPROVED\"), released",
  "oldString": "@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_audit_persistence_failure_cannot_leave_actionable_signal(tmp_path, monkeypatch, offline):\n    \"\"\"[SAFETY] If audit persistence fails, an actionable signal must not stand.\"\"\"\n    graph = _graph(tmp_path, monkeypatch, _buy_proposal(), _buy_decision(),\n                   risk_portfolio=RISK_PORTFOLIO)\n\n    def boom(*a, **k):\n        raise OSError(\"disk full\")\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(graph, \"_log_state\", boom)\n    with pytest.raises(OSError):\n        graph.propagate(\"NVDA\", e2e.TRADE_DATE)"

def thread_id(ticker: str, date: str, signature: str = "") -> str:
    """Deterministic thread ID for a ticker+date pair.

    ``signature`` folds in graph-shape-affecting run choices so a resume under a
    different graph can't reuse this checkpoint (#1089); omitting it keeps the
    legacy ID.
    """
    base = f"{ticker.upper()}:{date}"
    if signature:
        base = f"{base}:{signature}"
    return hashlib.sha256(base.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]


@contextmanager
def get_checkpointer(data_dir: str | Path, ticker: str) -> Generator[SqliteSaver, None, None]:

````text
All four gaps addressed within the approved scope. No production/engine changes; core tests untouched.

# Final Stage 2 Integration Test Corrections — Report

## 1. Corrected integration tests

**Gap 1 — CLI publication & configuration** (`test_decision_boundary.py`): replaced the fake-graph + mocked-`record_decision` test with `_run_real_cli`, which builds the **real** `TradingAgentsGraph` (only the LLM factory is pointed at the offline scripted model), runs the **real** `run_analysis`, and lets the **real** `record_decision` write the state log. `_build_run_config` is **wrapped** (delegates to the real function, then injects the additive `risk_portfolio` key) — not replaced. Three tests:
- `test_cli_displays_review_and_records_risk_controlled_result` — captured console shows the actual "recorded for review" notice; on-disk state log has `risk_verdict=REJECTED`, `final_rating=REVIEW`, `policy_version=fr-a1-v1`.
- `test_cli_default_path_without_snapshot_fails_closed` — no snapshot → `NEEDS_REVIEW`/`REVIEW`.
- `test_cli_reachable_config_path_can_approve` — `risk_portfolio` → `APPROVED`/`Buy`. No CLI flag invented; the required threading through `_build_run_config` is documented (ADR §14.4, plan §9.5).

**Gap 2 — Audit persistence safety** (`test_integration_retention.py`): added `test_audit_failure_does_not_release_actionable_buy_on_stream`, which simulates durable-store failure and asserts no `("Buy","APPROVED")` is ever streamed (fail-closed by raising also accepted). Audit content tests already require numeric inputs (`target_position_weight`, `portfolio_value`, `cash`, `target_sector`) explaining R2/R3, and no credentials/prompts. Backed by a focused ADR §14 "audit-before-publish" revision.

**Gap 3 — Actual integration overhead**: replaced the reconstructed-direct-call timing with `_bench_adapter` measuring the real `tradingagents.risk_gate.adapter.apply_gate` (input conversion + evaluation + audit) over 200 iterations, asserting **p95 ≤ 2000 ms** and printing p50/p95. Won't be claimed passing until the adapter exists.

**Gap 4 — Checkpoint compatibility**: retained the same-instance resume test; added `test_legacy_pre_gate_checkpoint_cannot_bypass_evaluation`, which writes a real checkpoint under a **legacy (pre-gate) signature** and asserts the gated lookup (`checkpoint_step` with the gated signature) finds nothing → fresh, evaluated run. Uses `thread_id()`, not substring checks.

## 2. Selected enforcement & audit boundary
Portfolio Manager **output-boundary adapter** (one evaluation), refined by ADR §14: for `APPROVED`, the durable audit is established **before** releasing an actionable `final_rating`; persistence failure fails closed (never emits an actionable BUY); `REJECTED`/`NEEDS_REVIEW` publish `REVIEW`. `_log_state` also records the audit for the manifest.

## 3. Exact file-write scope for implementation (unchanged from approved plan, +adapter sink)
- `tradingagents/risk_gate/adapter.py` (new: `build_inputs`, `apply_gate`, `_persist_audit`).
- `tradingagents/agents/state.py` (additive keys).
- `tradingagents/agents/trader/trader.py`, `tradingagents/agents/managers/portfolio_manager.py` (return structured objects; PM calls adapter).
- `tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py` (`risk_portfolio` threading incl. `_build_run_config`, `risk_gate` layout marker, audit persistence + failure guard in `_log_state`/`record_decision`).
- No changes to engine, `rating.py`, `reporting.py`, `cli/*` semantics.

## 4. Remaining known limitations
- No `risk_portfolio` CLI flag/env exists yet; default CLI fails closed until implementation threads it (documented, not invented).
- `_persist_audit` and `adapter.apply_gate` are proposed, not implemented — the perf and durable-audit tests are intentionally RED.
- Legacy-checkpoint test currently fails because today's `_run_signature` has no `risk_gate` marker (the gap the implementation closes).
- SELL/HOLD exemptions and affected-sector scope remain pending team confirmation (ADR §12).

## 5. Verification (actual exit codes)
| Command | Exit | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `ruff check tradingagents/risk_gate tests/risk_gate` | **0** | All checks passed |
| `pytest tests/risk_gate --collect-only` | **0** | **223 collected** |
| integration files | **1** | **24 failed, 3 passed** — expected pre-implementation RED (adapter/state keys/audit sink absent) |
| core (excl. 2 integration files) | **0** | **195 passed, 1 xpassed** (unchanged) |
| `pytest -q --ignore=tests/risk_gate` | **0** | 1412 passed, 1 skipped |

The 3 passing integration tests assert fail-closed/preserve behavior that already holds; none masks missing integration (legacy-checkpoint + perf + adapter tests are RED).

Stage 2 revision: audit-before-publish (from final test review)\n \n The output-boundary adapter (§13.2) computes the verdict before the PM node returns,\n so no consumer can see an actionable BUY that was not evaluated. The final review\n identified a narrower gap: **on-disk audit durability relative to publication**.\n \n ### 14.1 Decision\n \n The gate must establish the durable audit **before** an actionable (`APPROVED`)\n signal is released. Two facts constrain this:\n \n - The state log is written by `record_decision` *after* the stream ends; the PM\n   node return (and any streamed `final_rating`) precedes it.\n - A streamed `final_rating == \"Buy\"` could therefore be observed before the audit\n   is on disk if persistence happened only in `record_decision`.\n \n To guarantee safety without adding a second evaluation:\n \n 1.
