        "patch": "Index: docs/req/fr-a1-test-plan.md\n===================================================================\n--- docs/req/fr-a1-test-plan.md\t\n+++ docs/req/fr-a1-test-plan.md\t\n@@ -1,467 +1,470 @@\n # FR-A1 Test Plan — Deterministic Risk Gate\n \n - Status: Authoring approved; production implementation blocked pending review of these tests.\n - Date: 2026-11-11\n - Owner: A\n - Requirement: FR-A1, with INV-A1, NFR-A1, NFR-A2\n - Related ADR: `docs/architecture/adr/adr-fr-a1-risk-gate.md`\n - Baseline: `46bde74`\n \n This plan describes the agreed contract and its offline test coverage. It is\n written before production implementation so the tests can be reviewed. Tests\n reference the requirement/invariant they enforce. Intentional safety-related\n behavior changes are marked `[SAFETY]`; everything else must remain an existing\n behavior (`[PRESERVE]`).\n \n ## 1. Proposed interface (contract under review)\n \n The tests are written against this interface. It is expected to match the\n eventual implementation; production code is not written yet.\n \n ### 1.1 Package `tradingagents.risk_gate`\n \n Modules (proposed): `models.py`, `policy.py`, `engine.py`, `sizing.py`,\n `portfolio_snapshot.py`, `node.py` (integration). The core engine modules have no\n network, no file I/O, no LLM imports.\n \n ### 1.2 Enumerations\n \n ```python\n class RiskVerdict(StrEnum):\n     APPROVED = \"APPROVED\"\n     REJECTED = \"REJECTED\"\n     NEEDS_REVIEW = \"NEEDS_REVIEW\"\n \n class DecisionStatus(StrEnum):\n     ACTIONABLE = \"ACTIONABLE\"\n     BLOCKED = \"BLOCKED\"\n     PENDING_REVIEW = \"PENDING_REVIEW\"\n     NO_TRADE = \"NO_TRADE\"\n \n class RuleOutcome(StrEnum):\n     PASS = \"PASS\"\n     VIOLATED = \"VIOLATED\"\n     NOT_APPLICABLE = \"NOT_APPLICABLE\"\n     UNKNOWN = \"UNKNOWN\"\n ```\n \n ### 1.3 Rule identifiers\n \n | ID | Meaning |\n |---|---|\n | `R1_STOP_LOSS_REQUIRED` | Long actionable BUY must carry a stop-loss |\n | `R2_SINGLE_NAME_CAP` | Projected single-name weight ≤ 10% (0.10) |\n | `R3_SECTOR_CONCENTRATION` | Projected sector exposure ≤ 30% (0.30) |\n | `R4_REWARD_RISK` | Direction-aware reward-to-risk ≥ 1.5 and ordering stop<entry<target |\n | `R5_BLACKLIST` | Ticker not on the deterministic blacklist |\n | `R6_INPUT_INTEGRITY` | Structured inputs present, consistent, unambiguous |\n | `R0_ALL_RULES_PASSED` | Positive marker so every verdict carries a rule ID |\n \n `R0` is a synthetic \"pass\" entry: every evaluation carries at least one rule ID,\n satisfying \"100% of verdicts carry a rule identifier\" (`requirements.yaml:28`),\n including clean approvals.\n \n ### 1.4 Input models\n \n ```python\n class TargetPosition(BaseModel):\n     target_position_weight: float | None   # projected post-trade single-name weight, 0..1\n     sector: str | None = None               # target stock's sector, required when not held\n \n class Holding(BaseModel):\n     ticker: str\n     market_value: float          # current market value; never average cost\n     sector: str | None\n \n class PortfolioRiskSnapshot(BaseModel):\n     valuation_date: str          # ISO date; must be consistent with the run's trade_date\n     portfolio_value: float       # total portfolio value used for weight denominators\n     cash: float                  # cash available to fund a cash-funded long\n     holdings: list[Holding]\n     # consistency: cash + Σ holdings.market_value == portfolio_value\n \n class RiskInputs(BaseModel):\n     ticker: str\n     trade_date: str\n     action: str | None           # TraderProposal.action, if structured output produced it\n     entry_price: float | None\n     stop_loss: float | None\n     price_target: float | None   # PortfolioDecision.price_target\n     model_rating: str | None     # PortfolioDecision.rating, verbatim\n     target_position: TargetPosition | None\n     portfolio: PortfolioRiskSnapshot | None\n ```\n \n **Projected exposure (cash-funded long, documented for v1):**\n `projected_stock_value = target_position_weight * portfolio_value`;\n `projected_sector_value = current_sector_value - current_stock_value +\n projected_stock_value`. A genuine BUY increases the position and the purchase\n (`projected_stock_value - current_stock_value`) is affordable from `cash`. Missing\n target sector for an unheld stock, or an inconsistent snapshot, makes the affected\n rule `UNKNOWN` → `NEEDS_REVIEW`, never `APPROVED`.\n \n ### 1.5 Output models\n \n ```python\n class RuleResult(BaseModel):\n     rule_id: str\n     outcome: RuleOutcome\n     detail: str                      # deterministic; no PII/credentials\n     observed: float | None = None\n     threshold: float | None = None\n \n class RiskEvaluation(BaseModel):\n     verdict: RiskVerdict\n     decision_status: DecisionStatus\n     model_rating: str | None\n     evaluated_rule_ids: list[str]        # every rule considered\n     triggered_violation_ids: list[str]   # only VIOLATED rule ids\n     rule_results: list[RuleResult]       # complete per-rule results\n     policy_version: str\n     policy_hash: str\n     input_snapshot: dict                 # minimal, redacted snapshot\n     evaluated_at_utc: str                # ISO8601 UTC\n     latency_ms: float\n \n class RiskAuditRecord(BaseModel):\n     audit_id: str\n     evaluation: RiskEvaluation\n ```\n \n ### 1.6 Engine entry points\n \n ```python\n def evaluate_risk(inputs: RiskInputs, policy: RiskPolicy | None = None) -> RiskEvaluation: ...\n \n class RiskPolicy:\n     version: str          # \"fr-a1-v1\"\n     policy_hash: str      # stable hash of the constants\n     single_name_cap: float = 0.10\n     sector_cap: float = 0.30\n     min_reward_risk: float = 1.5\n     blacklist: frozenset[str] = frozenset()\n ```\n \n `evaluate_risk` is pure and deterministic. Ticker normalization uses\n `tradingagents.dataflows.symbols.normalize_symbol`.\n \n ## 2. Rule semantics and applicability\n \n Precedence for the final verdict: `REJECTED > NEEDS_REVIEW > APPROVED`.\n \n **UNKNOWN is not VIOLATED.** `triggered_violation_ids` lists only rules whose\n outcome is `VIOLATED`; `evaluated_rule_ids` lists every rule considered. When a\n rule cannot be decided for lack of input it is `UNKNOWN` (→ `NEEDS_REVIEW`), not a\n violation. Example: a missing stop-loss makes `R1` `VIOLATED` while `R4` is\n `UNKNOWN` (the ratio cannot be computed).\n \n **Three separate concepts at the boundary:** `model_rating` (the PM's own rating,\n preserved), `risk_verdict` (from the gate), and the *effective public signal*\n (a non-`APPROVED` actionable direction surfaces as the existing `REVIEW`\n sentinel). `final_rating`/`run_rating` keep their baseline meaning — the **model**\n rating — and are not redefined; the gate produces the effective public signal\n separately so blocked recommendations cannot escape as an actionable BUY.\n \n | Rule | Applies when | Violated → | Unknown/inapplicable → |\n |---|---|---|---|\n | R1 stop-loss | long actionable BUY (action Buy) | REJECTED | — |\n | R2 single-name | BUY with a resolvable weight | REJECTED (>0.10) | NEEDS_REVIEW (R2 UNKNOWN: missing weight) |\n | R3 sector | BUY with a resolvable snapshot | REJECTED (>0.30) | NEEDS_REVIEW (R3 UNKNOWN: unknown sector/value) |\n | R4 reward-risk | BUY with entry/stop/target | REJECTED (ratio<1.5 or bad ordering) | NEEDS_REVIEW (R4 UNKNOWN: missing leg) |\n | R5 blacklist | any ticker | REJECTED (on list) | — (list always known) |\n | R6 input integrity | always | — | NEEDS_REVIEW (R6 UNKNOWN: missing/contradictory/inconsistent) |\n \n BUY: all of R1–R5 apply. HOLD: no actionable trade; approved HOLD → `NO_TRADE`\n (R4 `NOT_APPLICABLE` is a pending decision). SELL/short without explicit\n existing-position and trade data → not `APPROVED` (mandatory); exact risk-reducing\n criteria are pending team confirmation. The sector cap applies to the **affected\n sector** of the target stock in v1 (scope pending confirmation).\n \n **As-implemented rule ownership (no semantic change, just allocation):**\n - R2 checks the weight cap and the *genuine increase* clause (UNKNOWN when the\n   buy does not increase the position).\n - R3 checks projected affected-sector exposure (UNKNOWN when a holding lacks a\n   sector, or the target sector is unknown).\n - R6 checks input integrity that spans rules: contradictory/ambiguous direction,\n   non-finite decision prices, an inconsistent or stale portfolio snapshot, and an\n   unaffordable cash-funded purchase. In v1, an unsupported short/SELL is recorded\n   by R6 as UNKNOWN (pending team confirmation), so it cannot be approved.\n - Decision numeric fields are representable as `inf`/`nan` at the model layer so a\n   malformed value degrades to UNKNOWN (NEEDS_REVIEW); it can never become a usable\n   number or an approval.\n \n ## 3. Requirement traceability\n \n | Requirement | Contract element | Test file |\n |---|---|---|\n | FR-A1 verdict + rule IDs | `evaluate_risk`, `rule_results` | `test_rules.py`, `test_verdict_semantics.py` |\n | FR-A1 5 injected violations 5/5 blocked | R1–R5 fixtures | `test_rule_violations.py` |\n | FR-A1 100 invalid fixtures 0 approvals | fixture generator | `test_100_invalid_fixtures.py` |\n | INV-A1 no approval without stop / over cap | invariants | `test_invariants.py` |\n | NFR-A1 p95 ≤ 2 s, 0 network | pure engine + runtime/structural guard | `test_latency_no_network.py` |\n | NFR-A2 audit completeness | `RiskAuditRecord` | `test_audit_trail.py` |\n | §5.1 verdict affects recommendation | boundary enforcement | `test_decision_boundary.py` |\n | §5.2 NO_TRADE for approved HOLD | `DecisionStatus` | `test_verdict_semantics.py` |\n | §5.3 structured weight/snapshot | `TargetPosition`, `PortfolioRiskSnapshot` | `test_input_contract.py` |\n | §5.4 trade scope | applicability | `test_trade_scope.py` |\n | §5.5 policy version/hash | `RiskPolicy` | `test_policy_versioning.py` |\n | Structured retention (API+CLI) | state keys | `test_integration_retention.py` |\n \n ## 4. Test matrix\n \n All tests are `@pytest.mark.unit`, offline (the repo's `conftest.py` already\n blocks sockets), parameterized deterministically. Files live under `tests/risk_gate/`.\n \n ### 4.1 Rule-level (`test_rules.py`)\n \n - R1: BUY missing stop → REJECTED, id `R1_STOP_LOSS_REQUIRED`.\n - R2: weight 0.12 → REJECTED; weight 0.10 → PASS; weight 0.099 → PASS.\n - R3: sector 0.35 → REJECTED; 0.30 → PASS.\n - R4: long RR 2.0 → PASS; RR 0.5 → REJECTED; short direction-aware.\n - R5: blacklisted ticker → REJECTED; normalization for `aapl`/`AAPL`.\n - Valid BUY (all in bounds) → APPROVED, `R0_ALL_RULES_PASSED` present.\n - Wrong-side stop (long stop ≥ entry) → REJECTED; wrong-side target → REJECTED.\n \n ### 4.2 Exact boundaries (`test_boundaries.py`)\n \n - 10% weight: `0.10` PASS, next representable above → REJECTED. The fixture holds a\n   positive AAPL position, so a target weight of `0.0` (and a target equal to the\n   held value) is **not approved** — a genuine BUY must increase the position.\n - 30% **projected post-trade** sector: `0.30` PASS (inclusive), just over REJECTED.\n - 1.5 RR: exactly `1.5` PASS; `1.4999...` REJECTED.\n \n ### 4.3 Injected violations (`test_rule_violations.py`)\n \n Five individually isolated fixtures, each asserting the expected rule id is\n `VIOLATED` and verdict `REJECTED`, with the *other* rules not violated: missing\n stop (R1; R4 may be UNKNOWN), single-name 12% (R2), projected sector 40% (R3),\n RR 0.5 (R4), blacklist (R5).\n \n ### 4.4 Malformed / missing inputs (`test_input_contract.py`)\n \n - Missing target position/weight → NEEDS_REVIEW, R2 `UNKNOWN`, PENDING_REVIEW.\n - Missing portfolio/sector → NEEDS_REVIEW, R3 `UNKNOWN`.\n - Missing target price → NEEDS_REVIEW, R4 `UNKNOWN`.\n - NaN/inf prices → NEEDS_REVIEW, never ACTIONABLE.\n - Contradictory proposal/decision direction → NEEDS_REVIEW (R6 `UNKNOWN`).\n - Inconsistent snapshot (holdings+cash ≠ portfolio_value), stale valuation date,\n   unaffordable purchase → NEEDS_REVIEW, never ACTIONABLE.\n \n ### 4.5 Verdict semantics (`test_verdict_semantics.py`)\n \n - Precedence REJECTED > NEEDS_REVIEW > APPROVED.\n - All applicable rules collected (no first-fail).\n - UNKNOWN is distinct from VIOLATED; `triggered_violation_ids` lists only VIOLATED.\n - `triggered_violation_ids` ⊆ `evaluated_rule_ids`; both present for clean runs.\n - Approved HOLD → `NO_TRADE`; approved BUY → `ACTIONABLE`; rejected → `BLOCKED`;\n   needs-review → `PENDING_REVIEW`; model rating preserved on reject.\n \n ### 4.6 Trade scope (`test_trade_scope.py`)\n \n Mandatory (hard assertions, not xfail): HOLD never ACTIONABLE; SELL/short without\n explicit position+trade data never APPROVED; ambiguous direction never APPROVED.\n A `test_proposed_*` records the pending SELL-with-data expectation separately.\n \n ### 4.7 Invariants (`test_invariants.py`)\n \n - APPROVED ⇒ stop-loss present for actionable BUY.\n - APPROVED ⇒ weight ≤ 0.10.\n - APPROVED ⇒ decision_status in {ACTIONABLE, NO_TRADE}.\n - Sweep over deterministic grid: no APPROVED violates INV-A1.\n \n ### 4.8 100 invalid fixtures (`test_100_invalid_fixtures.py`)\n \n Simple, independent, reproducible parameterized cases (no fragile dictionary-\n merging cross-products that could overwrite `target_position` or other inputs).\n Exactly 100 **distinct** fixtures are exercised; distinctness is keyed on the\n actual input payload and the policy (blacklist), excluding the case label.\n \n Cases span **all five rules plus input-integrity failures** (R1–R6). Every\n blacklist fixture explicitly blacklists the analyzed ticker (AAPL), so R5 applies.\n Each case declares the rule it targets and the outcome that rule must record:\n \n - `VIOLATED` cases assert the expected rule id is present with `VIOLATED` and is in\n   `triggered_violation_ids`.\n - `UNKNOWN` (input-integrity) cases assert the referenced rule is `UNKNOWN` and is\n   **not** falsely recorded as `VIOLATED`.\n - Aggregate: **0 of 100 APPROVED**, none ACTIONABLE; all of R1–R5 plus an\n   input-integrity `UNKNOWN` outcome are represented; the 100 are distinct.\n - A dedicated test asserts every blacklist fixture includes the analyzed ticker.\n \n The affordability fixture uses a consistent 1,000,000 book (cash 10,000, AAPL\n 20,000, MSFT 150,000, others 820,000 across several non-Technology sectors); target\n weight 0.05 → projected AAPL 50,000 (+30,000 increase) but only 10,000 cash, so R2\n (0.05 ≤ 0.10) and R3 (Technology 20%) pass and affordability is the only blocker,\n yielding `NEEDS_REVIEW` under the `REJECTED > NEEDS_REVIEW > APPROVED` precedence.\n \n ### 4.9 Audit (`test_audit_trail.py`)\n \n - Required *values* verified (policy hash length, UTC timestamp format, latency,\n   snapshot non-empty and value-bearing), not mere key presence.\n - 10 evaluations → 100% audit coverage with identical version/hash.\n - No credentials or raw prompt fields.\n \n ### 4.10 Policy versioning (`test_policy_versioning.py`)\n \n - `version == \"fr-a1-v1\"`; `policy_hash` stable; distinct hash when a threshold\n   changes; version/hash recorded in evaluation.\n \n ### 4.11 Latency / no network (`test_latency_no_network.py`)\n \n - 1000 evaluations; measured **core** p95 ≤ 2000 ms; the measured p50/p95 is\n   reported in the test output. Core latency is distinguished from integration\n   overhead (graph wiring is covered separately).\n - A runtime socket guard (every connect/`getaddrinfo` refuses) is installed for the\n   evaluation loop; a subprocess structural check asserts importing the engine\n   alone pulls in no network/LLM module.\n \n ### 4.12 Integration acceptance (`test_integration_retention.py`, `test_decision_boundary.py`)\n \n **These are NOT approved for the core stage.** They are retained for the later\n integration stage and will require separate review and approval before integration.\n They exercise graph/CLI/checkpoint code and are expected to fail (RED) until that\n stage. `[SAFETY]`/`[PRESERVE]` marked, real graph/CLI behavioral tests (not\n existence checks).\n \n - Programmatic API: **unconditional** assertions for REJECTED and for NEEDS_REVIEW —\n   expected `risk_verdict`, effective public signal `REVIEW`, preserved\n   `model_rating`, and `decision_status` (`BLOCKED`/`PENDING_REVIEW`).\n - CLI stream path: a real `run_analysis` drive with a scripted streamed REJECTED\n   BUY verifies the decision recorded downstream is not an actionable BUY\n   (effective signal `REVIEW`, `decision_status` BLOCKED, `model_rating` kept).\n - Structured objects retained in state without Markdown parsing (`[SAFETY]`).\n - Audit persistence: state log records `risk_verdict` and `policy_version`\n   (`[SAFETY]`).\n - Checkpoint safety: the run signature carries a `risk_gate` **marker**, and a\n   pre-gate checkpoint cannot resume into a gated graph — asserted structurally on\n   the marker list, not by searching a hash for a word (`[SAFETY]`).\n - Existing rendered strings and `run_rating` (model rating) unchanged (`[PRESERVE]`).\n \n ## 5. Expected outcomes before implementation\n \n Because production code is absent, the risk-gate tests import the engine at test\n execution time and fail (RED) with `ModuleNotFoundError: tradingagents.risk_gate`.\n There is **no module-level importorskip and no production stub**. Test files are\n collected before implementation; individual tests fail for real, proving they\n exercise the gate. Collection succeeds; failures are the honest pre-implementation\n state, never counted as passes. The existing regression suite must be unaffected\n (`[PRESERVE]`).\n \n ## 6. Intentional safety changes vs regression\n \n - `[SAFETY]` items intentionally change observable behavior at the decision\n   boundary (non-APPROVED directions become `REVIEW`/blocked). These are not\n   regressions.\n - `[PRESERVE]` items must remain identical; failing ones indicate unintended\n   regression and must not be \"fixed\" by weakening assertions.\n \n ## 7. Pending scope decisions (recorded separately)\n \n Mandatory safety behavior is encoded as hard assertions, not non-strict xfail.\n Genuinely unresolved policy extensions are recorded as `test_proposed_*` or here:\n \n - P1 HOLD applicability of R4 (proposed: `NOT_APPLICABLE`).\n - P2 SELL risk-reducing criteria and required explicit data (mandatory:\n   unsupported SELL never approved).\n - P3 Blacklist source (proposed: injectable policy).\n - P4 FR-A2 boundary: NEEDS_REVIEW blocked from automatic execution.\n - P5 Sector snapshot additive contract details.\n - P6 Sector-cap scope: affected sector (v1 default) vs all sectors.\n \n ## 8. Staged implementation: core vs integration\n \n Stage 1 (next, on approval) implements **only the independent risk engine** under\n `tradingagents/risk_gate/` (pure, no network/file-I/O/LLM) and its **core** tests.\n It does **not** modify graph, agent, CLI, reporting, rating, memory, or checkpoint\n code. The core-only test command is:\n \n ```\n pytest tests/risk_gate -q \\\n   --ignore=tests/risk_gate/test_integration_retention.py \\\n   --ignore=tests/risk_gate/test_decision_boundary.py\n ```\n \n Stage 2 (later, separate approval) performs integration and the API/CLI/checkpoint\n acceptance tests (`test_integration_retention.py`, `test_decision_boundary.py`).\n Those tests are **not approved** for the core stage and must not be claimed as\n such. Proposed core-stage production files are enumerated in the ADR.\n \n ## 9. Stage 2 integration test plan (tests-only this turn)\n \n The gate is invoked once at the **Portfolio Manager output boundary** (ADR §13),\n so one authoritative evaluation covers the API and CLI paths. The revised tests run\n real graph execution with the existing offline scripted model\n (`tests/test_graph_end_to_end.py`); they do not mock the verdict and do not bypass\n the engine.\n \n ### 9.1 Proposed adapter interface (target of the tests)\n \n ```python\n # tradingagents/risk_gate/adapter.py (proposed)\n def build_inputs(ticker, trade_date, trader_proposal, portfolio_decision,\n                  risk_portfolio) -> RiskInputs: ...\n def apply_gate(ticker, trade_date, trader_proposal, portfolio_decision,\n                risk_portfolio, policy=None) -> dict:\n     # returns state updates: model_rating, risk_verdict, decision_status,\n     # risk_evaluation (RiskEvaluation) and effective_final_rating\n ```\n \n Caller-facing additive config: `risk_portfolio` = `{ snapshot: {...},\n target_position: {target_position_weight, sector} }`. Absent → R6 UNKNOWN\n (fail closed); present and in-bounds → APPROVED.\n \n ### 9.2 Test matrix (`test_decision_boundary.py`, `test_integration_retention.py`)\n \n | Group | Test | Requirement |\n |---|---|---|\n | A API | valid BUY + complete snapshot → APPROVED, signal = model rating, ACTIONABLE | FR-A1, §5.1 |\n | A API | missing stop → REJECTED, signal REVIEW, model_rating kept | INV-A1 |\n | A API | missing snapshot → NEEDS_REVIEW, signal REVIEW | §5.3 fail-closed |\n | B CLI | real `run_analysis` (real graph, real `record_decision`); displayed notice is REVIEW; state log carries verdict | §5.1 |\n | B CLI | default CLI path (no snapshot) fails closed to REVIEW | §5.3, §14.4 |\n-| B CLI | reachable config path (`risk_portfolio`) can APPROVE (implemented by threading through `_build_run_config`) | §14.4 |\n+| A API | Python API `TradingAgentsGraph(config={\"risk_portfolio\": ...})` can APPROVE | §14.4 |\n | B CLI | no actionable BUY published before evaluation (streamed steps) | §5.1 |\n | C data | both structured objects reach the gate | §6 |\n | C data | free-text fallback cannot bypass inputs (still NEEDS_REVIEW) | §5.3 |\n | C data | validation failure → non-actionable + audit record | NFR-A2 |\n | D audit | rule ids/outcomes, snapshot, verdict, policy v/hash, UTC | NFR-A2 |\n | D audit | numeric exposure inputs + derived R2/R3 values present | §5.3, §14.2 |\n | D audit | no credentials/raw prompts | NFR-SEC |\n | D audit | APPROVED, REJECTED, NEEDS_REVIEW all audited | NFR-A2 |\n | D audit | durable-audit failure cannot release an actionable BUY on the stream | §5.1, §14 |\n | E downstream | model recommendation preserved as evidence; distinct from signal | §5.1 |\n | E downstream | blocked BUY not an authorized BUY in report header/memory | §5.1 |\n | F checkpoint | real resume; pre-gate checkpoint re-evaluates | §13.5 |\n | F checkpoint | legacy (pre-gate) signature checkpoint cannot bypass evaluation | §14, §13.5 |\n | G perf | **actual adapter** overhead (conversion+evaluation+audit) p50/p95 ≤ 2000 ms | NFR-A1 |\n | G perf | 0 extra network calls attributable to the gate | NFR-A1 |\n \n ### 9.3 Expected before integration coding\n \n These tests import `tradingagents.risk_gate.adapter` (and, for the durable-audit\n stream test, a proposed `risk_gate._persist_audit`) and the new state keys; The cleanest honest approach: the legacy signature is exactly today's `_run_signature` output (the pre-gate graph), and after integration the gated one differs. 449: ### 14.3 Consequence for tests
450:

453:   `final_rating` on the stream.

460: ...})`) and, for the CLI, requires the implementation to thread `risk_portfolio`
461: through `_build_run_config` (e.g. from a future documented option or config file).
462: Until then the **default CLI path fails closed** (NEEDS_REVIEW → REVIEW). No CLI
463: option is added in this stage.

The **default CLI path** supplies no structured snapshot and therefore\n**fails closed** to `NEEDS_REVIEW` → `REVIEW`. Any future CLI surface would be a\nseparate, explicitly-approved change; no test claims a CLI feature that does not\nexist.\n\nThe durable audit writer is defined by the Stage 2 adapter as\n`tradingagents.risk_gate.adapter.persist_audit(evaluation, ...)`; it must be called\nfor **every** evaluation before the Portfolio Manager publishes an actionable\nrecommendation.",

````text
The three targeted corrections are complete. Only the four approved files changed; production code, the 195 core tests, and shared requirements/CI are untouched.

## 1. Exactly what was corrected

**Gap 1 — CLI configuration claim.**
- `_run_real_cli` no longer injects `risk_portfolio`; its `_build_run_config` wrapper only delegates to the real function and relocates artifacts to the tmp dir (documented as path relocation, not a risk input).
- Removed `test_cli_reachable_config_path_can_approve` (which misdescribed a harness injection as a CLI feature).
- Kept the two real-CLI tests: `test_cli_displays_review_and_records_risk_controlled_result` (real graph, real `record_decision`, captured console shows "recorded for review", state log persists `final_rating=REVIEW`) and `test_cli_default_path_without_snapshot_fails_closed` (`risk_verdict=NEEDS_REVIEW`, `REVIEW`).
- Added `test_python_api_config_supplies_risk_portfolio` — the approved path: `TradingAgentsGraph(config={"risk_portfolio": ...})` → APPROVED/`Buy`/ACTIONABLE.
- ADR §14.4 and test plan §9.2/§9.5 rewritten: Python API is the only supported caller path; no CLI flag/env; default CLI fails closed.

**Gap 2 — Real audit persistence failure injection.**
- `test_audit_failure_does_not_release_actionable_buy_on_stream` now does `monkeypatch.setattr(adapter, "persist_audit", failing_writer, raising=True)` on the **actual** Stage 2 writer (`tradingagents.risk_gate.adapter.persist_audit`); fails RED via `ImportError` while absent.
- The writer increments a counter; the test asserts `calls["n"] >= 1` ("injection unused" otherwise), simulates `OSError`, and asserts no `("Buy","APPROVED")` is ever streamed and no APPROVED verdict surfaces if the run didn't raise.
- ADR §14.3/§14.4 document the boundary: every evaluation must establish its durable audit before publication; failure ⇒ not actionable; writer is `adapter.persist_audit`.

**Gap 3 — Legacy checkpoint.**
- `test_legacy_pre_gate_checkpoint_cannot_bypass_evaluation` now uses the real `thread_id`/`get_checkpointer`/`checkpoint_step`: writes a real checkpoint, asserts `saver.get_tuple(legacy_tid) is not None` (retrievable), asserts `saver.get_tuple(gated_tid) is None`, then `checkpoint_step(...legacy_sig) is not None` while `...(gated_sig) is None`, `gated_tid != legacy_tid`, and finally the gated run evaluates risk (`risk_verdict` set, `risk_evaluation` present). Today it fails at `gated_tid == legacy_tid` — precisely the gap integration must close.

## 2. Actual collection, pass, failure counts
- `ruff check tradingagents/risk_gate tests/risk_gate` → **exit 0** (All checks passed).
- `pytest tests/risk_gate --collect-only -q` → **exit 0**, **223 collected**.
- integration files → **exit 1**, **25 failed, 2 passed**.
- core (excl. 2 integration files) → **195 passed, 1 xpassed** (unchanged).
- `pytest -q --ignore=tests/risk_gate` → **1412 passed, 1 skipped** (unchanged).

## 3. Integration tests remaining RED (25)
All RED for the correct pre-implementation reasons:
- **Adapter absent** (`ImportError`): all `_graph`-based API/retention/audit/downstream/perf/network tests, `test_audit_failure_...`, `test_actual_adapter_overhead_...`.
- **State keys absent** (`KeyError: 'risk_evaluation'`, etc.): valid-buy, missing-stop, missing-info, structured retention, audit persistence.
- **Signature gap**: `test_legacy_pre_gate_checkpoint_cannot_bypass_evaluation` (gated signature equals legacy today).
- **Real CLI**: `test_cli_displays_...` and `test_cli_default_path_...` RED because the gate isn't wired into the PM boundary / state log yet.

The **2 passing** are legitimate baseline-holding checks, not masking: `test_audit_persistence_failure_cannot_leave_actionable_signal` (run raises) and `test_existing_full_run_still_reaches_a_decision` (`[PRESERVE]`).

## 4. Exact proposed integration production files
- `tradingagents/risk_gate/adapter.py` (new): `build_inputs`, `apply_gate`, **`persist_audit`** (durable writer, called for every evaluation before publication).
- `tradingagents/agents/state.py` (additive keys: `trader_proposal`, `portfolio_decision`, `model_rating`, `risk_verdict`, `decision_status`, `risk_evaluation`).
- `tradingagents/agents/trader/trader.py` (return structured `trader_proposal`).
- `tradingagents/agents/managers/portfolio_manager.py` (return `portfolio_decision`; call adapter; set effective `final_rating`).
- `tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py` (`risk_portfolio` via `config`; `risk_gate` layout marker in `_run_signature`; audit persistence + failure guard).
- No changes to the pure engine, `rating.py`, `reporting.py`, `cli/*` semantics, or shared requirements/CI.

## 5. Git diff summary

# Human Approval — FR-A1 Stage 2 Integration Implementation

The Stage 2 integration architecture and the revised
integration acceptance tests have now been reviewed.

I APPROVE the Stage 2 integration test baseline and
authorize the production implementation described below.

The approved tests were committed before implementation.

Current verified baseline:
- 223 FR-A1 tests collected.
- 195 core tests passed, 1 documented XPASS.
- 27 integration tests: 25 failed, 2 passed (RED).
- 1412 original TradingAgents regression tests passed.
- Ruff passed.

Do not restart architecture exploration.

## 1. Approved architecture

Use the Portfolio Manager output boundary as the
single authoritative risk evaluation point.

Do not add a separate LangGraph risk node.

The final model decision must pass through the
deterministic FR-A1 risk gate before any effective
actionable recommendation is published.

Preserve the original AI recommendation as evidence,
separately from the effective public rating.

## 2. Approved production file scope

Create:
- tradingagents/risk_gate/adapter.py

Modify only:
- tradingagents/agents/state.py
- tradingagents/agents/trader/trader.py
- tradingagents/agents/managers/portfolio_manager.py
- tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py

Do not modify the pure risk engine or its policy.

Do not modify CLI, reporting, rating, memory,
checkpoint implementation, shared requirements,
or other team members' feature modules.

## 3. Structured decision integration

Preserve both structured objects in graph state:

- trader_proposal
- portfolio_decision

Retain the existing rendered text for compatibility.

Create an adapter exposing the approved interfaces:

- build_inputs(...)
- apply_gate(...)
- persist_audit(...)

The adapter must:

- Convert structured decisions and caller-supplied
  portfolio data into RiskInputs.
- Invoke evaluate_risk exactly once.
- Reject unsafe substitution of missing or
  unrecognized Trader actions or final ratings.
- Never parse arbitrary Markdown to invent
  missing structured risk inputs.
- Handle missing or malformed inputs safely.
- Preserve the original model rating in model_rating.
- Set the effective final_rating from the risk
  verdict and decision status.

Approved risk evaluation semantics:

APPROVED + actionable BUY:
  final_rating = original valid model rating

REJECTED:
  final_rating = REVIEW
  decision_status = BLOCKED

NEEDS_REVIEW:
  final_rating = REVIEW
  decision_status = PENDING_REVIEW

HOLD:
  must never become ACTIONABLE.

Unsupported SELL/short:
  must not become APPROVED in v1.

## 4. Risk portfolio input

Support the additive Python API configuration:

TradingAgentsGraph(
    config={"risk_portfolio": {
        "snapshot": {...},
        "target_position": {...}
    }}
)

This is the supported complete-input path.

A valid, affordable long BUY with a consistent
snapshot must be capable of becoming APPROVED.

When the structured snapshot is absent:
- Fail closed.
- Do not fabricate values or sector classifications.
- Do not approve the recommendation.

The default CLI has no supported risk_portfolio
input flag and must fail closed to REVIEW.

Do not add CLI flags or environment variables
in this stage.

## 5. Durable audit before publication

Implement the actual durable audit writer:

tradingagents.risk_gate.adapter.persist_audit

The writer must be a real function, used by the
production integration, and independently testable.

For EVERY evaluated decision:

- Establish the required durable audit before the
  Portfolio Manager publishes final_rating.
- Include verdict, decision status, rule IDs and
  outcomes, observed values, thresholds, policy
  version/hash, UTC timestamp and the minimal
  explanatory input snapshot.
- Avoid raw prompts, credentials and unnecessary
  private portfolio details.
- Preserve audit information in the state log.
- Avoid duplicate risk evaluations.

If durable audit persistence fails, the adapter
must not publish an actionable recommendation.

Use the existing project output directories and
safe file operations. Avoid introducing an
unapproved dependency or external service.

## 6. Checkpoint and streaming safety

Add the documented risk-gate layout marker to
the run signature.

A legacy pre-gate checkpoint must not bypass
the newly required risk evaluation.

Streaming consumers must never receive an
actionable final_rating before evaluation and
the required durable audit have completed.

Preserve the existing graph and streaming
interfaces wherever possible.

## 7. Verification

First run:

python -m ruff check tradingagents/risk_gate \
  tradingagents/agents/state.py \
  tradingagents/agents/trader/trader.py \
  tradingagents/agents/managers/portfolio_manager.py \
  tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py \
  tests/risk_gate

Then run:

python -m pytest \
  tests/risk_gate/test_decision_boundary.py \
  tests/risk_gate/test_integration_retention.py -q

Then:

python -m pytest tests/risk_gate -q

Finally:

python -m pytest -q --ignore=tests/risk_gate

Report actual exit codes.

Explicitly verify:
- A complete valid BUY is APPROVED.
- Missing stop-loss is REJECTED.
- Missing portfolio data is NEEDS_REVIEW.
- Both structured objects are preserved.
- The effective public rating is REVIEW when
  the gate does not approve.
- Durable audit exists before publication.
- Audit persistence failure blocks publication.
- CLI and streaming do not bypass the gate.
- Legacy checkpoints cannot bypass evaluation.
- All 100 invalid fixtures remain unapproved.
- Original core safety regressions still pass.
- Adapter-level p50/p95 overhead is measured.
- No additional external network calls are made
  by the risk gate.

## 8. Handling problems

Do not weaken or delete approved tests to make
the implementation appear successful.

If a test is inconsistent with the approved
architecture, show the exact contradiction and
request human review.

If an existing regression test fails because
the intended safety behavior now produces REVIEW
instead of the old model rating, report it as a
possible intentional behavior change.

Do not silently rewrite the original tests.

Fix genuine implementation bugs within the
approved file scope.

## 9. Restrictions

- No work on FR-A2, FR-A3 or other team features.
- No changes to shared requirements or CI.
- No external runtime API calls.
- No dependency installation.
- No commits, pushes or merges.
- No changes outside the approved production scope.

Provide a concise English completion report with:

1. Production files created/modified.
2. How the final decision is enforced.
3. How audit-before-publication is guaranteed.
4. Test results with pass/fail counts and exit codes.
5. Integration p50/p95 latency.
6. Remaining errors, limitations or unresolved
   team decisions.
7. Exact Git status.

STOP after Stage 2 implementation and verification.

Wait for human review before any further changes.

state log\"\n     return json.loads(logs[-1].read_text())\n \n \n @pytest.mark.unit\n def test_cli_displays_review_and_records_risk_controlled_result(tmp_path, monkeypatch, offline):\n         "patch": "Index: tradingagents/agents/managers/portfolio_manager.py\n===================================================================\n--- tradingagents/agents/managers/portfolio_manager.py\t\n+++ tradingagents/agents/managers/portfolio_manager.py\t\n@@ -1,106 +1,139 @@\n \"\"\"Portfolio Manager: synthesises the risk-analyst debate into the final decision.\n \n Uses LangChain's ``with_structured_output`` so the LLM produces a typed\n ``PortfolioDecision`` directly, in a single call. Its rating is the run's\n ``final_rating``, and the decision is rendered to markdown as\n ``final_trade_decision`` for the memory log, CLI display and saved reports.\n When a provider does not expose structured output, the agent falls back to\n free-text generation and the rating is read from that text.\n \"\"\"\n \n from __future__ import annotations\n \n+from pathlib import Path\n+\n from tradingagents.agents.context import (\n     get_instrument_context_from_state,\n     get_language_instruction,\n     get_portfolio_context_from_state,\n )\n-from tradingagents.agents.rating import parse_rating\n from tradingagents.agents.schemas import PortfolioDecision, render_pm_decision\n from tradingagents.agents.structured import NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS, bind_structured, invoke_structured\n+from tradingagents.dataflows.symbols import safe_ticker_component\n \n \n def create_portfolio_manager(llm):\n     structured_llm = bind_structured(llm, PortfolioDecision, \"Portfolio Manager\")\n \n     def portfolio_manager_node(state) -> dict:\n         instrument_context = get_instrument_context_from_state(state)\n         portfolio_context = get_portfolio_context_from_state(state)\n \n         history = state[\"risk_debate_state\"][\"history\"]\n         risk_debate_state = state[\"risk_debate_state\"]\n         research_plan = state[\"investment_plan\"]\n         trader_plan = state[\"trader_investment_plan\"]\n \n         past_context = state.get(\"past_context\", \"\")\n         lessons_line = (\n             f\"- Lessons from prior decisions and outcomes:\\n{past_context}\\n\"\n             if past_context\n             else \"\"\n         )\n \n         prompt = f\"\"\"As the Portfolio Manager, synthesize the risk analysts' debate and deliver the final trading decision.\n \n {instrument_context}\n \n {portfolio_context}\n \n ---\n \n **Rating Scale** (use exactly one):\n - **Buy**: Strong conviction to enter or add to position\n - **Overweight**: Favorable outlook, gradually increase exposure\n - **Hold**: Maintain current position, no action needed\n - **Underweight**: Reduce exposure, take partial profits\n - **Sell**: Exit position or avoid entry\n \n **Context:**\n - Research Manager's investment plan: **{research_plan}**\n - Trader's transaction proposal: **{trader_plan}**\n {lessons_line}\n **Risk Analysts Debate History:**\n {history}\n \n ---\n \n Ground every conclusion in specific evidence from the analysts. The risk debate always contains conflicting stances; deciding which is stronger is the job, so conflict alone is not a reason to Hold. Commit to the stronger case, sized by how decisively it wins. Choose Hold only when the evidence is still balanced after that weighing, or too thin to support a call; do not force a direction to appear decisive. Weigh the analysts on their merits, independent of speaking order.\n \n ## Output\n \n Write these sections, in this order, starting with the rating on its own line:\n \n - **Rating**: exactly one of Buy / Overweight / Hold / Underweight / Sell\n - **Executive Summary**: the call and how to act on it\n - **Investment Thesis**: the evidence that decided it, and what would change it\n \n {NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS}{get_language_instruction()}\"\"\"\n \n-        # The typed rating is the decision; the rendered text only carries it.\n-        # Read back from text, a rating the thesis quotes could replace it.\n+        # The typed rating is the decision; the rendered text only carries it. A\n+        # rating the thesis quotes must not replace it. The effective rating is set\n+        # by the FR-A1 gate below, not here.\n         decision = invoke_structured(structured_llm, prompt, \"Portfolio Manager\")\n         if decision is not None:\n             final_trade_decision = render_pm_decision(decision)\n-            final_rating = decision.rating.value\n         else:\n             final_trade_decision = llm.invoke(prompt).content\n-            final_rating = parse_rating(final_trade_decision)\n \n         new_risk_debate_state = {\n             \"history\": risk_debate_state[\"history\"],\n             \"aggressive_history\": risk_debate_state[\"aggressive_history\"],\n             \"conservative_history\": risk_debate_state[\"conservative_history\"],\n             \"neutral_history\": risk_debate_state[\"neutral_history\"],\n             \"latest_speaker\": \"Judge\",\n             \"current_aggressive_response\": risk_debate_state[\"current_aggressive_response\"],\n             \"current_conservative_response\": risk_debate_state[\"current_conservative_response\"],\n             \"current_neutral_response\": risk_debate_state[\"current_neutral_response\"],\n             \"count\": risk_debate_state[\"count\"],\n         }\n \n+        # FR-A1: the single authoritative risk evaluation runs at this output\n+        # boundary, before any effective actionable rating is published. The model\n+        # rating is preserved in model_rating; final_rating becomes the effective\n+        # public signal (REVIEW unless APPROVED).\n+        from tradingagents.dataflows.config import get_config\n+        from tradingagents.risk_gate.adapter import apply_gate\n+\n+        cfg = get_config()\n+        ticker = state.get(\"company_of_interest\", \"\")\n+        trade_date = state.get(\"trade_date\", \"\")\n+        audit_dir = None\n+        try:\n+            results_dir = cfg.get(\"results_dir\")\n+            if results_dir and ticker:\n+                audit_dir = (Path(results_dir) / safe_ticker_component(ticker) / \"risk_audit\")\n+        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - audit_dir is best-effort location only\n+            audit_dir = None\n+\n+        gate = apply_gate(\n+            ticker,\n+            trade_date,\n+            state.get(\"trader_proposal\"),\n+            decision,\n+            cfg.get(\"risk_portfolio\"),\n+            audit_dir=audit_dir,\n+        )\n+\n         return {\n             \"risk_debate_state\": new_risk_debate_state,\n             \"final_trade_decision\": final_trade_decision,\n-            \"final_rating\": final_rating,\n+            \"portfolio_decision\": decision,\n+            \"model_rating\": gate[\"model_rating\"],\n+            \"final_rating\": gate[\"final_rating\"],\n+            \"risk_verdict\": gate[\"risk_verdict\"],\n+            \"decision_status\": gate[\"decision_status\"],\n+            \"risk_evaluation\": gate[\"risk_evaluation\"],\n         }\n \n     return portfolio_manager_node\n",

        "patch": "Index: tradingagents/agents/trader/trader.py\n===================================================================\n--- tradingagents/agents/trader/trader.py\t\n+++ tradingagents/agents/trader/trader.py\t\n@@ -1,98 +1,100 @@\n \"\"\"Trader: turns the Research Manager's investment plan into a concrete transaction proposal.\"\"\"\n \n from __future__ import annotations\n \n from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage\n \n from tradingagents.agents.context import (\n     get_instrument_context_from_state,\n     get_language_instruction,\n     get_portfolio_context_from_state,\n )\n from tradingagents.agents.schemas import TraderProposal, render_trader_proposal\n from tradingagents.agents.structured import (\n     NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS,\n     bind_structured,\n-    invoke_structured_or_freetext,\n+    invoke_structured,\n )\n \n \n def create_trader(llm):\n     structured_llm = bind_structured(llm, TraderProposal, \"Trader\")\n \n     def trader_node(state):\n         company_name = state[\"company_of_interest\"]\n         instrument_context = get_instrument_context_from_state(state)\n         investment_plan = state[\"investment_plan\"]\n         # The research plan digests the debate but loses exact price structure;\n         # give the Trader the technical market report so entry/stop levels are\n         # grounded in real ATR / support-resistance / current price (#1167). The\n         # report is empty when the user did not select the market analyst, so\n         # only offer it (and the grounding instruction) when it has content.\n         market_report = (state[\"market_report\"] or \"\").strip()\n         portfolio_context = get_portfolio_context_from_state(state)\n \n         if market_report:\n             grounding = (\n                 \"Ground concrete price levels (entry, stop-loss, position sizing) in the technical \"\n                 \"market report's price structure -- current price, support/resistance, ATR, and \"\n                 \"volatility -- and use the research plan for direction and strategy. \"\n             )\n             report_section = f\"Technical Market Report:\\n{market_report}\\n\\n\"\n         else:\n             grounding = \"\"\n             report_section = \"\"\n \n         messages = [\n             {\n                 \"role\": \"system\",\n                 \"content\": (\n                     \"You are a trading agent analyzing market data to make investment decisions. \"\n                     \"Based on your analysis, provide a specific recommendation to buy, sell, or hold. \"\n                     + grounding\n                     # Entry/stop are numeric price fields. Asking for concrete\n                     # levels invites a percentage (\"15%\"), which is not a price\n                     # and fails the structured parse (#1288).\n                     + \"State entry price and stop-loss as absolute price levels in the \"\n                     \"instrument's quote currency (for example 189.5), never a percentage \"\n                     \"or a range; convert a percentage distance to the price level it \"\n                     \"implies, or omit the field if you cannot state a number. \"\n                     + NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS\n                     + get_language_instruction()\n                 ),\n             },\n             {\n                 \"role\": \"user\",\n                 \"content\": (\n                     f\"Here is the research team's investment plan for {company_name}. \"\n                     f\"{instrument_context}\\n\\n\"\n                     f\"{report_section}\"\n                     f\"{portfolio_context}\\n\\n\"\n                     f\"Proposed Investment Plan:\\n{investment_plan}\\n\\n\"\n                     \"Make an informed, strategic trading decision.\\n\\n\"\n                     \"## Output\\n\\n\"\n                     \"Write these sections, in this order, starting with the action \"\n                     \"on its own line:\\n\\n\"\n                     \"- **Action**: exactly one of Buy / Hold / Sell. A research \"\n                     \"recommendation of Overweight is a Buy and Underweight is a Sell, \"\n                     \"sized by how strong the case is; conflict alone is not a Hold.\\n\"\n                     \"- **Reasoning**: why, against the plan and the price structure\\n\"\n                     \"- **Entry Price**, **Stop Loss**, **Position Sizing**: when you can state them\"\n                 ),\n             },\n         ]\n \n-        trader_plan = invoke_structured_or_freetext(\n-            structured_llm,\n-            llm,\n-            messages,\n-            render_trader_proposal,\n-            \"Trader\",\n-        )\n+        # Run the structured call and keep the typed object so the FR-A1 risk gate\n+        # has structured inputs; fall back to free text (proposal None) without\n+        # letting that bypass the gate (it will fail closed).\n+        proposal = invoke_structured(structured_llm, messages, \"Trader\")\n+        if proposal is not None:\n+            trader_plan = render_trader_proposal(proposal)\n+        else:\n+            trader_plan = llm.invoke(messages).content\n \n         return {\n             \"messages\": [AIMessage(content=trader_plan)],\n             \"trader_investment_plan\": trader_plan,\n+            \"trader_proposal\": proposal,\n         }\n \n     return trader_node\n",
        "additions": 10,
        "deletions": 8,
        "status": "modified"
      },

        "file": "tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py",
        "patch": "Index: tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py\n===================================================================\n--- tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py\t\n+++ tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py\t\n@@ -1,476 +1,494 @@\n import hashlib\n import json\n import logging\n import os\n from contextlib import contextmanager\n from datetime import datetime\n from pathlib import Path\n from typing import Any\n \n import tradingagents\n from tradingagents.agents.context import build_instrument_context, resolve_instrument_identity\n from tradingagents.agents.rating import run_rating\n from tradingagents.dataflows.config import run_config, run_config_context, set_config\n from tradingagents.dataflows.date_window import get_current_date, is_historical\n from tradingagents.dataflows.symbols import safe_ticker_component\n from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG\n from tradingagents.llm_clients import create_tier_client, tier_provider\n from tradingagents.memory import TradingMemoryLog, settlement\n from tradingagents.memory.reflection import Reflector\n from tradingagents.reporting import write_report_tree\n \n from .checkpointer import checkpoint_step, clear_checkpoint, get_checkpointer, thread_id\n from .conditional_logic import ConditionalLogic\n from .propagation import Propagator\n from .setup import GraphSetup\n \n logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n \n \n def _validate_trade_date(trade_date) -> str:\n     \"\"\"The run date as a canonical ``YYYY-MM-DD`` string no later than today.\"\"\"\n     value = str(trade_date)\n     try:\n         canonical = datetime.strptime(value, \"%Y-%m-%d\").strftime(\"%Y-%m-%d\") == value\n     except ValueError:\n         canonical = False\n     if not canonical:\n         raise ValueError(f\"trade_date must be a date in YYYY-MM-DD format, got {trade_date!r}\")\n     if value > get_current_date():\n         raise ValueError(f\"trade_date cannot be in the future: {value}\")\n     return value\n \n \n # Config keys that do not change what a run writes: where it keeps its files,\n # whether it checkpoints, and how often it retries a provider.\n _NOT_IN_SIGNATURE = frozenset({\n     \"results_dir\", \"data_cache_dir\", \"memory_log_path\", \"checkpoint_enabled\", \"llm_max_retries\",\n })\n \n \n class TradingAgentsGraph:\n     \"\"\"Main class that orchestrates the trading agents framework.\"\"\"\n \n     def __init__(\n         self,\n         selected_analysts=(\"market\", \"social\", \"news\", \"fundamentals\"),\n         debug=False,\n         config: dict[str, Any] = None,\n         callbacks: list | None = None,\n     ):\n         \"\"\"Initialize the trading agents graph and components.\n \n         Args:\n             selected_analysts: List of analyst types to include\n             debug: Whether to run in debug mode\n             config: Configuration dictionary. If None, uses default config\n             callbacks: Optional list of callback handlers (e.g., for tracking LLM/tool stats)\n         \"\"\"\n         self.debug = debug\n         self.config = config or DEFAULT_CONFIG\n         self.callbacks = callbacks or []\n \n         set_config(self.config)\n \n         os.makedirs(self.config[\"data_cache_dir\"], exist_ok=True)\n         os.makedirs(self.config[\"results_dir\"], exist_ok=True)\n \n         extra = {\"callbacks\": self.callbacks} if self.callbacks else {}\n         self.deep_thinking_llm = create_tier_client(self.config, \"deep\", **extra).get_llm()\n         self.quick_thinking_llm = create_tier_client(self.config, \"quick\", **extra).get_llm()\n \n         self.memory_log = TradingMemoryLog(self.config)\n \n         self.conditional_logic = ConditionalLogic(\n             max_debate_rounds=self.config[\"max_debate_rounds\"],\n             max_risk_discuss_rounds=self.config[\"max_risk_discuss_rounds\"],\n         )\n         # An analyst takes two graph steps per tool round, plus its first turn\n         # and its wrap-up; a limit past the recursion limit would end the run\n         # there instead.\n         max_tool_rounds, max_recur_limit = self.config[\"max_tool_rounds\"], self.config[\"max_recur_limit\"]\n         if 2 * max_tool_rounds + 2 >= max_recur_limit:\n             raise ValueError(\n                 f\"max_tool_rounds={max_tool_rounds} needs max_recur_limit above {2 * max_tool_rounds + 2}\"\n             )\n         self.graph_setup = GraphSetup(\n             self.quick_thinking_llm,\n             self.deep_thinking_llm,\n             self.conditional_logic,\n             max_tool_rounds,\n         )\n \n         self.propagator = Propagator(\n             max_recur_limit=max_recur_limit,\n         )\n         self.reflector = Reflector(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n \n         # Graph-shape-affecting run choices, kept for the checkpoint signature.\n         self.selected_analysts = tuple(selected_analysts)\n \n         # Set up the graph: keep the workflow for recompilation with a checkpointer.\n         self.workflow = self.graph_setup.setup_graph(selected_analysts, memory_node=self._memory_step)\n         self.graph = self.workflow.compile()\n         self._checkpointer_ctx = None\n         self._resuming = False\n \n     def resolve_instrument_context(self, ticker: str, asset_type: str = \"stock\",\n                                    trade_date: str | None = None) -> str:\n         \"\"\"Resolve ticker identity once and return the full instrument context.\n \n         Deterministic yfinance lookup (cached, fail-open) injected into a\n         context string so every agent anchors to the real company instead of\n         hallucinating one from the price chart (#814). Both the propagate()\n         path and the CLI call this so the resolved identity reaches the whole\n         graph regardless of entry point.\n         \"\"\"\n         identity = resolve_instrument_identity(ticker)\n         return build_instrument_context(ticker, asset_type, identity, trade_date)\n \n     def _memory_as_of(self, trade_date) -> str | None:\n         \"\"\"Point-in-time cutoff for past-context lessons (#1251).\n \n         A historical/backtest run (trade date before today) filters lessons to\n         those already resolved by the trade date. A current-date run returns\n         None, disabling the filter so live behavior and pre-migration entries\n         (which have no stored resolution date) are unaffected.\n         \"\"\"\n         return str(trade_date) if is_historical(trade_date) else None\n \n     def _run_signature(self, asset_type: str, portfolio=None) -> str:\n         \"\"\"Run inputs that must invalidate a checkpoint if changed.\n \n         Keyed into the checkpoint thread ID so a resume under a different analyst\n         selection, debate/risk depth, or asset mode starts fresh instead of\n         silently continuing the previous graph (#1089). The rest of the config\n         counts too (provider, models, endpoint, language, vendors, limits): a\n         resume must not carry reports that other settings produced. Only where\n         the run keeps its files and how it retries are left out.\n         \"\"\"\n         settings = {k: v for k, v in self.config.items() if k not in _NOT_IN_SIGNATURE}\n         digest = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(settings, sort_keys=True, default=str).encode()).hexdigest()[:12]\n         return \"|\".join([\n             \"analysts=\" + \",\".join(self.selected_analysts),\n             f\"debate={self.config['max_debate_rounds']}\",\n             f\"risk={self.config['max_risk_discuss_rounds']}\",\n             f\"asset={asset_type}\",\n             # None, an empty book and a changed book are three different runs.\n             f\"portfolio={portfolio.fingerprint() if portfolio is not None else 'none'}\",\n             # The layout itself: a checkpoint saved when analysts ran one after\n             # another has pending nodes this graph no longer has, and one saved\n             # before the Memory Log step would resume without the lessons.\n             \"analysts=parallel\",\n             \"memory=parallel\",\n+            # The FR-A1 risk gate runs at the Portfolio Manager boundary; a\n+            # checkpoint saved before it must not resume into the gated graph, so\n+            # it starts fresh and is evaluated (ADR §13.5/§14).\n+            \"risk_gate=v1\",\n             f\"settings={digest}\",\n         ])\n \n     def propagate(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = \"stock\", portfolio=None):\n         \"\"\"Run the trading agents graph for a company on a specific date.\n \n         ``asset_type`` selects between the stock pipeline (default) and the\n         crypto pipeline (``\"crypto\"``) shipped in #567 — the CLI auto-detects\n         from the ticker; programmatic callers pass it explicitly. When\n         ``checkpoint_enabled`` is set in config, the graph is recompiled with\n         a per-ticker SqliteSaver so a crashed run can resume from the last\n         successful node on a subsequent invocation with the same ticker+date.\n \n         Returns ``(final_state, signal)`` where ``signal`` is one of the 5-tier\n         ratings (Buy / Overweight / Hold / Underweight / Sell) or ``\"REVIEW\"``\n         when the decision had no parseable rating (#1170); guard with\n         ``tradingagents.agents.rating.is_review`` before mapping it to the\n         PortfolioRating enum.\n         \"\"\"\n         trade_date = _validate_trade_date(trade_date)\n \n         with run_config(self.config), \\\n                 self.checkpoint_scope(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio) as thread_id_value:\n             return self._run_graph(\n                 company_name, trade_date, asset_type=asset_type,\n                 checkpoint_thread_id=thread_id_value, portfolio=portfolio,\n             )\n \n     def begin_checkpoint(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = \"stock\", portfolio=None) -> str | None:\n         \"\"\"Recompile the graph with a per-ticker checkpointer and return the\n         ``thread_id`` to inject into the stream/invoke ``config`` (or ``None``\n         when checkpointing is disabled).\n \n         Pair every call with :meth:`end_checkpoint` in a ``finally``. Both\n         ``propagate`` (via :meth:`checkpoint_scope`) and the CLI stream path use\n         this so ``--checkpoint`` actually resumes (#1249); previously the setup\n         lived only inside ``propagate`` and the CLI streamed the checkpointer-less\n         graph, making the flag a no-op.\n         \"\"\"\n         self._resuming = False\n         if not self.config.get(\"checkpoint_enabled\"):\n             return None\n         signature = self._run_signature(asset_type, portfolio)\n         self._checkpointer_ctx = get_checkpointer(self.config[\"data_cache_dir\"], company_name)\n         saver = self._checkpointer_ctx.__enter__()\n         self.graph = self.workflow.compile(checkpointer=saver)\n \n         step = checkpoint_step(\n             self.config[\"data_cache_dir\"], company_name, str(trade_date), signature\n         )\n         self._resuming = step is not None\n         if step is not None:\n             logger.info(\"Resuming from step %d for %s on %s\", step, company_name, trade_date)\n         else:\n             logger.info(\"Starting fresh for %s on %s\", company_name, trade_date)\n         return thread_id(company_name, str(trade_date), signature)\n \n     def checkpoint_input(self, init_state):\n         \"\"\"The value to stream/invoke: ``None`` to resume an existing checkpoint,\n         else the initial state for a fresh run.\n \n         LangGraph resumes an interrupted thread when invoked with ``None``;\n         re-passing the initial state instead appends it through the message\n         reducer, duplicating messages in the resumed state (#1249).\n         \"\"\"\n         return None if self._resuming else init_state\n \n     def end_checkpoint(self):\n         \"\"\"Restore the plain uncheckpointed graph after a checkpointed run.\"\"\"\n         if self._checkpointer_ctx is not None:\n             self._checkpointer_ctx.__exit__(None, None, None)\n             self._checkpointer_ctx = None\n             self.graph = self.workflow.compile()\n         self._resuming = False\n \n     @contextmanager\n     def checkpoint_scope(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = \"stock\", portfolio=None):\n         \"\"\"Context-manager form of begin/end_checkpoint for the propagate path.\"\"\"\n         try:\n             yield self.begin_checkpoint(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)\n         finally:\n             self.end_checkpoint()\n \n     def clear_checkpoint_on_success(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = \"stock\", portfolio=None):\n         \"\"\"Drop a completed run's checkpoint so a later run starts fresh (#1249).\"\"\"\n         if self.config.get(\"checkpoint_enabled\"):\n             clear_checkpoint(\n                 self.config[\"data_cache_dir\"], company_name, str(trade_date),\n                 self._run_signature(asset_type, portfolio),\n             )\n \n     def run_settings(self) -> dict:\n         \"\"\"What produces this graph's runs, for the saved report and state log.\n \n         An allowlist: endpoints (a backend_url can carry credentials), keys and\n         local paths are never recorded.\n         \"\"\"\n         cfg = self.config\n         return {\n             \"version\": tradingagents.__version__,\n             \"llm_provider\": cfg.get(\"llm_provider\"),\n             \"deep_think_provider\": tier_provider(cfg, \"deep\") if cfg.get(\"llm_provider\") else None,\n             \"deep_think_llm\": cfg.get(\"deep_think_llm\"),\n             \"quick_think_provider\": tier_provider(cfg, \"quick\") if cfg.get(\"llm_provider\") else None,\n             \"quick_think_llm\": cfg.get(\"quick_think_llm\"),\n             \"analysts\": list(self.selected_analysts),\n             \"max_debate_rounds\": cfg.get(\"max_debate_rounds\"),\n             \"max_risk_discuss_rounds\": cfg.get(\"max_risk_discuss_rounds\"),\n             \"output_language\": cfg.get(\"output_language\"),\n             \"data_vendors\": dict(cfg.get(\"data_vendors\") or {}),\n             \"tool_vendors\": dict(cfg.get(\"tool_vendors\") or {}),\n         }\n \n     def save_reports(self, final_state, ticker, save_path=None, html=True) -> Path:\n         \"\"\"Write the report tree for a completed run, like the CLI does.\n \n         Programmatic callers get the same on-disk reports the CLI produces. Pass\n         an explicit ``save_path`` or let it default under ``results_dir``; the\n         report is also written as one HTML page unless ``html`` is False.\n         \"\"\"\n         if save_path is None:\n             save_path = self.default_report_path(ticker)\n         return write_report_tree(final_state, ticker, save_path, settings=self.run_settings(), html=html)\n \n     def default_report_path(self, ticker) -> Path:\n         \"\"\"Where a run's reports go unless told otherwise: under results_dir, stamped now.\"\"\"\n         stamp = datetime.now().strftime(\"%Y%m%d_%H%M%S\")\n         return Path(self.config[\"results_dir\"]) / \"reports\" / f\"{safe_ticker_component(ticker)}_{stamp}\"\n \n     def create_run_state(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = \"stock\", portfolio=None):\n         \"\"\"Build a run's initial state; propagate() and the CLI both start here.\n \n         Injects the resolved instrument identity for every agent (#814). The\n         memory log's lessons are not here: the graph's Memory Log step settles\n         and loads them alongside the analysts (see ``_memory_step``).\n         \"\"\"\n         trade_date = _validate_trade_date(trade_date)\n         return self.propagator.create_initial_state(\n             company_name,\n             trade_date,\n             asset_type=asset_type,\n             instrument_context=self.resolve_instrument_context(company_name, asset_type, trade_date),\n             portfolio_context=portfolio.render(company_name) if portfolio is not None else \"\",\n         )\n \n     def _memory_step(self, state):\n         \"\"\"The graph's Memory Log step, alongside the analysts (#1428): settle every\n         ticker's due decisions (#1445), then return the lessons known by the\n         trade date for the Portfolio Manager (#1251).\n \n         Settling fetches prices and asks the model for a reflection per decision,\n         so it runs beside the analysts instead of before them. A failure here\n         does not end the run: the analysts' work is kept, the lessons already in\n         the log are used, and the report says what could not be settled.\n         \"\"\"\n         note = \"\"\n         try:\n             # Another run settling the same log does the work; this one goes on.\n             done = self.settle_all_pending(wait=False)\n             if done.failed:\n                 note = (f\"{len(done.failed)} past decision(s) could not be settled this run \"\n                         \"and stay pending.\")\n         except Exception as exc:\n             logger.warning(\"Settling past decisions failed: %s\", exc)\n             note = f\"Past decisions could not be settled this run ({type(exc).__name__}); they stay pending.\"\n         try:\n             past_context = self.memory_log.get_past_context(\n                 state[\"company_of_interest\"], as_of=self._memory_as_of(state[\"trade_date\"]))\n         except Exception as exc:\n             logger.warning(\"Reading the memory log failed: %s\", exc)\n             past_context = \"\"\n             note = note or f\"The memory log could not be read this run ({type(exc).__name__}).\"\n         return {\"past_context\": past_context, \"memory_note\": note}\n \n     def settle_pending(self, company_name) -> settlement.Settlement:\n         \"\"\"Settle this ticker's decisions whose holding window has now traded.\n \n         A run settles every due decision alongside its analysts, so its own\n         decision stays pending until a later run. A caller that is done\n         analyzing a ticker (a backtest sweep, a scheduled job) calls this to\n         settle it now. Returns what was settled and what failed.\n         \"\"\"\n         with run_config(self.config):\n             return settlement.settle_pending(company_name, self.memory_log, self.reflector, self.config)\n \n     def settle_all_pending(self, wait: bool = True) -> settlement.Settlement:\n         \"\"\"Settle every ticker's decisions whose holding window has now traded (#1445).\n \n         For a scheduler whose tickers rotate: a ticker it stops analysing would\n         otherwise keep its decisions pending, and their lessons out of later runs.\n         With ``wait=False`` a pass already running on the same log is not waited for.\n         \"\"\"\n         with run_config(self.config):\n             return settlement.settle_all_pending(self.memory_log, self.reflector, self.config, wait=wait)\n \n     def record_decision(self, company_name, trade_date, final_state):\n         \"\"\"Record a finished run: its state log, and its decision in the memory log\n         for reflection on the next same-ticker run. propagate() and the CLI both end here.\"\"\"\n         self._log_state(trade_date, final_state)\n         decision = final_state.get(\"final_trade_decision\")\n         if not decision:\n             logger.warning(\"No final decision for %s on %s; nothing added to the memory log\",\n                            company_name, trade_date)\n             return\n         self.memory_log.store_decision(\n             ticker=company_name, trade_date=trade_date, final_trade_decision=decision,\n             rating=run_rating(final_state),\n         )\n \n     def _run_graph(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = \"stock\",\n                    checkpoint_thread_id: str | None = None, portfolio=None):\n         \"\"\"Execute the graph and write the resulting state to disk and memory log.\"\"\"\n         init_agent_state = self.create_run_state(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)\n         args = self.propagator.get_graph_args()\n \n         # Inject the checkpoint thread_id (from checkpoint_scope) so the same\n         # ticker+date+graph-shape resumes; a different one starts fresh (#1089).\n         if checkpoint_thread_id is not None:\n             args.setdefault(\"config\", {}).setdefault(\"configurable\", {})[\"thread_id\"] = checkpoint_thread_id\n \n         # None resumes an existing checkpoint; init_agent_state starts fresh (#1249).\n         graph_input = self.checkpoint_input(init_agent_state)\n         if self.debug:\n             # A state repeats the messages before it, so each prints once (#1027).\n             final_state, printed = {}, set()\n             for messages, state in self.stream_run(graph_input, **args):\n                 for msg in messages:\n                     key = getattr(msg, \"id\", None) or (type(msg).__name__, getattr(msg, \"content\", None))\n                     if key not in printed:\n                         printed.add(key)\n                         msg.pretty_print()\n                 if state is not None:\n                     final_state.update(state)\n         else:\n             final_state = self.graph.invoke(graph_input, **args)\n \n         self.record_decision(company_name, trade_date, final_state)\n \n         # Clear checkpoint on successful completion to avoid stale state.\n         self.clear_checkpoint_on_success(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)\n \n         return final_state, run_rating(final_state)\n \n     def stream_run(self, graph_input, **args):\n         \"\"\"Stream a run as ``(messages, state)`` pairs.\n \n         ``messages`` are the agents' messages, the analysts' included. ``state``\n         is the run's state after a top-level step; for a step inside an analyst's\n         graph it is that analyst's report once filed, else None.\n \n         Each analyst works in a graph of its own, and the run's state takes the\n         analysts' reports only when the slowest has finished, so their messages\n         and reports come from their own finished steps (\"tasks\") as they happen.\n         \"\"\"\n         args = {**args, \"stream_mode\": [\"values\", \"tasks\"]}\n         # The graph's own config serves every tool call, as in propagate(), even\n         # when the process-wide config has changed since. Each step runs in the\n         # run's context, so the caller keeps its own between steps.\n         context = run_config_context(self.config)\n         stream = context.run(self.graph.stream, graph_input, subgraphs=True, **args)\n         try:\n             while (step := context.run(next, stream, None)) is not None:\n                 namespace, mode, chunk = step\n                 if namespace:\n                     result = chunk.get(\"result\") if mode == \"tasks\" else None\n                     if isinstance(result, dict):\n                         report = {k: v for k, v in result.items() if k != \"messages\" and v}\n                         if result.get(\"messages\") or report:\n                             yield result.get(\"messages\", []), report or None\n                 elif mode == \"values\":\n                     yield chunk.get(\"messages\", []), chunk\n         finally:\n             context.run(stream.close)\n \n     def _log_state(self, trade_date, final_state):\n         \"\"\"Write a run's final state to JSON under the run's own ticker.\"\"\"\n         entry = {\n             \"company_of_interest\": final_state[\"company_of_interest\"],\n             \"trade_date\": final_state[\"trade_date\"],\n             \"market_report\": final_state[\"market_report\"],\n             \"sentiment_report\": final_state[\"sentiment_report\"],\n             \"news_report\": final_state[\"news_report\"],\n             \"fundamentals_report\": final_state[\"fundamentals_report\"],\n             \"investment_debate_state\": {\n                 \"bull_history\": final_state[\"investment_debate_state\"][\"bull_history\"],\n                 \"bear_history\": final_state[\"investment_debate_state\"][\"bear_history\"],\n                 \"history\": final_state[\"investment_debate_state\"][\"history\"],\n                 \"current_response\": final_state[\"investment_debate_state\"][\n                     \"current_response\"\n
