# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A. Programmatic API
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_valid_buy_with_complete_inputs_is_approved(tmp_path, monkeypatch, offline):
    """[SAFETY] A valid BUY with a complete snapshot is APPROVED and actionable."""
    graph = _graph(tmp_path, monkeypatch, _buy_proposal(), _buy_decision(),
                   risk_portfolio=RISK_PORTFOLIO)
    state, signal = graph.propagate("NVDA", e2e.TRADE_DATE)

    assert state["risk_verdict"] == "APPROVED"
    assert state["decision_status"] == "ACTIONABLE"
    assert signal == "Buy"                       # effective public signal is the model rating
    assert state["model_rating"] == "Buy"        # preserved as evidence


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_missing_stop_loss_is_rejected_and_review(tmp_path, monkeypatch, offline):
    """[SAFETY] INV-A1: a BUY without a stop-loss is REJECTED and REVIEW."""
    graph = _graph(tmp_path, monkeypatch, _buy_proposal(stop_loss=None), _buy_decision(),
                   risk_portfolio=RISK_PORTFOLIO)
    state, signal = graph.propagate("NVDA", e2e.TRADE_DATE)

    assert state["risk_verdict"] == "REJECTED"
    assert state["decision_status"] == "BLOCKED"
    assert signal == RATING_REVIEW
    assert state["model_rating"] == "Buy"        # original recommendation retained


@pytest.mark.unit
def test_missing_required_information_is_needs_review_and_review(tmp_path, monkeypatch, offline):
    """[SAFETY] Without the structured snapshot the gate fails closed: REVIEW."""
    graph = _graph(tmp_path, monkeypatch, _buy_proposal(), _buy_decision(),
                   risk_portfolio=None)           # nothing supplied -> incomplete inputs
    state, signal = graph.propagate("NVDA", e2e.TRADE_DATE)

    assert state["risk_verdict"] == "NEEDS_REVIEW"
    assert state["decision_status"] == "PENDING_REVIEW"
    assert signal == RATING_REVIEW
    assert state["model_rating"] == "Buy"

{
  "content": "# FR-A1 Demo — Deterministic Risk Gate (Reproducible, Offline)\n\nThis folder reproduces the FR-A1 risk-gate behaviour on deterministic local data.\nIt uses the **real** implementation (`tradingagents.risk_gate`) and, for the\nfull-graph section, the repository's existing offline scripted-model test\ninfrastructure. There is **no network, no external API, and no LLM call**.\n\n- `run_demo.py` — the runnable demonstration script.\n- `demo-output.txt` — the verbatim captured output of running the script.\n\n## How to reproduce\n\nFrom the repository root:\n\n```bash\npython docs/evidence/fr-a1/demo/run_demo.py\n```\n\nRecommended environment note: the script pins the repository root on `sys.path`\nso the full-graph section can import `tests.test_graph_end_to_end`. It needs only\nthe project's own dependencies (already required by the repository).\n\n## What is shown\n\n### Section 1 — adapter-level demonstrations\n\nCalls `tradingagents.risk_gate.adapter.apply_gate(...)` directly with deterministic\n`TraderProposal`, `PortfolioDecision`, and `risk_portfolio` inputs. For each case it\nreports:\n\n- original AI model rating (`model_rating`, preserved as evidence),\n- **core rule verdict** (`risk_evaluation.verdict` — the policy outcome),\n- **effective publication verdict** (`risk_verdict`),\n- final public rating (`final_rating`),\n- decision status,\n- triggered / unknown rules,\n- audit persistence result (a real JSON file written to a temporary directory).\n\n| Case | Scenario | Expected outcome |\n|---|---|---|\n| A | Valid BUY with complete risk inputs | APPROVED / ACTIONABLE, `final_rating` = Buy |\n| B | BUY without stop-loss | REJECTED / BLOCKED, `final_rating` = REVIEW (R1 VIOLATED) |\n| C | BUY without portfolio snapshot | NEEDS_REVIEW / PENDING_REVIEW, REVIEW (R2/R3 UNKNOWN) |\n| D | Single-name concentration over 10% (12%) | REJECTED / BLOCKED (R2 VIOLATED) |\n| E | Conflicting sector classification | never APPROVED; NEEDS_REVIEW (R3 UNKNOWN) |\n| F | Audit persistence failure | fail-closed exception; no actionable output |\n| G | No audit destination (would-be APPROVED) | downgraded to NEEDS_REVIEW / PENDING_REVIEW, REVIEW |\n\n### Section 2 — full-graph integration\n\nRuns the real `TradingAgentsGraph` with the offline scripted model and a supplied\n`risk_portfolio`, proving the decision boundary end-to-end (effective signal,\npreserved `model_rating`, both structured objects retained). If the environment\ncannot import the test infrastructure, this section reports that fact honestly and\nthe adapter-level results above remain the authoritative evidence.\n\n## Deterministic data\n\nThe portfolio fixtures are fixed, internally consistent books:\n\n- Valid book: `portfolio_value = 1,000,000 = cash 830,000 + NVDA 20,000 + MSFT\n  150,000`; NVDA target weight `0.05` → projected `50,000` (an affordable\n  `+30,000` increase); projected Technology `= 170,000 - 20,000 + 50,000 =\n  200,000` (20% ≤ 30%).\n- Conflicting-sector book: real Technology `300,000` (30%); buying NVDA raises it\n  to `350,000` (35%), while the supplied target sector is `Energy` — a conflict\n  that must not be allowed to hide the concentration.\n\n## Important distinctions\n\n- **Core rule verdict vs publication verdict.** `risk_evaluation.verdict` is the\n  policy outcome of the rules. `risk_verdict` is the *effective publication*\n  outcome, which additionally requires a durable audit. Case G shows core rules\n  APPROVED but publication NEEDS_REVIEW because no audit was written.\n- **Durability caveat.** `persist_audit` writes and closes a JSON file; it does not\n  `fsync`.   "content": "# FR-A1 D5 — Session Transcript Integrity\n\nThe course requires a **full raw AI coding-agent session transcript with human\nannotations**. This document identifies where the raw records actually live and how\nto preserve them. It does **not** contain a synthetic transcript, and it does **not**\nclaim the D5 submission is complete unless the raw export below has been produced.\n\n## Where the raw OpenCode session records live\n\nOpenCode stores sessions locally in a SQLite database and accompanying logs:\n\n- Database: `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`\n  - Tables relevant to a transcript: `session`, `message`, `part`\n    (`part` holds the JSON `data` for each message part — text, tool calls, tool\n    results, reasoning, etc.),\n  - plus `session_message` linking messages to sessions.\n- Runtime log: `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log` (the active file observed\n  was `opencode.log`, ~2 MB at the time of this review).\n- Snapshots: `~/.local/share/opencode/snapshot/`.\n\nRaw sessions observed in the database for this work (read-only query at this\nreview):\n\n| Session id | Title | Recorded messages |\n|---|---|---|\n| `ses_e370b0736ffeCmg7sOktmZ` | FR-A1 Deterministic Risk Gate 设计与测试计划 | 458 |\n| `ses_e372492e6ffe7GI2ddI30U` | FR-A1 风险闸门只读可行性与实施计划 | 29 |\n\nThe large session is the extended FR-A1 design → test → implementation → review →\nevidence session; the smaller one covers the earlier read-only feasibility planning.\n\n## How to preserve the raw transcript (do this before it ages out)\n\n1. **Stop writing** to the DB for the sessions to export (pause the agent), or copy\n   the DB and its `-wal`/`-shm` sidecars together for a consistent snapshot:\n   `cp opencode.db opencode.db-wal opencode.db-shm <dest>/`.\n2. **Export the raw session** (messages + parts, end to end, no summarizing) to\n   JSONL. A safe read-only recipe:\n\n   ```bash\n   python - <<'PY' > fr-a1-raw-transcript.jsonl\n   import sqlite3, os, json\n   p = os.path.expanduser(\"~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db\")\n   con = sqlite3.connect(f\"file:{p}?mode=ro\", uri=True)\n   sid = \"ses_e370b0736ffeCmg7sOktmZ\"   # and/or ses_e372492e6ffe7GI2ddI30U\n   for mid, ts, data in con.execute(\n       \"select id, time_created, data from message where session_id=? order by time_created, id\", (sid,)):\n       print(json.dumps({\"type\": \"message\", \"id\": mid, \"time\": ts, \"data\": json.loads(data)}, ensure_ascii=False))\n       for pid, pts, pdata in con.execute(\n           \"select id, time_created, data from part where message_id=? order by time_created, id\", (mid,)):\n           print(json.dumps({\"type\": \"part\", \"id\": pid, \"time\": pts, \"data\": json.loads(pdata)}, ensure_ascii=False))\n   con.close()\n   PY\n   ```\n\n   Repeat for the second session id if both are to be included. Do not edit or\n   truncate the exported parts; the requirement is the *raw* transcript.\n3. **Preserve the runtime log** in parallel (`cp ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log\n   <dest>/opencode.log`) as corroborating evidence.\n4. Keep the raw export and the log read-only; add human annotations as a **separate**\n   layer (below), not by editing the raw file.\n\n## Human annotation outline (to attach alongside the raw export)\n\nAnnotate by session/message reference; do not rewrite the transcript. Suggested\nanchors, matching the actual approval gates in this work:\n\n1. Requirements classification + architecture candidates (risk engine vs adapter).\n2. Test-plan approval and fixture corrections (portfolio consistency; blacklist\n   must target the analyzed ticker; directed 100-fixture set).\n3. Pre-implementation RED evidence required; core engine implementation approval.\n4. Core safety-edge review → RED tests → approved fixes (BUG-001..003).\n5. Stage 2 output-boundary architecture approval; CLI vs Python-API config decision.\n6. Audit-before-publication ADR revision; two final safety fixes approved.\n7. Evidence packaging (this folder); note that D5 must use the raw export, not\n   these summaries.\n\n## Integrity statement\n\nThese markdown summaries (`contribution-summary.md`, `human-review-milestones.md`)\nare **derived** aids for the human, not the D5 deliverable. The D5 deliverable is the\nraw JSONL export produced by the recipe above, plus the human's annotations. Until\nthat export is generated and attached, the D5 transcript should be treated as\n**not yet complete**.\n",

# FR-A1 — Final Demo Reliability Correction

The FR-A1 evidence packaging is complete and
the actual offline demonstration succeeded.

Human review found one small evidence-quality gap:

run_demo.py can catch a full-graph exception,
print a warning, and still exit with code 0.

The script also prints adapter outcomes without
automatically checking all expected results.

Please make one strictly scoped correction.

## Required changes

1. Make the demo return a non-zero exit code if
   the full-graph integration demonstration fails.

2. Add explicit checks for scenarios A-G:
   - Valid BUY is APPROVED and ACTIONABLE.
   - Missing stop-loss is REJECTED.
   - Missing snapshot is NEEDS_REVIEW.
   - Single-name cap violation is REJECTED.
   - Conflicting sector is not approved.
   - Audit writer failure is actually triggered.
   - Missing audit destination cannot publish
     an ACTIONABLE recommendation.

3. Keep the actual results and explanation visible.

4. Do not fabricate results or silently treat
   unexpected exceptions as success.

5. Preserve the distinction between adapter-level
   evidence and full-graph evidence.

## Approved write scope

Modify only:
- docs/evidence/fr-a1/demo/run_demo.py
- docs/evidence/fr-a1/demo/demo-output.txt
- docs/evidence/fr-a1/demo/README.md

No other file changes.

## Verification

Run:
python -m ruff check \
  docs/evidence/fr-a1/demo/run_demo.py

python docs/evidence/fr-a1/demo/run_demo.py

python -m pytest tests/risk_gate -q

git diff --check

Capture actual exit codes.

Do not change production code, tests, ADR,
shared requirements, CI or other team features.

Do not commit or push.

Respond in English.
STOP after verification.

print(f\"\\n[{label}]\")\n        print(f\"  original model rating : {gate['model_rating']}\")\n        print(f\"  core rule verdict     : {ev.verdict} / {ev.decision_status}\")\n        print(f\"  effective risk_verdict: {gate['risk_verdict']}\")\n        print(f\"  final public rating   : {gate['final_rating']}\")\n        print(f\"  decision status       : {gate['decision_status']}\")\n        print(f\"  rules                 : {_rule_summary(ev)}\")\n        print(f\"  triggered violations  : {ev.triggered_violation_ids}\")\n        print(f\"  audit persisted       : {wrote}\")\n finally:\n        if saved_writer is not None:\n            adapter_mod.persist_audit = saved_writer\n\n\n_CASES: list[dict] = []\n_FAILURES: list[str] = []\n\n\ndef check(case_id: str, label: str, ```text

Calls `tradingagents.risk_gate.adapter.apply_gate(...)` directly with deterministic
`TraderProposal`, `PortfolioDecision`, and `risk_portfolio` inputs. For each case it
reports:

- original AI model rating (`model_rating`, preserved as evidence),
- **core rule verdict** (`risk_evaluation.verdict` — the policy outcome),
- **effective publication verdict** (`risk_verdict`),
- final public rating (`final_rating`),
- decision status,
- triggered / unknown rules,
- audit persistence result (a real JSON file written to a temporary directory).

| Case | Scenario | Expected outcome |
|---|---|---|
| A | Valid BUY with complete risk inputs | APPROVED / ACTIONABLE, `final_rating` = Buy |
| B | BUY without stop-loss | REJECTED / BLOCKED, `final_rating` = REVIEW (R1 VIOLATED) |
| C | BUY without portfolio snapshot | NEEDS_REVIEW / PENDING_REVIEW, REVIEW (R2/R3 UNKNOWN) |
| D | Single-name concentration over 10% (12%) | REJECTED / BLOCKED (R2 VIOLATED) |
| E | Conflicting sector classification | never APPROVED; NEEDS_REVIEW (R3 UNKNOWN) |
| F | Audit persistence failure | fail-closed exception; no actionable output |
| G | No audit destination (would-be APPROVED) | downgraded to NEEDS_REVIEW / PENDING_REVIEW, REVIEW |

### Section 2 — full-graph integration

`risk_portfolio`, proving the decision boundary end-to-end (effective signal,
preserved `model_rating`, both structured objects retained). If the environment
cannot import the test infrastructure, this section reports that fact honestly and
the adapter-level results above remain the authoritative evidence.

## Deterministic data

- Valid book: `portfolio_value = 1,000,000 = cash 830,000 + NVDA 20,000 + MSFT

All done. The ADR modification is from the prior evidence-packaging turn (not this one); this turn only touched the three approved demo files, which live under the untracked `docs/evidence/`.

# FR-A1 Demo Reliability Correction — Report

## Changes made (only the 3 approved files)

**`docs/evidence/fr-a1/demo/run_demo.py`**
1. **Non-zero exit on failure.** `adapter_demo()` and `full_graph_demo()` now return a pass/fail boolean; `main()` aggregates all checks and returns `1` if any check fails or the full-graph section raises. A full-graph exception is recorded as `check FG: FAIL` with the exception type/message — never coerced to success.
2. **Explicit A–G assertions.** `run_adapter_case()` now returns an observation dict; each scenario is verified:
   - **A** core `APPROVED` and decision `ACTIONABLE`.
   - **B** `REJECTED` with `R1_STOP_LOSS_REQUIRED`.
   - **C** `NEEDS_REVIEW` / `PENDING_REVIEW`.
   - **D** `REJECTED` with `R2_SINGLE_NAME_CAP`.
   - **E** not `APPROVED` and not `ACTIONABLE`.
   - **F** writer actually invoked (`writer_calls ≥ 1`), raised `OSError`, no audit written.
   - **G** core `APPROVED` but publication non-actionable (`final_rating == REVIEW`), no audit written.
3. **Results and explanation remain visible.** Each case still prints the full structured record, plus `check <id>: PASS|FAIL — detail`, a `SUMMARY: n/8 …`, `RESULT:`, and a `FAILURES:` list on failure.

order by time_created,id\",(sid,)).fetchall()\n    path=os.path.join(\"snapshot_export\",out)\n    nmsg=0; npart=0\n    with open(path,\"w\",encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n        f.write(json.dumps({\"type\":\"session\",\"session\":meta},ensure_ascii=False)+\"\\n\")\n        for m in msgs:\n            nmsg+=1\n            parts=con.execute(\"select id,time_created,time_updated,data from part where message_id=? ```text
All artifacts are in place, verified, and outside Git. Repository working tree is clean.

# FR-A1 D5 Raw Agent Session Preservation — Report

## 1. Exported file paths (outside Git: `~/code/CS5351/fr_a1_private_evidence/`)

**Native OpenCode export** (authoritative raw, messages + parts incl. tool calls/results):
- `raw/ses_e370b0736ffeCmg7sOktmZVaEc.json` (5.1 MB) — main FR-A1 session
- `raw/ses_e372492e6ffe7GI2ddI30Ur9lH.json` (584 KB) — earlier feasibility session

**Sanitized native export** (`opencode export --sanitize`) for safe review/annotation:
- `sanitized/ses_e370….sanitized.json` (1.5 MB) and `sanitized/ses_e372….sanitized.json` (92 KB)

**Snapshot SQLite export (JSONL) + frozen DB reference** used to prove completeness:
- `snapshot_export/db_export_ses_e370….jsonl` (4.5 MB), `db_export_ses_e372….jsonl` (552 KB)
- `db_snapshot/opencode.db` (+`-wal`,`-shm`) — frozen copy taken for verification

**Reports:** `verification/completeness-report.md`, `verification/annotation-index.md`, `README.md`.

The source database at `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` was accessed **read-only** and never modified.

## 2. Completeness verification

| Artifact | Main msgs/parts | Feas msgs/parts |
|---|---:|---:|
| Frozen snapshot DB | **489 / 1944** | **29 / 107** |
| Snapshot SQLite export | **489 / 1944** (exact match) | **29 / 107** (exact match) |
| Native raw export | 492 / 1956 | 29 / 107 |
| Sanitized export | 492 / 1956 | 29 / 107 |
| Live DB at report time | 499 / 1984 | 29 / 107 |

- **Snapshot export = frozen DB exactly** for both sessions → no missing records in that capture.
- The **main session is live and still growing**, so the native export (492) and live DB (499) differ by messages accrued after each capture — expected for an active session, not data loss. The feasibility session (29/107) matches everywhere.
- File sizes and SHA-256 digests are recorded in `completeness-report.md`.

## 3. Sensitive-data review
- Scanned both raw exports for `openai_key`, `aws_key`, `Bearer …`, `api_key/secret/token/password` assignments, and `PRIVATE KEY` blocks: **zero matches** in all five categories.
- The only long-hex matches are benign internal identifiers: git commit hashes, `policy_hash` value, and OpenCode `"snapshot"` record IDs (confirmed by field context). **No secret values were printed** and none were edited.
- Sanitized exports were produced with the native `--sanitize` and re-scanned: clean. The untouched raw originals are preserved privately; no raw transcript entered Git.

## 4. Human annotation index status
`verification/annotation-index.md` maps all **eight required categories** to the **actual user-message IDs** of the 18 human turns in the main session (e.g. requirements/process `msg_1c8f4f91…`, architecture approval `msg_1c8fd1ab…`, test-plan `msg_1c908f50…`, RED-before-code `msg_1c928f21…`, core impl approval `msg_1c9318da…`, safety discovery `msg_1c93cd0d…`, safety fix `msg_1c95ef33…`, integration design/impl `msg_1c9688db…`/`msg_1c9a122f…`, safety review/fix `msg_1c9b1b6a…`/`msg_1c9bed61…`, audit-before-publication `msg_1c9ca22b…`, evidence `msg_1c9d0c10…`, demo reliability `msg_1c9de2a5…`, D5 `msg_1c9e49dd…`). Each entry states the human instruction, why it mattered, and the resulting action. ```text
# CS5351 Project — FR-A1 Risk Gate: Read-Only Feasibility Analysis

## Context

We are enhancing TauricResearch/TradingAgents at baseline
commit 9fa1196 (version 0.7.1).

I am responsible for FR-A1: Deterministic Risk Gate.

Our group will implement individual features locally before
integrating them into the shared GitHub repository.

All generated code changes must be made through OpenCode
under explicit human supervision.

## Requirement FR-A1

Before a trading recommendation is finalized, the system
shall validate TraderProposal and PortfolioDecision against
a versioned risk policy.

The deterministic validator shall return one of:
- APPROVED
- REJECTED
- NEEDS_REVIEW

Every verdict must include applicable rule identifiers
and the policy version.

The current draft defines five violation scenarios:

R1. Missing required stop-loss information.
R2. Single-stock exposure exceeding 10%.
R3. Sector concentration exceeding 30%.
R4. Risk-reward ratio below 1.5.
R5. A blacklisted stock.

The draft acceptance criterion requires that all five
injected violation scenarios must NOT be approved,
and 100% of verdicts must include rule identifiers.

Related requirements:
- INV-A1: Missing required stop loss or excessive stock
  exposure must never receive APPROVED.
- NFR-A1: Deterministic, network-free risk evaluation
  with low latency.
- NFR-A2: Auditable verdicts including policy version,
  rule IDs, input reference, decision, and timestamp.

FR-A2 (human approval workflow) and FR-A3 (advanced
policy configuration) are outside my current scope.

## Strict READ-ONLY Rules

1. Do not create, modify, or delete any files.
2. Do not generate implementation code yet.
3. Do not install dependencies or modify the environment.
4. Do not run live TradingAgents analyses.
5. Do not call external financial APIs.
6. Do not read or expose credentials, tokens, or secrets.
7. Do not commit, push, merge, or change Git branches.
8. Use the actual source at the current commit.
9. Distinguish verified findings from assumptions.
10. Respond entirely in English.

## Tasks

### A. Inspect Existing Data Structures

Read and analyze the relevant definitions in:
- tradingagents/agents/schemas.py
- tradingagents/agents/state.py
- tradingagents/portfolio.py
- tradingagents/agents/managers/portfolio_manager.py
- tradingagents/agents/trader/trader.py

Identify the exact fields available in:
- TraderProposal
- PortfolioDecision
- AgentState
- PortfolioContext

For each FR-A1 risk rule, identify:
- Required inputs
- Which inputs already exist
- Which inputs are missing
- Whether any input is unstructured free text
- Whether the rule can be evaluated deterministically

Do not invent fields.

### B. Inspect Existing Safety Behavior

Determine what validation already exists in the baseline.

Distinguish:
- Schema validation
- Rating parsing
- LLM-generated risk analysis
- Deterministic enforcement

Explain what new behavior FR-A1 would actually add.

### C. Identify the Integration Boundary

Inspect the graph and decision propagation paths.

Compare at least two possible integration points:
1. Immediately after TraderProposal generation.
2. After PortfolioDecision generation, before final
   persistence or publication.

Explain the advantages, disadvantages, and impact
on existing state, reporting, memory, and tests.

Recommend the minimum safe integration approach.

Avoid redesigning the entire LangGraph workflow.

### D. Define Risk-Rule Semantics

For each of the five rules, propose precise behavior
for APPROVED, REJECTED, or NEEDS_REVIEW.

Address:
- Missing or malformed numerical inputs
- BUY versus HOLD versus SELL
- Selling an existing holding versus initiating a short
- Required portfolio exposure and sector information
- How risk-reward ratio should be computed
- Conflicting information between proposal and decision
- Blacklist source and policy version

Do not treat unavailable information as proof of safety.

Do not invent financial data.

### E. Define the Smallest Interface Contract

Propose a small, deterministic risk-gate interface.

Specify:
- Inputs
- Outputs
- Verdict semantics
- Rule IDs
- Policy version
- Audit fields
- Error handling

Prefer explicit structured input over parsing arbitrary
LLM prose.

Keep the risk verdict separate from the LLM's market rating.

### F. Propose Offline Tests Before Implementation

Provide a test matrix covering:
- Five required violation cases
- At least two valid cases
- Missing or malformed data
- HOLD and SELL applicability
- Conflicting risk information
- Audit-field completeness
- Network-free execution
- Integration with the final decision flow
- Existing regression tests

Each test must specify:
- Input fixture
- Expected verdict
- Expected rule ID
- Requirement or invariant ID

No tests or implementation files should be written yet.

### G. Proposed Implementation Plan

List:
1. The minimal files to add.
2. The minimal existing files to modify.
3. Dependencies on other team members.
4. Main integration risks.
5. Proposed implementation stages.
6. Verification commands.
7. Which behaviors require group approval.

Provide exact paths and relevant function names.

## Required Output Format

1. Verified source findings
2. Input availability table for R1-R5
3. Existing versus missing capabilities
4. Integration alternatives
5. Recommended interface contract
6. Rule semantics and edge cases
7. Offline test approval matrix
8. Minimal implementation plan
9. Open questions requiring human approval

Do not implement anything.

STOP after presenting the analysis and plan.
Wait for explicit human approval before writing code.

1: """Pydantic schemas used by agents that produce structured output.
2: 
3: The framework's primary artifact is still prose: each agent's natural-language
4: reasoning is what users read in the saved markdown reports and what the
5: downstream agents read as context.  Structured output is layered onto the
6: three decision-making agents (Research Manager, Trader, Portfolio Manager)
7: so that:
8: 
9: - Their outputs follow consistent section headers across runs and providers
10: - Each provider's native structured-output mode is used (json_schema for
11:   OpenAI/xAI, response_schema for Gemini, tool-use for Anthropic)
12: - Schema field descriptions become the model's output instructions, freeing
13:   the prompt body to focus on context and the rating-scale guidance
14: - A render helper turns the parsed Pydantic instance back into the same
15:   markdown shape the rest of the system already consumes, so display,
16:   memory log, and saved reports keep working unchanged
17: """
18: 
19: from __future__ import annotations
20: 
21: from enum import StrEnum
22: from typing import Literal
23: 
24: from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator
25: 
26: # LLMs sometimes write a placeholder string ("None", "N/A", ...) into an optional
27: # numeric field instead of omitting it. Coerce those to None so the structured
28: # call validates instead of erroring (#1058). Pydantic still parses real numeric
29: # strings ("189.5") to float.
30: _NULLISH_FLOAT = {"", "none", "n/a", "na", "null", "nil", "-", "tbd", "unknown"}
31: 
32: 
33: def _coerce_optional_float(value):
34:     """Normalise an LLM-written optional numeric field before validation.
35: 
36:     Three shapes show up in practice: a placeholder string ("None", "N/A") in
37:     place of an omitted value (#1058); a percentage where a price was asked for
38:     ("15%", #1288); and a human-formatted price ("$1,234.50"). A percentage
39:     cannot be salvaged into an absolute level -- reading "15%" as 15 would put a
40:     stop at $15 on a $600 stock -- so it is dropped like a placeholder, leaving
41:     one bad field to null out instead of failing the whole proposal. A formatted
42:     price is reduced to its number.
43: 
44:     Anything that is not a single number is dropped the same way. A range
45:     ("150-160") or a hedge ("around 150") would otherwise reach pydantic, fail
46:     validation, and discard the whole decision, losing every field the model got
47:     right along with the price.
48:     """
49:     if not isinstance(value, str):
50:         return value
51:     text = value.strip()
52:     if text.lower() in _NULLISH_FLOAT or text.endswith("%"):
53:         return None
54:     cleaned = text.replace(",", "").lstrip("$€£¥").strip()
55:     try:
56:         return float(cleaned)
57:     except ValueError:
58:         return None

141: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
142: # Trader
143: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
144: 
145: 
146: class TraderProposal(BaseModel):
147:     """Structured transaction proposal produced by the Trader.
148: 
149:     The trader reads the Research Manager's investment plan and the analyst
150:     reports, then turns them into a concrete transaction: what action to
151:     take, the reasoning that justifies it, and the practical levels for
152:     entry, stop-loss, and sizing.
153:     """
154: 
155:     action: TraderAction = Field(
156:         description="The transaction direction. Exactly one of Buy / Hold / Sell.",
157:     )
158:     reasoning: str = Field(
159:         description=(
160:             "The case for this action, anchored in the analysts' reports and "
161:             "the research plan. Two to four sentences."
162:         ),
163:     )
164:     entry_price: float | None = Field(
165:         default=None,
166:         description=(
167:             "Optional entry price target as an absolute number in the instrument's "
168:             "quote currency (e.g. 189.5), never a percentage or a range. Omit it "
169:             "if you cannot state a specific level."
170:         ),
171:     )
172:     stop_loss: float | None = Field(
173:         default=None,
174:         description=(
175:             "Optional stop-loss as an absolute price in the instrument's quote "
176:             "currency (e.g. 172.0), never a percentage. Convert a percentage "
177:             "distance to the price level it implies, or omit it."
178:         ),
179:     )
180:     position_sizing: str | None = Field(
181:         default=None,
182:         description="Optional sizing guidance, e.g. '5% of portfolio'.",
183:     )
184: 
185:     @field_validator("entry_price", "stop_loss", mode="before")
186:     @classmethod
187:     def _nullish_float_to_none(cls, v):
188:         return _coerce_optional_float(v)
189: 
190: 
191: def render_trader_proposal(proposal: TraderProposal) -> str:
192:     """Render a TraderProposal to markdown.
193: 
194:     The trailing ``FINAL TRANSACTION PROPOSAL: **BUY/HOLD/SELL**`` line is
195:     preserved for backward compatibility with the analyst stop-signal text
196:     and any external code that greps for it.
197:     """
198:     parts = [
199:         f"**Action**: {proposal.action.value}",
200:         "",
201:         f"**Reasoning**: {proposal.reasoning}",
202:     ]
203:     # Named even when absent, so a reader can tell a level the trader chose not
204:     # to give from one the schema never asked for.
205:     for label, value in (("Entry Price", proposal.entry_price),
206:                          ("Stop Loss", proposal.stop_loss),
207:                          ("Position Sizing", proposal.position_sizing)):
208:         parts.extend(["", f"**{label}**: {value if value is not None and value != '' else 'not provided'}"])
209:     parts.extend([
210:         "",
211:         f"FINAL TRANSACTION PROPOSAL: **{proposal.action.value.upper()}**",
212:     ])
213:     return "\n".join(parts)
214: 
215: 
216: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
217: # Portfolio Manager
218: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
219: 
220: 
221: class PortfolioDecision(BaseModel):
222:     """Structured output produced by the Portfolio Manager.
223: 
224:     The model fills every field as part of its primary LLM call; no separate
225:     extraction pass is required. Field descriptions double as the model's
226:     output instructions, so the prompt body only needs to convey context and
227:     the rating-scale guidance.
228:     """
229: 
230:     rating: PortfolioRating = Field(
231:         description=(
232:             "The final position rating. Exactly one of Buy / Overweight / Hold / "
233:             "Underweight / Sell, picked based on the analysts' debate. "
234:             "Conflicting arguments alone are not a reason to Hold: commit to the "
235:             "stronger side, sized by how decisively it wins. Choose Hold only "
236:             "when the evidence is still balanced after weighing, or too thin to "
237:             "support a call."
238:         ),
239:     )
240:     executive_summary: str = Field(
241:         description=(
242:             "A concise action plan covering entry strategy, position sizing, "
243:             "key risk levels, and time horizon. Two to four sentences."
244:         ),
245:     )
246:     investment_thesis: str = Field(
247:         description=(
248:             "Detailed reasoning anchored in specific evidence from the analysts' "
249:             "debate. If prior lessons are referenced in the prompt context, "
250:             "incorporate them; otherwise rely solely on the current analysis."
251:         ),
252:     )
253:     price_target: float | None = Field(
254:         default=None,
255:         description="Optional target price in the instrument's quote currency.",
256:     )
257:     time_horizon: str | None = Field(
258:         default=None,
259:         description="Optional recommended holding period, e.g. '3-6 months'.",
260:     )
261: 
262:     @field_validator("price_target", mode="before")
263:     @classmethod
264:     def _nullish_float_to_none(cls, v):
265:         return _coerce_optional_float(v)
266: 
267: 
268: def render_pm_decision(decision: PortfolioDecision) -> str:
269:     """Render a PortfolioDecision back to the markdown shape the rest of the system expects.
270: 
271:     Memory log, CLI display, and saved report files all read this markdown,
272:     so the rendered output preserves the exact section headers (``**Rating**``,
273:     ``**Executive Summary**``, ``**Investment Thesis**``) that downstream
274:     parsers and the report writers already handle.
275:     """
276:     parts = [
277:         f"**Rating**: {decision.rating.value}",
278:         "",
279:         f"**Executive Summary**: {decision.executive_summary}",
280:         "",
281:         f"**Investment Thesis**: {decision.investment_thesis}",
282:     ]
283:     # Named even when absent: a missing line reads as a field nobody asked for,
284:     # so a reader cannot tell "no target" from "target not reported".
285:     target = decision.price_target if decision.price_target is not None else "not provided"
286:     parts.extend(["", f"**Price Target**: {target}"])
287:     parts.extend(["", f"**Time Horizon**: {decision.time_horizon or 'not provided'}"])
288:     return "\n".join(parts)
289: 
290: 
291: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
292: # Sentiment Analyst
293: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
294: 
295: 
296: class SentimentBand(StrEnum):
297:     """Discrete sentiment direction produced by the Sentiment Analyst.
298: 
299:     Six tiers keep the signal granular enough to be actionable while remaining
300:     small enough for every provider to map reliably from its JSON output.
301:     """
302: 
303:     BULLISH = "Bullish"
304:     MILDLY_BULLISH = "Mildly Bullish"
305:     NEUTRAL = "Neutral"
306:     MIXED = "Mixed"
307:     MILDLY_BEARISH = "Mildly Bearish"
308:     BEARISH = "Bearish"
309: 
310: 
311: class SentimentReport(BaseModel):
312:     """Structured sentiment report produced by the Sentiment Analyst.
313: 
314:     Replaces the previous free-form prose output so downstream consumers
315:     (dashboards, audit logs, PDF renderers, other agents) can read
316:     ``overall_band`` and ``overall_score`` without maintaining fragile regex
317:     fallbacks that drift with every model release. ``narrative`` preserves the
318:     rich source-by-source analysis; ``render_sentiment_report`` prepends a
319:     deterministic header so the saved report stays human-readable.
320:     """
321: 
322:     overall_band: SentimentBand = Field(
323:         description=(
324:             "Overall sentiment direction. Exactly one of: "
325:             "Bullish / Mildly Bullish / Neutral / Mixed / Mildly Bearish / Bearish. "
326:             "Use Mixed when sources point in clearly different directions. "
327:             "Use Neutral only when all sources are genuinely silent or non-committal."
328:         ),
329:     )
330:     overall_score: float = Field(
331:         ge=0.0,
332:         le=10.0,
333:         description=(
334:             "Numeric sentiment intensity on a 0–10 scale. "
335:             "0 = maximally bearish, 5 = neutral, 10 = maximally bullish. "
336:             "Guideline for consistency with overall_band: "
337:             "Bullish ~6.5–10, Mildly Bullish ~5.5–6.4, Neutral/Mixed ~4.5–5.5, "
338:             "Mildly Bearish ~3.5–4.4, Bearish ~0–3.4. "
339:             "Only the 0–10 bounds are enforced."
340:         ),
341:     )
342:     confidence: Literal["low", "medium", "high"] = Field(
343:         description=(
344:             "Confidence in the assessment based on data quality and sample size. "
345:             "Use 'low' when one or more sources returned a placeholder or fewer "
346:             "than 5 data points; 'medium' when data is present but sparse; "
347:             "'high' when all three sources returned substantive data."
348:         ),
349:     )
350:     narrative: str = Field(
351:         description=(
352:             "Full sentiment report covering, in order: "
353:             "(1) source-by-source breakdown with specific evidence (cite message "
354:             "counts, ratios, notable posts); "
355:             "(2) cross-source divergences and alignments; "
356:             "(3) dominant narrative themes; "
357:             "(4) catalysts and risks surfaced by the data; "
358:             "(5) a markdown table summarising key sentiment signals, their "
359:             "direction, source, and supporting evidence. "
360:             "Keep it informative and substantive: develop each section thoroughly "
361:             "with concrete evidence so every point adds new signal for the trader."
362:         ),
363:     )
364: 
365: 
366: def render_sentiment_report(report: SentimentReport) -> str:
367:     """Render a SentimentReport to the markdown shape the rest of the system expects.
368: 
369:     The structured header (band + score + confidence) is prepended to the
370:     narrative so the saved report is both human-readable and machine-parseable
371:     without regex.
372:     """
373:     return "\n".join([
374:         f"**Overall Sentiment:** **{report.overall_band.value}** "
375:         f"(Score: {report.overall_score:.1f}/10)",
376:         f"**Confidence:** {report.confidence.capitalize()}",
377:         "",
378:         report.narrative,
379:     ])

1: """The caller's book, as the decision agents see it.
2: 
3: Optional input to a run: what is held, at what average price, and how much cash
4: is free. Without it the agents cannot tell adding to a full position from
5: opening a new one. Three states are distinct and must stay so: a position, a
6: flat book, and no context at all, since treating "not provided" as "flat" would
7: invent a fact about the caller's account.
8: 
9: Broker-neutral by construction: quantities are generic units and the currency is
10: whatever label the caller passes, so nothing here implies a venue or an
11: execution path.
12: """
13: 
14: from __future__ import annotations
15: 
16: import hashlib
17: import json
18: from pathlib import Path
19: 
20: from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, ValidationError
21: 
22: from tradingagents.dataflows.symbols import normalize_symbol
23: 
24: 
25: class Position(BaseModel):
26:     model_config = ConfigDict(allow_inf_nan=False)
27: 
28:     ticker: str = Field(description="Instrument symbol, e.g. AAPL")
29:     quantity: float = Field(description="Signed units held; negative is short")
30:     average_price: float | None = Field(default=None, description="Average entry price per unit")
31: 
32: 
33: class PortfolioContext(BaseModel):
34:     model_config = ConfigDict(allow_inf_nan=False)
35: 
36:     cash: float | None = Field(default=None, description="Free cash available")
37:     currency: str | None = Field(default=None, description="Currency label for cash and prices")
38:     positions: list[Position] = Field(default_factory=list)
39: 
40:     def positions_in(self, ticker: str) -> list[Position]:
41:         """The holdings of the instrument the run prices for ``ticker``, under any
42:         broker spelling (BTCUSDT, 700.HK). Holdings keep the spelling they were
43:         given: a symbol can also name another instrument (WTI the stock)."""
44:         symbol = normalize_symbol(ticker)
45:         return [p for p in self.positions if normalize_symbol(p.ticker) == symbol]
46: 
47:     def position_in(self, ticker: str) -> Position | None:
48:         held = self.positions_in(ticker)
49:         return held[0] if held else None
50: 
51:     def render(self, ticker: str) -> str:
52:         """The portfolio block for the decision agents, led by the analyzed instrument."""
53:         symbol = normalize_symbol(ticker)
54:         held = self.positions_in(symbol)
55:         lines = []
56:         for position in held:
57:             price = f", average price {position.average_price:,.2f}" if position.average_price is not None else ""
58:             spelled = position.ticker.strip().upper()
59:             listed = f" (listed as {position.ticker})" if spelled != symbol else ""
60:             lines.append(f"- Current position in {symbol}: {position.quantity:,.4g} units{price}{listed}")
61:         if not held:
62:             lines.append(f"- No current position in {symbol}")
63:         if self.cash is not None:
64:             lines.append(f"- Cash available: {self.cash:,.2f}{' ' + self.currency if self.currency else ''}")
65:         others = [p for p in self.positions if all(p is not h for h in held)]
66:         if others:
67:             lines.append("- Other positions: " + ", ".join(f"{p.ticker.upper()} {p.quantity:,.4g}" for p in others))
68:         return "Portfolio at the analysis date:\n" + "\n".join(lines)
69: 
70:     def fingerprint(self) -> str:
71:         """Stable digest of the book, so a changed one cannot resume a stale run."""
72:         return hashlib.sha256(self.model_dump_json().encode()).hexdigest()[:12]
73: 
74: 
75: def load_portfolio(path: str | Path) -> PortfolioContext:
76:     """Read a portfolio JSON file, failing before the run rather than mid-graph."""
77:     try:
78:         data = json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
79:         return PortfolioContext.model_validate(data)
80:     except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, ValidationError) as exc:
81:         raise ValueError(f"portfolio file {path} is not usable: {exc}") from exc

<content>
1: """Portfolio Manager: synthesises the risk-analyst debate into the final decision.
2: 
3: Uses LangChain's ``with_structured_output`` so the LLM produces a typed
4: ``PortfolioDecision`` directly, in a single call. Its rating is the run's
5: ``final_rating``, and the decision is rendered to markdown as
6: ``final_trade_decision`` for the memory log, CLI display and saved reports.
7: When a provider does not expose structured output, the agent falls back to
8: free-text generation and the rating is read from that text.
9: """
10: 
11: from __future__ import annotations
12: 
13: from tradingagents.agents.context import (
14:     get_instrument_context_from_state,
15:     get_language_instruction,
16:     get_portfolio_context_from_state,
17: )
18: from tradingagents.agents.rating import parse_rating
19: from tradingagents.agents.schemas import PortfolioDecision, render_pm_decision
20: from tradingagents.agents.structured import NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS, bind_structured, invoke_structured
21: 
22: 
23: def create_portfolio_manager(llm):
24:     structured_llm = bind_structured(llm, PortfolioDecision, "Portfolio Manager")
25: 
26:     def portfolio_manager_node(state) -> dict:
27:         instrument_context = get_instrument_context_from_state(state)
28:         portfolio_context = get_portfolio_context_from_state(state)
29: 
30:         history = state["risk_debate_state"]["history"]
31:         risk_debate_state = state["risk_debate_state"]
32:         research_plan = state["investment_plan"]
33:         trader_plan = state["trader_investment_plan"]
34: 
35:         past_context = state.get("past_context", "")
36:         lessons_line = (
37:             f"- Lessons from prior decisions and outcomes:\n{past_context}\n"
38:             if past_context
39:             else ""
40:         )
41: 
42:         prompt = f"""As the Portfolio Manager, synthesize the risk analysts' debate and deliver the final trading decision.
43: 
44: {instrument_context}
45: 
46: {portfolio_context}
47: 
48: ---
49: 
50: **Rating Scale** (use exactly one):
51: - **Buy**: Strong conviction to enter or add to position
52: - **Overweight**: Favorable outlook, gradually increase exposure
53: - **Hold**: Maintain current position, no action needed
54: - **Underweight**: Reduce exposure, take partial profits
55: - **Sell**: Exit position or avoid entry
56: 
57: **Context:**
58: - Research Manager's investment plan: **{research_plan}**
59: - Trader's transaction proposal: **{trader_plan}**
60: {lessons_line}
61: **Risk Analysts Debate History:**
62: {history}
63: 
64: ---
65: 
66: Ground every conclusion in specific evidence from the analysts. The risk debate always contains conflicting stances; deciding which is stronger is the job, so conflict alone is not a reason to Hold. Commit to the stronger case, sized by how decisively it wins. Choose Hold only when the evidence is still balanced after that weighing, or too thin to support a call; do not force a direction to appear decisive. Weigh the analysts on their merits, independent of speaking order.
67: 
68: ## Output
69: 
70: Write these sections, in this order, starting with the rating on its own line:
71: 
72: - **Rating**: exactly one of Buy / Overweight / Hold / Underweight / Sell
73: - **Executive Summary**: the call and how to act on it
74: - **Investment Thesis**: the evidence that decided it, and what would change it
75: 
76: {NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS}{get_language_instruction()}"""
77: 
78:         # The typed rating is the decision; the rendered text only carries it.
79:         # Read back from text, a rating the thesis quotes could replace it.
80:         decision = invoke_structured(structured_llm, prompt, "Portfolio Manager")
81:         if decision is not None:
82:             final_trade_decision = render_pm_decision(decision)
83:             final_rating = decision.rating.value
84:         else:
85:             final_trade_decision = llm.invoke(prompt).content
86:             final_rating = parse_rating(final_trade_decision)
87: 
88:         new_risk_debate_state = {
89:             "history": risk_debate_state["history"],
90:             "aggressive_history": risk_debate_state["aggressive_history"],
91:             "conservative_history": risk_debate_state["conservative_history"],
92:             "neutral_history": risk_debate_state["neutral_history"],
93:             "latest_speaker": "Judge",
94:             "current_aggressive_response": risk_debate_state["current_aggressive_response"],
95:             "current_conservative_response": risk_debate_state["current_conservative_response"],
96:             "current_neutral_response": risk_debate_state["current_neutral_response"],
97:             "count": risk_debate_state["count"],

1: """Prompt context shared by the agents: instrument identity, output language and portfolio."""
2: 
3: import functools
4: import logging
5: from collections.abc import Mapping
6: from typing import Any
7: 
8: from tradingagents.dataflows.date_window import is_historical

11: logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

13: 
14: def get_language_instruction() -> str:
15:     """Return a prompt instruction for the configured output language.
16: 
17:     Returns empty string when English (default), so no extra tokens are used.
18:     Applied to every agent whose output reaches the saved report —
19:     analysts, researchers, debaters, research manager, trader, and
20:     portfolio manager — so a non-English run produces a fully localized
21:     report rather than a mix of languages.
22:     """
23:     from tradingagents.dataflows.config import get_config
24:     lang = get_config().get("output_language", "English")
25:     if lang.strip().lower() == "english":
26:         return ""
27:     # The labelled lines are read by the program, so they keep their English
28:     # label and value: a translated rating line leaves the reader prose to
29:     # search, where a negated rating ("not a Sell") reads as the call (#1435).
30:     return (
31:         f" Write your entire response in {lang}, except the labelled lines the format"
32:         f" asks for (the \"**Rating**:\" line, \"FINAL TRANSACTION PROPOSAL:\"):"
33:         f" keep their label and value in English, exactly as specified."
34:     )
35: 
36: 
37: def opponent_argument_or_opening(text: str, opponent: str) -> str:
38:     """Opponent's latest argument, or an explicit opening marker when empty.
39: 
40:     The first speaker in each debate round receives an empty opponent response;
41:     interpolating it into a "refute the opponent" prompt makes the model
42:     fabricate the other side's position. Returning a clear "has not spoken yet"
43:     marker instead lets it open with its own case (#1176).
44:     """
45:     text = (text or "").strip()
46:     if text:
47:         return text
48:     return f"(The {opponent} has not spoken yet — open the debate with your own case.)"
49: 
50: 
51: def _clean_identity_value(value: Any) -> str | None:
52:     """Return a trimmed string, or None for empty / placeholder-ish values."""
53:     if not isinstance(value, str):
54:         return None
55:     cleaned = value.strip()
56:     if not cleaned or cleaned.lower() in {"none", "n/a", "nan", "null"}:
57:         return None
58:     return cleaned
59: 
60: 
61: def resolve_instrument_identity(ticker: str) -> dict:
62:     """Resolve deterministic identity metadata (company name, sector, …) for a ticker.
63: 
64:     This exists to stop the pipeline from hallucinating a *different* company
65:     when a chart pattern suggests a different industry than the real one
66:     (#814): without a ground-truth name, the market analyst would pattern-match
67:     the price action to a narrative and invent an identity that then cascaded
68:     through every downstream agent.
69: 
70:     Best-effort by design: if yfinance is unavailable, rate-limited, or doesn't
71:     recognise the ticker, we return ``{}`` and the caller falls back to
72:     ticker-only context rather than failing before analysis starts. An answer
73:     is cached for the process; a failed lookup is asked again next time.
74: 
75:     Identity resolves for the same instrument the price path fetches
76:     (``XAUUSD`` -> ``GC=F``, #983).
77:     """
78:     try:
79:         return _identity(ticker)
80:     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — fail open, never block the run
81:         logger.debug("Could not resolve instrument identity for %s: %s", ticker, exc)
82:         return {}
83: 
84: 
85: @functools.lru_cache(maxsize=256)
86: def _identity(ticker: str) -> dict:
87:     """The vendor's identity fields for ``ticker``; raises if the lookup fails."""
88:     info = get_company_profile(ticker)
89:     identity: dict[str, str] = {}
90:     company_name = _clean_identity_value(info.get("longName")) or _clean_identity_value(
91:         info.get("shortName")
92:     )
93:     if company_name:
94:         identity["company_name"] = company_name
95:     for source_key, target_key in (
96:         ("sector", "sector"),
97:         ("industry", "industry"),
98:         ("exchange", "exchange"),
99:         ("quoteType", "quote_type"),
100:     ):
101:         value = _clean_identity_value(info.get(source_key))
102:         if value:
103:             identity[target_key] = value
104:     return identity
105: 
106: 
107: def build_instrument_context(
108:     ticker: str,
109:     asset_type: str = "stock",
110:     identity: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
111:     trade_date: str | None = None,
112: ) -> str:
113:     """Describe the exact instrument so agents preserve identity and ticker.
114: 
115:     When ``identity`` is provided (resolved deterministically via
116:     :func:`resolve_instrument_identity`), the company name and business
117:     classification are injected so agents anchor to the real company rather
118:     than pattern-matching the price chart to a wrong one (#814).
119: 
120:     That profile carries no historical vintage: it describes the company today.
121:     A run dated earlier gets the current name alone, as a way to tell the
122:     company apart from others rather than as what it was called then; a sector,
123:     industry or exchange it holds today is not given, since it may not have held
124:     on the analysis date.
125:     """
126:     is_crypto = asset_type == "crypto"
127:     instrument_label = "asset" if is_crypto else "instrument"
128:     context = (
129:         f"The {instrument_label} to analyze is `{ticker}`. "
130:         "The tools serve this instrument; refer to it by this exact ticker in every report and recommendation, "
131:         "preserving any exchange suffix (e.g. `.TO`, `.L`, `.HK`, `.T`, `-USD`)."
132:     )
133: 
134:     identity = identity or {}
135:     name = identity.get("company_name") or identity.get("name")

172: def get_instrument_context_from_state(state: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str:
173:     """Return the instrument context for the current run.

175:     Prefers the identity-resolved context computed once at run start and

177:     Falls back to a ticker-only context — with no network lookup — when the
178:     state was constructed without it (bare programmatic states, tests), so a

205:     """Return the caller's portfolio block, or a notice that none was given.
206:

53: def _analyst_graph(spec, agent, max_tool_rounds: int):
54:     """One analyst as a graph of its own: the model and its tools, on a private message history.
55: 
56:     It returns only its report, so analysts running side by side never write the
57:     same key, and its tool calls never reach the other analysts' messages. After
58:     ``max_tool_rounds`` rounds of tool calls it is told to write its report, and
59:     that turn ends it whatever it answers, so a model that keeps calling tools
60:     cannot run the graph into its recursion limit (#1420).
61:     """
62:     output = TypedDict(f"{spec.key.capitalize()}Report", {spec.report_key: str})
63:     graph = StateGraph(AgentState, output_schema=output)
64:     graph.add_node("agent", agent)
65:     graph.add_edge(START, "agent")
66:     if not spec.tools:
67:         graph.add_edge("agent", END)
68:         return graph.compile()

198:         ``propagate`` (via :meth:`checkpoint_scope`) and the CLI stream path use
199:         this so ``--checkpoint`` actually resumes (#1249); previously the setup
200:         lived only inside ``propagate`` and the CLI streamed the checkpointer-less
201:         graph, making the flag a no-op.
202:         """
203:         self._resuming = False
204:         if not self.config.get("checkpoint_enabled"):
205:             return None
206:         signature = self._run_signature(asset_type, portfolio)
207:         self._checkpointer_ctx = get_checkpointer(self.config["data_cache_dir"], company_name)
208:         saver = self._checkpointer_ctx.__enter__()
209:         self.graph = self.workflow.compile(checkpointer=saver)
210: 
211:         step = checkpoint_step(
212:             self.config["data_cache_dir"], company_name, str(trade_date), signature
213:         )
214:         self._resuming = step is not None
215:         if step is not None:
216:             logger.info("Resuming from step %d for %s on %s", step, company_name, trade_date)
217:         else:
218:             logger.info("Starting fresh for %s on %s", company_name, trade_date)
219:         return thread_id(company_name, str(trade_date), signature)
220: 
221:     def checkpoint_input(self, init_state):
222:         """The value to stream/invoke: ``None`` to resume an existing checkpoint,
223:         else the initial state for a fresh run.
224: 
225:         LangGraph resumes an interrupted thread when invoked with ``None``;
226:         re-passing the initial state instead appends it through the message
227:         reducer, duplicating messages in the resumed state (#1249).
228:         """
229:         return None if self._resuming else init_state
230: 
231:     def end_checkpoint(self):
232:         """Restore the plain uncheckpointed graph after a checkpointed run."""
233:         if self._checkpointer_ctx is not None:
234:             self._checkpointer_ctx.__exit__(None, None, None)
235:             self._checkpointer_ctx = None
236:             self.graph = self.workflow.compile()
237:         self._resuming = False
238: 
239:     @contextmanager
240:     def checkpoint_scope(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = "stock", portfolio=None):
241:         """Context-manager form of begin/end_checkpoint for the propagate path."""
242:         try:
243:             yield self.begin_checkpoint(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)
244:         finally:
245:             self.end_checkpoint()
246: 
247:     def clear_checkpoint_on_success(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = "stock", portfolio=None):
248:         """Drop a completed run's checkpoint so a later run starts fresh (#1249)."""
249:         if self.config.get("checkpoint_enabled"):
250:             clear_checkpoint(
251:                 self.config["data_cache_dir"], company_name, str(trade_date),
252:                 self._run_signature(asset_type, portfolio),
253:             )
254: 
255:     def run_settings(self) -> dict:
256:         """What produces this graph's runs, for the saved report and state log.
257: 
258:         An allowlist: endpoints (a backend_url can carry credentials), keys and
259:         local paths are never recorded.
260:         """
261:         cfg = self.config
262:         return {
263:             "version": tradingagents.__version__,
264:             "llm_provider": cfg.get("llm_provider"),
265:             "deep_think_provider": tier_provider(cfg, "deep") if cfg.get("llm_provider") else None,
266:             "deep_think_llm": cfg.get("deep_think_llm"),
267:             "quick_think_provider": tier_provider(cfg, "quick") if cfg.get("llm_provider") else None,
268:             "quick_think_llm": cfg.get("quick_think_llm"),
269:             "analysts": list(self.selected_analysts),
270:             "max_debate_rounds": cfg.get("max_debate_rounds"),
271:             "max_risk_discuss_rounds": cfg.get("max_risk_discuss_rounds"),
272:             "output_language": cfg.get("output_language"),
273:             "data_vendors": dict(cfg.get("data_vendors") or {}),
274:             "tool_vendors": dict(cfg.get("tool_vendors") or {}),
275:         }
276: 
277:     def save_reports(self, final_state, ticker, save_path=None, html=True) -> Path:
278:         """Write the report tree for a completed run, like the CLI does.
279: 
280:         Programmatic callers get the same on-disk reports the CLI produces. Pass
281:         an explicit ``save_path`` or let it default under ``results_dir``; the
282:         report is also written as one HTML page unless ``html`` is False.
283:         """
284:         if save_path is None:
285:             save_path = self.default_report_path(ticker)
286:         return write_report_tree(final_state, ticker, save_path, settings=self.run_settings(), html=html)
287: 
288:     def default_report_path(self, ticker) -> Path:
289:         """Where a run's reports go unless told otherwise: under results_dir, stamped now."""
290:         stamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
291:         return Path(self.config["results_dir"]) / "reports" / f"{safe_ticker_component(ticker)}_{stamp}"
292: 
293:     def create_run_state(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = "stock", portfolio=None):
294:         """Build a run's initial state; propagate() and the CLI both start here.
295: 
296:         Injects the resolved instrument identity for every agent (#814). The
297:         memory log's lessons are not here: the graph's Memory Log step settles
298:         and loads them alongside the analysts (see ``_memory_step``).
299:         """
300:         trade_date = _validate_trade_date(trade_date)
301:         return self.propagator.create_initial_state(
302:             company_name,
303:             trade_date,
304:             asset_type=asset_type,
305:             instrument_context=self.resolve_instrument_context(company_name, asset_type, trade_date),
306:             portfolio_context=portfolio.render(company_name) if portfolio is not None else "",
307:         )
308: 
309:     def _memory_step(self, state):
310:         """The graph's Memory Log step, alongside the analysts (#1428): settle every
311:         ticker's due decisions (#1445), then return the lessons known by the
312:         trade date for the Portfolio Manager (#1251).
313: 
314:         Settling fetches prices and asks the model for a reflection per decision,
315:         so it runs beside the analysts instead of before them. A failure here
316:         does not end the run: the analysts' work is kept, the lessons already in
317:         the log are used, and the report says what could not be settled.
318:         """
319:         note = ""
320:         try:
321:             # Another run settling the same log does the work; this one goes on.
322:             done = self.settle_all_pending(wait=False)
323:             if done.failed:
324:                 note = (f"{len(done.failed)} past decision(s) could not be settled this run "
325:                         "and stay pending.")
326:         except Exception as exc:
327:             logger.warning("Settling past decisions failed: %s", exc)
328:             note = f"Past decisions could not be settled this run ({type(exc).__name__}); they stay pending."
329:         try:
330:             past_context = self.memory_log.get_past_context(
331:                 state["company_of_interest"], as_of=self._memory_as_of(state["trade_date"]))
332:         except Exception as exc:
333:             logger.warning("Reading the memory log failed: %s", exc)
334:             past_context = ""
335:             note = note or f"The memory log could not be read this run ({type(exc).__name__})."
336:         return {"past_context": past_context, "memory_note": note}
337: 
338:     def settle_pending(self, company_name) -> settlement.Settlement:
339:         """Settle this ticker's decisions whose holding window has now traded.
340: 
341:         A run settles every due decision alongside its analysts, so its own
342:         decision stays pending until a later run. A caller that is done
343:         analyzing a ticker (a backtest sweep, a scheduled job) calls this to
344:         settle it now. Returns what was settled and what failed.
345:         """
346:         with run_config(self.config):
347:             return settlement.settle_pending(company_name, self.memory_log, self.reflector, self.config)
348: 
349:     def settle_all_pending(self, wait: bool = True) -> settlement.Settlement:
350:         """Settle every ticker's decisions whose holding window has now traded (#1445).
351: 
352:         For a scheduler whose tickers rotate: a ticker it stops analysing would
353:         otherwise keep its decisions pending, and their lessons out of later runs.
354:         With ``wait=False`` a pass already running on the same log is not waited for.
355:         """
356:         with run_config(self.config):
357:             return settlement.settle_all_pending(self.memory_log, self.reflector, self.config, wait=wait)
358: 
359:     def record_decision(self, company_name, trade_date, final_state):
360:         """Record a finished run: its state log, and its decision in the memory log
361:         for reflection on the next same-ticker run. propagate() and the CLI both end here."""
362:         self._log_state(trade_date, final_state)
363:         decision = final_state.get("final_trade_decision")
364:         if not decision:
365:             logger.warning("No final decision for %s on %s; nothing added to the memory log",
366:                            company_name, trade_date)
367:             return
368:         self.memory_log.store_decision(
369:             ticker=company_name, trade_date=trade_date, final_trade_decision=decision,
370:             rating=run_rating(final_state),
371:         )
372: 
373:     def _run_graph(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = "stock",
374:                    checkpoint_thread_id: str | None = None, portfolio=None):
375:         """Execute the graph and write the resulting state to disk and memory log."""
376:         init_agent_state = self.create_run_state(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)
377:         args = self.propagator.get_graph_args()
378: 
379:         # Inject the checkpoint thread_id (from checkpoint_scope) so the same
380:         # ticker+date+graph-shape resumes; a different one starts fresh (#1089).
381:         if checkpoint_thread_id is not None:
382:             args.setdefault("config", {}).setdefault("configurable", {})["thread_id"] = checkpoint_thread_id
383: 
384:         # None resumes an existing checkpoint; init_agent_state starts fresh (#1249).
385:         graph_input = self.checkpoint_input(init_agent_state)
386:         if self.debug:
387:             # A state repeats the messages before it, so each prints once (#1027).
388:             final_state, printed = {}, set()
389:             for messages, state in self.stream_run(graph_input, **args):
390:                 for msg in messages:
391:                     key = getattr(msg, "id", None) or (type(msg).__name__, getattr(msg, "content", None))
392:                     if key not in printed:
393:                         printed.add(key)
394:                         msg.pretty_print()
395:                 if state is not None:
396:                     final_state.update(state)
397:         else:
398:             final_state = self.graph.invoke(graph_input, **args)
399: 
400:         self.record_decision(company_name, trade_date, final_state)
401: 
402:         # Clear checkpoint on successful completion to avoid stale state.
403:         self.clear_checkpoint_on_success(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)
404: 
405:         return final_state, run_rating(final_state)
406: 
407:     def stream_run(self, graph_input, **args):
408:         """Stream a run as ``(messages, state)`` pairs.
409: 
410:         ``messages`` are the agents' messages, the analysts' included. ``state``
411:         is the run's state after a top-level step; for a step inside an analyst's
412:         graph it is that analyst's report once filed, else None.
413: 
414:         Each analyst works in a graph of its own, and the run's state takes the
415:         analysts' reports only when the slowest has finished, so their messages
416:         and reports come from their own finished steps ("tasks") as they happen.
417:         """
418:         args = {**args, "stream_mode": ["values", "tasks"]}
419:         # The graph's own config serves every tool call, as in propagate(), even
420:         # when the process-wide config has changed since. Each step runs in the
421:         # run's context, so the caller keeps its own between steps.
422:         context = run_config_context(self.config)
423:         stream = context.run(self.graph.stream, graph_input, subgraphs=True, **args)
424:         try:
425:             while (step := context.run(next, stream, None)) is not None:
426:                 namespace, mode, chunk = step
427:                 if namespace:
428:                     result = chunk.get("result") if mode == "tasks" else None
429:                     if isinstance(result, dict):
430:                         report = {k: v for k, v in result.items() if k != "messages" and v}
431:                         if result.get("messages") or report:
432:                             yield result.get("messages", []), report or None
433:                 elif mode == "values":
434:                     yield chunk.get("messages", []), chunk
435:         finally:
436:             context.run(stream.close)
437:

1: """Shared 5-tier rating vocabulary and a deterministic heuristic parser.
2: 
3: The same five-tier scale (Buy, Overweight, Hold, Underweight, Sell) is used by:
4: - The Research Manager (investment plan recommendation)
5: - The Portfolio Manager (final position decision; its free-text fallback is read here)
6: - The memory log (rating tag stored alongside each decision entry)
7: 
8: Centralising it here avoids drift between those call sites.
9: 
10: ``extract_rating`` returns ``None`` when no rating can be found, and every
11: caller turns that into ``REVIEW`` rather than a tradeable position: a decision
12: nobody can read is not a Hold, and a Hold recorded in its place is quoted back to
13: the next run as a call that was never made (#1170).
14: """
15: 
16: from __future__ import annotations
17: 
18: import re
19: import unicodedata
20: 
21: # Canonical, ordered 5-tier scale (most bullish to most bearish).
22: RATINGS_5_TIER: tuple[str, ...] = (
23:     "Buy", "Overweight", "Hold", "Underweight", "Sell",
24: )
25: 
26: # Signal emitted when the model's decision has no recognizable rating. It is not
27: # a tradeable position: it flags output that needs a human/re-run rather than
28: # silently degrading to Hold. Callers that map the signal onto the 5-tier enum
29: # (e.g. ``PortfolioRating(signal)``) should guard with ``is_review`` first.
30: RATING_REVIEW = "REVIEW"
31: 
32: _RATING_SET = {r.lower() for r in RATINGS_5_TIER}
33: 
34: # Matches "Rating: X" / "rating - X" / "Rating — **X**" — tolerates markdown
35: # bold wrappers and any dash or colon a model writes as the separator. "rating"
36: # must start a word, so "Operating margin: Sell-side" is not a label.
37: _RATING_LABEL_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![a-z])rating\b[^:\-\u2010-\u2015]*[:\-\u2010-\u2015][\s*]*(\w+)",
38:                               re.IGNORECASE)
39: 
40: # The decision's own rating line, in the shape the Portfolio Manager is asked to
41: # open with ("- **Rating**: X", "**Final Rating**: X", "## Our rating - X"): an
42: # optional list marker, emphasis and heading marks, and only words naming the
43: # decision itself before "rating". "Consensus rating: Buy" or "Trader's rating:
44: # Buy" is someone else's rating.
45: _OWN_QUALIFIER = r"(?:(?:final|our|overall|my|recommended|updated|revised|new|current)\s+)*"
46: _RATING_LINE_RE = re.compile(
47:     r"\s*(?P<item>(?:[-+*\u2022]|\d+[.)])\s+)?[\s*_#]*" + _OWN_QUALIFIER
48:     + r"rating[^\w:\-\u2010-\u2015]*[:\-\u2010-\u2015][\s*]*(?P<value>\w+)",
49:     re.IGNORECASE,
50: )
51: 
52: # A line presenting the scale rather than a decision ("Rating Scale: Buy, ...").
53: _RATING_SCALE_RE = re.compile(r"rating\s*(scale|options|legend)", re.IGNORECASE)
54: 
55: def extract_rating(text: str) -> str | None:
56:     """Extract a 5-tier rating from its label, or ``None`` if there is none.
57: 
58:     Reads an explicit "Rating: X" label (tolerant of markdown bold) in the
59:     NFKC-normalized text, so fullwidth punctuation like ``Rating：Overweight``
60:     matches as ASCII does: the decision's opening rating line, else its own
61:     rating lines or, failing those, every label, when they agree.
62:     """
63:     if not text:
64:         return None
65:     norm = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", text)
66: 
67:     # The decision is asked to open with its rating, so a first line (after any
68:     # headings) in that shape is the call. A list item there may also be a quote
69:     # heading a list of other parties' ratings, so it counts with the decision's
70:     # other rating lines, which leave out list items; failing those, every label
71:     # counts. Either way they must agree: ratings that differ, with nothing
72:     # marking which one is the call, are no call (#1170). Lines presenting the
73:     # scale itself are a legend the model echoed, not a call.
74:     lines = [line for line in norm.splitlines() if line.strip() and not _RATING_SCALE_RE.search(line)]
75:     first = next((line for line in lines if not line.lstrip().startswith("#")
76:                   or _RATING_LINE_RE.match(line)), "")
77:     m = _RATING_LINE_RE.match(first)
78:     opening = m if m and m.group("value").lower() in _RATING_SET else None
79:     if opening and not opening.group("item"):
80:         return opening.group("value").capitalize()
81: 
82:     own = [opening.group("value").capitalize()] if opening else []
83:     labels = []
84:     for line in lines:
85:         m = _RATING_LINE_RE.match(line)
86:         if m and not m.group("item") and m.group("value").lower() in _RATING_SET:
87:             own.append(m.group("value").capitalize())
88:         labels += [v.capitalize() for v in _RATING_LABEL_RE.findall(line) if v.lower() in _RATING_SET]
89:     # Without a label there is no call to read: a rating word in the prose may be
90:     # one the text argues against ("not a Sell"), and reading it reports a
91:     # direction nobody decided.
92:     found = own or labels
93:     return found[0] if found and len(set(found)) == 1 else None
94: 
95: 
96: def parse_rating(text: str, default: str = RATING_REVIEW) -> str:
97:     """Extract a 5-tier rating, or ``REVIEW`` when the decision has none.
98: 
99:     For callers that need a string for every decision, such as the memory log's
100:     entry tag. The default is the review sentinel, never a tradeable rating.
101:     """
102:     rating = extract_rating(text)
103:     return rating if rating is not None else default
104: 
105: 
106: def run_rating(final_state: dict) -> str:
107:     """A finished run's rating: the Portfolio Manager's own, else read from its decision.
108: 
109:     The fallback serves a state without ``final_rating``, such as a run an older
110:     version completed and a checkpoint hands back unchanged.
111:     """
112:     return final_state.get("final_rating") or parse_rating(final_state.get("final_trade_decision", ""))
113: 
114: 
115: def is_review(signal: str) -> bool:
116:     """Whether a signal is the non-tradeable REVIEW sentinel (#1170)."""
117:     return signal == RATING_REVIEW

It is not\n# a tradeable position: it flags output that needs a human/re-run rather than\n# silently degrading to Hold. Callers that map the signal onto the 5-tier enum\n# (e.g. ``PortfolioRating(signal)``) should guard with ``is_review`` first.\nRATING_REVIEW = \"REVIEW\"\n\n_RATING_SET = {r.lower() for r in RATINGS_5_TIER}\n\n# Matches \"Rating: X\" / \"rating - X\" / \"Rating — **X**\" — tolerates markdown\n# bold wrappers and any dash or colon a model writes as the separator. \"rating\"\n# must start a word, so \"Operating margin: Sell-side\" is not a label.\n_RATING_LABEL_RE = re.compile(r\"(?<![a-z])rating\\b[^:\\-\\u2010-\\u2015]*[:\\-\\u2010-\\u2015][\\s*]*(\\w+)\",\n                              re.IGNORECASE)\n\n# The decision's own rating line, in the shape the Portfolio Manager is asked to\n# open with (\"- **Rating**: X\", \"**Final Rating**: X\", \"## Our rating - X\"): an\n# optional list marker, emphasis and heading marks, and only words naming the\n# decision itself before \"rating\". \"Consensus rating: Buy\" or \"Trader's rating:\n# Buy\" is someone else's rating.\n_OWN_QUALIFIER = r\"(?:(?:final|our|overall|my|recommended|updated|revised|new|current)\\s+)*\"\n_RATING_LINE_RE = re.compile(\n    r\"\\s*(?P<item>(?:[-+*\\u2022]|\\d+[.)])\\s+)?[\\s*_#]*\" + _OWN_QUALIFIER\n    + r\"rating[^\\w:\\-\\u2010-\\u2015]*[:\\-\\u2010-\\u2015][\\s*]*(?P<value>\\w+)\",\n    re.IGNORECASE,\n)\n\n# A line presenting the scale rather than a decision (\"Rating Scale: Buy, ...\").\n_RATING_SCALE_RE = re.compile(r\"rating\\s*(scale|options|legend)\", re.IGNORECASE)\n\ndef extract_rating(text: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Extract a 5-tier rating from its label, or ``None`` if there is none.\n\n    Reads an explicit \"Rating: X\" label (tolerant of markdown bold) in the\n    NFKC-normalized text, so fullwidth punctuation like ``Rating：Overweight``\n    matches as ASCII does: the decision's opening rating line, else its own\n    rating lines or, failing those, every label, when they agree.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not text:\n        return None\n    norm = unicodedata.normalize(\"NFKC\", text)\n\n    # The decision is asked to open with its rating, so a first line (after any\n    # headings) in that shape is the call. A list item there may also be a quote\n    # heading a list of other parties' ratings, so it counts with the decision's\n    # other rating lines, which leave out list items; failing those, every label\n    # counts. Either way they must agree: ratings that differ, with nothing\n    # marking which one is the call, are no call (#1170). Lines presenting the\n    # scale itself are a legend the model echoed, not a call.\n    lines = [line for line in norm.splitlines() if line.strip() and not _RATING_SCALE_RE.search(line)]\n    first = next((line for line in lines if not line.lstrip().startswith(\"#\")\n                  or _RATING_LINE_RE.match(line)), \"\")\n    m = _RATING_LINE_RE.match(first)\n    opening = m if m and m.group(\"value\").lower() in _RATING_SET else None\n    if opening and not opening.group(\"item\"):\n        return opening.group(\"value\").capitalize()\n\n    own = [opening.group(\"value\").capitalize()] if opening else []\n    labels = []\n    for line in lines:\n        m = _RATING_LINE_RE.match(line)\n        if m and not m.group(\"item\") and m.group(\"value\").lower() in _RATING_SET:\n            own.append(m.group(\"value\").capitalize())\n        labels += [v.capitalize() for v in _RATING_LABEL_RE.findall(line) if v.lower() in _RATING_SET]\n    # Without a label there is no call to read: a rating word in the prose may be\n    # one the text argues against (\"not a Sell\"), and reading it reports a\n    # direction nobody decided.\n    found = own or labels\n    return found[0] if found and len(set(found)) == 1 else None\n\n\ndef parse_rating(text: str, default: str = RATING_REVIEW) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Extract a 5-tier rating, or ``REVIEW`` when the decision has none.\n\n    For callers that need a string for every decision, such as the memory log's\n    entry tag. The default is the review sentinel, never a tradeable rating.\n    \"\"\"\n    rating = extract_rating(text)\n    return rating if rating is not None else default\n\n\ndef run_rating(final_state: dict) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A finished run's rating: the Portfolio Manager's own, else read from its decision.\n\n    The fallback serves a state without ``final_rating``, such as a run an older\n    version completed and a checkpoint hands back unchanged.\n    \"\"\"\n    return final_state.get(\"final_rating\") or parse_rating(final_state.get(\"final_trade_decision\", \"\"))\n\n\ndef is_review(signal: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Whether a signal is the non-tradeable REVIEW sentinel (#1170).\"\"\"\n    return signal == RATING_REVIEW",
